topic_desc: Brahmin are a cornerstone of wasteland survival, providing meat, milk, and labor across post-War America. Edible cuts include the udder, chuck, brisket, rib, loin, and sirloin. They possess eight-compartment stomachs, udders, and four testicles, and can carry loads up to roughly 500 pounds. Their waste is valued as fertilizer. In the New California Republic, brahmin herding has grown into a powerful industry, with Brahmin Barons wielding considerable political influence over laws and policy. In the Capital Wasteland, brahmin are seen in settlements such as Megaton, Arefu, and the Republic of Dave, and are used by traders to transport wares. The Brotherhood of Steel has used pack brahmin to distribute clean water to wasteland inhabitants following the activation of Project Purity. Though generally docile and seldom hostile, wild aggressive brahmin can produce a loud roar. A rare mutation occasionally produces a single-headed specimen, known as a mono-headed brahmin.
topic_desc_basic: Brahmin are two-headed cattle that serve as a major food source and form of transportation throughout the wasteland, raised for their meat and milk while their waste is used as fertilizer. When utilized by merchants to carry goods, these creatures are known as pack brahmin, and they are a common, non-dangerous sight in settlements like Megaton, Arefu, and the Republic of Dave. In the New California Republic, herding brahmin is a significant industry where wealthy Brahmin Barons influence politicians and laws. Occasionally, a brahmin is born with a single head, a rare mutation referred to as a mono-headed brahmin.

topic_desc: Centaurs are grotesque mutant creatures composed primarily of human and canine components, named for their three pairs of leg-like arms. In earlier wasteland accounts, centaurs possessed two heads—one canine, one humanoid—each connected to the body by thick, elongated necks converging at the torso's base. In the Capital Wasteland, centaurs display a single head with three writhing tentacle-like tongues and bones protruding from their bodies. Instead of legs, they use multiple human arms to drag themselves along the ground. They are slow-moving but possess both ranged and close-range attacks, capable of spitting radioactive projectiles. Centaurs are most commonly found accompanying super mutants, serving as watchdogs and companions. Significant concentrations exist in the basement of the Chryslus Building and near the Seward Square skybridge, with additional specimens found in Vault 87. Moira Brown's terminal entries suggest centaurs may be capable of speech due to the abundance of their tongues. In the Den, Mom's Diner has been known to serve centaur chops.
topic_desc_basic: Centaurs are large, fleshy mutated creatures composed of human and canine components, named for their three pairs of leg-like arms. topic_desc: Deathclaws were originally engineered by the pre-war United States government from Jackson's Chameleon stock to replace human soldiers in close-combat search-and-destroy missions. At least one deathclaw was deployed during the Alaskan Reclamation Operation, where it killed several Chinese soldiers. Following the Great War, deathclaws spread across North America, establishing packs governed by a pack leader and pack mother. Their nests frequently disrupt trade routes, and the only reliable way to dislodge a nest is to kill the pack mother. Behemoths are regarded as the only creatures posing a greater threat. Some wastelanders who have never encountered deathclaws consider them mythical, vampiric, or ghostly. The Enclave conducted extensive experiments on deathclaws, including the creation of Intelligent Deathclaws at Vault 13 through FEV injection. These creatures gained sufficient intelligence to recognize their intended role as expendable Enclave soldiers and feigned compliance until they could seek freedom. The Enclave also used domestication units to pacify deathclaws at Raven Rock. In the Capital Wasteland, deathclaws nest at the Deathclaw Sanctuary and Old Olney, the latter driving out a group of ghouls led by Sanders. In the Mojave Wasteland, deathclaws congregate at the Gypsum Train Yard and Deathclaw Promontory. After the NCRCF prison break, Powder Gangers stole dynamite from Quarry Junction, halting work and allowing a pack to occupy the area, blocking travel along the Long 15. A Legendary Deathclaw inhabits Dead Wind Cavern.
topic_desc_basic: Deathclaws are large, highly dangerous mutated predators originally engineered by the pre-war United States government from Jackson's Chameleon stock as replacements for human soldiers in close-combat missions. The Enclave experimented on Deathclaws in several locations, including the creation of Intelligent Deathclaws at Vault 13 through FEV injection, resulting in creatures with increased intelligence who eventually recognized their intended role as expendable soldiers.

topic_desc: Eyebots are aerial, spherical robots equipped with a loudspeaker and a forward-mounted electrical weapon, with several long antennas protruding from their shells. They are common in the Mojave Wasteland and the Divide, where they broadcast signals, relay messages, and respond to perceived threats. Although a single eyebot is not heavily armed, its power system may explode when the robot is destroyed, endangering anything nearby. The best-known example in the Mojave is ED-E, whose casing and internal records connect it to pre-War Enclave research and long-distance travel. Pre-War popular media also featured an eyebot character named RALPHIE, and surviving posters in the Divide show that the robot's distinctive shape was familiar to the American public. Broken units found throughout the Divide provide evidence of the region's former robotic infrastructure and the violence that destroyed it.
topic_desc_basic: Eyebots are small, spherical aerial robots equipped with a loudspeaker and an electrical weapon mounted on the front, along with several long antennas extending from their top and back. Though individually not very dangerous, eyebots are known to detonate when destroyed, posing a minor hazard to anything nearby. A notable eyebot designated ED-E has gained some recognition among wastelanders, and pre-War popular media even featured an eyebot character named RALPHIE, suggesting these robots were well known to the American public before the Great War.

topic_desc: The exact cause of a ghoul turning feral remains unknown, though the condition is characterized by brain degeneration and is considered an illness by some. Feral ghouls possess no body heat and emit lethal radiation, preferring dark environments such as underground areas or nighttime surfaces. They screech when enemies approach and attack primarily with their hands, though some—such as those at Camp Searchlight—retain enough function to use weapons. Curiously, feral ghouls display mixed behaviors toward non-feral ghouls: some are non-combative, while others are openly hostile. A ghoul mask can fool them into neutrality. The widespread assumption that all ghouls inevitably become feral drives significant prejudice against non-feral ghouls across the wasteland.
topic_desc_basic: Feral Ghouls are irradiated humans who have lost their minds to brain degeneration, becoming aggressive and dangerous. They are known by many names, including Mindless Ghouls, Zombies, Crazies, and Post-Necrotic Humans. They emit lethal radiation, prefer dark places, and attack with their hands, though some can still use weapons. Their existence fuels prejudice against all ghouls, as many humans assume every ghoul will eventually turn feral.

topic_desc: The Mister Gutsy was developed by General Atomics International as a dedicated combat variant of the civilian Mister Handy, commissioned by the United States Army before the Great War. Units saw action during the Battle of Anchorage in January 2077. General Atomics programmed them as effective soldiers, but vague programming definitions caused issues with their simulated personality units, granting them the ability to refuse orders from commanders they deemed incompetent or who were under court martial. Units carried "ABC" and "MGZ" serial numbers, with variants ranked Mister, Sergeant, Lieutenant, Major, and Colonel. A field medic model was also produced, incapable of combat but possessing encyclopedic medical knowledge, particularly in surgery. In the Mojave Wasteland, Mister Gutsies can be found at Nellis Air Force Base, HELIOS One, and other pre-war installations.

topic_desc: The Mister Handy is a service and maintenance robot utilizing a powerful propulsion system to hover above ground level. Its spherical chassis is fitted with three optical sensors and three primary appendages for manual labor, including a buzz saw and a rudimentary flamethrower. In the Mojave Wasteland, Mister Handy units can be found at several locations including the Securitron Vault, REPCONN Headquarters, Sunset Sarsaparilla Headquarters, H&H Tools Factory, New Vegas Steel, and the Saturnite Alloy Research Facility. The Mister Handy platform also served as the basis for the military Mister Gutsy variant. These robots represent some of the most ubiquitous pre-war robotics still functioning in the post-nuclear world, performing maintenance and service tasks long after their original owners perished.

topic_desc: Mole rats are mutated descendants of a species closely resembling a larger variant of heterocephalus glaber, having survived the Great War by burrowing underground where soil shielded them from direct nuclear blasts. Subsequent radioactive fallout greatly increased their size and aggression. The Enclave conducted field research on mole rats, documenting observations at a small outpost west of the Temple of the Union. Moira Brown noted that mole rats can be domesticated, but only after de-clawing, de-teething, and a lobotomy. Some wastelanders have trained and kept them as pets, and raiders have hosted mole rat races at a dedicated track. Mole rats charge their prey and lunge several feet to bite with large incisors, though they may retreat if severely outmatched. They are found throughout the Capital Wasteland and as far afield as Point Lookout.

topic_desc: The RobCo Protectron was among the most versatile pre-War commercial robots, deployed across the United States in roles ranging from security to firefighting. Its three photo sensors provided visual input while a fission battery housed behind an access panel supplied power. Each unit was stored in a dedicated pod interfaced through the Standard Protectron Control Interface v2.40. The Protectron's introduction had significant social consequences: automation displaced human workers, and resulting labor strikes turned violent. RobCo produced numerous specialised variants. Construction models carried internal nail guns and were built to withstand damage. Firefighter models were fitted with internal cryo guns. Medic models used their hands as defibrillators and could deliver shock attacks in combat. Police units likewise employed shock-based tactics. Protectrons could even cook food using internal temperatures reaching one thousand degrees. Software personalities included the R04 V9 Office Helper, the RS3 V4.1.6 Utility Helper with pest extermination programs, and the RX2 V1.16.4 Vault Helper with Vault protocols. A prototype called the Protect-O-Bot was displayed at the REPCONN Headquarters museum. In the Mojave Wasteland, Protectrons have been found guarding HELIOS One, Mr. House's secret bunker beneath the Fort, and the H&H Tools Factory. Named units include Fisto, Primm Slim, and Vendortron.
topic_desc_basic: The RobCo Protectron is a sturdy pre-War security automaton used in both private and business sectors across the United States. topic_desc: Radroaches are descended from the pre-War Great American Cockroach, known scientifically as periplaneta americana. Enclave field research terminals have documented the species' pre-War origins. Following the Great War, these insects proliferated throughout the Capital Wasteland, congregating in significant numbers at locations such as the RobCo Facility, the Nuka-Cola Plant offices, and the Gillian House in Minefield. Radroaches are generally hostile to humans, flapping their wings and antennae as a pre-attack display. Their meat is edible, though widely regarded as unpalatable; Moira Brown of Megaton famously compared the taste to old feet. Despite their ubiquity, radroaches exhibit no body part that can be crippled to induce frenzy, unlike many other wasteland creatures. Unusual specimens have been documented: two caged radroaches named Fluffy and Jitters were found in an abandoned shack, and a recluse known as Gallo kept undersized radroaches as pets in the County Sewer Mainline. Radroaches near the so-called Roach King have been observed as non-hostile. Undersized specimens have also been reported in Vault 108's living quarters cafeteria.

topic_desc: Radscorpions are large, mutated arthropods descended from the North American Emperor scorpion. Following the Great War, exposure to radiation and the Forced Evolutionary Virus caused dramatic growth in the species, producing specimens far larger than their pre-War ancestors. These creatures are encountered throughout the wasteland and are widely feared for their aggressive temperament and potent venom. The venom has proven medically significant: antidotes have been successfully derived from it, providing wastelanders and medical practitioners with a means to treat radscorpion stings. The combination of radiation and FEV exposure responsible for the radscorpion's enlarged size is consistent with mutations observed in other post-War species. Radscorpions represent one of the more dangerous common threats faced by travelers in both the Capital Wasteland and the Mojave Wasteland, where their armoured exoskeletons and venomous tails make them formidable opponents even for experienced wastelanders.

topic_desc: Robobrains represent General Atomics International's first successful union of organic matter and robotics, developed under Doctor Bert Riggs before the Great War. Research and production spanned facilities operated by General Atomics, RobCo Industries, and the US Army Robotics Division, including Sierra Army Depot, RB-2851, and the RobCo Sales & Service Center. Early models used chimpanzee brains, with each successive model providing superior upgrades: increased energy efficiency, improved brain longevity, enhanced visual cortex connections for better motor skills and perception, and tactical combat capabilities. General Atomics ultimately sought human brains to augment the robot's functions, accelerate decision-making, and ensure unquestioning obedience. Candidates for brain extraction were drawn from military and civilian prisons, focusing on adults of high intelligence and sufficient constitution to survive the removal process. Candidates with low intelligence, mental disorders, or poor brain health were terminated. Robobrains with an IQ below 80 were classified as defective and disposed of at the Robotics Disposal Ground. Successful candidates had their brains removed, analysed, reconditioned, and placed in Biomed Gel before attachment to the robotic chassis. The removal process prevented personality retention. Additional research into brain extraction and isolation was conducted at the St. Aubin Medical Facility in Point Lookout, though the robobrain never reached full production there. In the Mojave Wasteland, robobrains have been observed serving the NCR near Hoover Dam at Ranger Station Delta, while hostile units have been encountered at HELIOS One, Vault 11, the H&H Tools Factory, and Big MT.

topic_desc: The sentry bot was engineered as a pre-war autonomous security platform designed to project overwhelming force in defense of installations and personnel. Its armament configuration pairs a minigun or Gatling laser on the right arm with a missile launcher on the left, allowing it to engage multiple threat types simultaneously. A critical design feature is the cooldown phase following sustained fire, during which the robot's fusion core is exposed and vulnerable to attack. The combat inhibitor mounted on the unit's back regulates targeting and behavior; if destroyed, the robot enters a frenzied state, attacking indiscriminately. Uniquely, sentry bots are equipped with judicial circuits that grant them limited law-enforcement authority. When they witness murder or theft, these circuits activate and the robot issues an immediate death sentence, pursuing the identified criminal with lethal intent. In the Mojave Wasteland, sentry bots appear in locations such as Vault 11 and the Securitron Vault. The Big MT research facility houses Mk series variants, while dedicated Army models patrol the Divide. Named units include Koch, an antique sentry bot, and RY-589 Ultimo Bot. Upon destruction, sentry bots detonate violently.
topic_desc_basic: Sentry Bots are heavy combat robots created to provide security through overwhelming firepower, utilizing a minigun or Gatling Laser on one arm and a Missile Launcher on the other. A combat inhibitor on their back can cause them to frenzy if damaged, and their fusion core becomes vulnerable during a cooldown phase after attacking. These robots are found throughout the Mojave Wasteland, Big MT, and the Divide, with variants including the Mk series and dedicated Army models.

topic_desc: Super Mutants originate from Forced Evolutionary Virus research that began at West Tek, with FEV samples transferred to Mariposa Military Base on January 7, 2077, under the direction of Leon Von Felden and Robert Anderson. The virus produced approximately a 60% increase in size and a potential 200% intelligence increase in successful subjects, though outcomes varied dramatically by strain. In the Capital Wasteland, the Evolutionary Experimentation Program at Vault 87 produced a distinct strain beginning in 2078. These mutants grow larger and stronger with age, but suffered reduced intelligence and sterility. Their inability to reproduce drove an obsessive campaign to capture humans for conversion using FEV, or "green stuff," at Vault 87. By 2277, dwindling FEV reserves left them increasingly desperate. In the Mojave, Marcus led a group of first-generation mutants to found Black Mountain, using the site's radiation as a natural deterrent. A rift with the Nightkin officer Tabitha, whose mental state deteriorated after her robot companion Rhonda broke down, eventually forced Marcus to leave and establish Jacobstown. Jacobstown became a refuge for first-generation Super Mutants and Nightkin, with Doctor Henry researching cures for Nightkin mental illnesses caused by prolonged Stealth Boy use. Meanwhile, Black Mountain became the hostile State of Utobitha under Tabitha's command, where Nightkin and second-generation mutants harassed travelers along I-15.
topic_desc_basic: Super Mutants, sometimes simply called Mutants, are hulking humanoid creatures created by exposing humans to the Forced Evolutionary Virus. Various strains of these mutants exist across the wasteland, originating from places like Mariposa Military Base, Vault 87, the Institute, and West Tek facilities. While many are hostile and obsessively seek out more of the virus, often referred to as "green stuff," to expand their numbers, some groups coexist peacefully with humans.

topic_desc: Abominations represent the alien inhabitants' most disturbing experimentation conducted aboard Mothership Zeta. Through processes documented in recorded logs, the aliens systematically transform captured humans into hybrid creatures, though the conversion proves fatal for many subjects. The survivors emerge as gaunt, hostile beings with semi-transparent skin that reveals underlying physiology, and disproportionately long arms suited for close-quarters violence. Unlike the alien crew, abominations employ no ranged weaponry. Their behavioral pattern is distinctive: upon detecting an intruder, an abomination will point at the target and emit a loud wail before charging at speed, swiping with its elongated limbs. This warning behavior provides a brief window before the attack commences. Abominations are encountered both confined within cells and roaming the corridors of Mothership Zeta, suggesting they may be released or escape containment. The Biological Research section of the vessel serves as their primary habitat, consistent with their status as experimental subjects. Notably, abominations demonstrate considerable physical resilience, resisting knockdown effects from weapons that reliably topple other targets. When destroyed, their bodies yield assorted items including alien power modules, alien epoxy, pre-war money, cigarettes, harmonicas, and pre-war books, suggesting their human origins retained personal effects through the transformation.

topic_desc: The extraterrestrial beings encountered aboard Mothership Zeta represent a technologically advanced civilization capable of interstellar travel, long-term cryostasis, teleportation, and holographic projection. The most commonly observed specimens wear distinctive white spacesuits and behave with uniform hostility toward all intruders aboard their vessel. Their armament includes disintegrators and atomizers for ranged engagement, as well as shock batons for close-quarters combat. Some aliens project an Inertia Suppression Field, a personal energy barrier that enhances their survivability in combat, with the field's effectiveness scaling according to the individual alien's tier. In battle, aliens equipped with melee weapons tend to rush opponents, while others maintain distance and employ their ranged arsenal. The aliens also deploy Guardian Drones as support units. Beyond the crew, the ship contains alien workers who lack combat capability and cower when confronted, though their presence can disrupt shipboard systems and scripted events. Evidence of extraterrestrial visitation to Earth exists independently of Mothership Zeta: a dead alien bearing an Alien Blaster was discovered far north of the Scrapyard in the Capital Wasteland, suggesting at least one prior incursion or crash on the planet's surface. The aliens' interest in humanity is further evidenced by their cryostasis chambers, which hold preserved human captives from various historical periods, and their biological research programs that transform human subjects into abominations.

topic_desc: The bloatfly represents one of the more peculiar results of post-War insect mutation in the Capital Wasteland. Enclave researchers operating at an outpost near Megaton included the bloatfly among the regional creatures they studied, tentatively placing it within the Tabanidae family of biting flies. The species adapted to its enlarged scale through a unique gland that permits balance and sustained speed despite its increased mass, though this same gland is believed to be toxic if ingested. Bloatflies attack by ejecting their own maggots as live projectiles, a deeply unusual reproductive-aggressive behavior, and their carapaces offer minimal protection against weapons. Their wings produce a faint clicking sound reminiscent of giant ant movement, while their death is marked by a high-pitched chattering noise. They congregate wherever carrion is plentiful, including the entrance chamber of Vault 92 and the hillsides near Reclining Groves Resort Homes, where dead Wastelanders provide a ready food source.
topic_desc_basic: Bloatflies are mutated insects found in the Capital Wasteland, descended from either the common housefly or biting horse fly. The Enclave tentatively classified them within the Tabanidae family, noting that they evolved a unique gland to balance and maintain speed at their enlarged size, though this gland may be toxic if consumed. They attack by launching their own maggots as projectiles and can explode upon death. Bloatflies are known to congregate in areas with available carrion, such as near Reclining Groves Resort Homes where they feed on dead Wastelanders, and within the entrance area of Vault 92.

topic_desc: Aboard the alien spacecraft Mothership Zeta, drones serve as multipurpose robotic units deployed by the alien crew for combat, personal assistance, and weapons testing. The Experimental Weapons Drones represent a specialized variant encountered within the vessel's Weapons Lab, where alien experimenters use them to fire upon brahmin that emerge from a Teleportation Matrix, apparently studying weapon effects on living subjects. All drones on the ship, including these experimental models, are produced at the Robot Assembly facility. Each Experimental Weapons Drone is armed with a Drone Cannon or its enhanced variant, the Drone Cannon Ex-B, firing arced explosive projectiles. Drones found deactivated inside Alien Robot Pods throughout the vessel can be reactivated using a Drone Control Device, which temporarily recruits them as followers. Their hover-platform locomotion can be disrupted by targeting the platform itself, though curiously, standard EMP weapons such as pulse grenades and pulse mines have no effect on these alien constructs.

topic_desc: The fire ants of the Capital Wasteland are an unintended product of scientific experimentation conducted by Doctor Lesko, who sought to reverse the gigantism afflicting wasteland ant populations through genetic manipulation. A small error in his genetic work produced an entirely different mutation rather than the intended size reduction, yielding a species capable of producing and projecting fire. Lesko termed the mechanism pyrosis: the ants expel flammable venom from modified venom sacs and ignite it by clicking their mandibles together to create a spark. In behavior, fire ants retain the swarming tactics of ordinary giant ants, overwhelming targets through numbers. They exhibit a high resistance to fire, consistent with their own incendiary biology. Damaging their antennae can trigger a frenzied state, causing disorientation and erratic aggression. The creatures are not uniformly hostile and may ignore passersby unless provoked. Their emergence in the Capital Wasteland is tied directly to Lesko's experiments and the disruption they caused to local ant colonies.
topic_desc_basic: Fire ants are mutated insects found in the Capital Wasteland, created accidentally by Doctor Lesko through genetic manipulation. The doctor was attempting to return giant ants to their normal size, but a small error in his work produced a different mutation altogether. These creatures breathe fire through a process Lesko calls pyrosis, expelling flammable venom from their venom sacks and igniting it with a spark made by clicking their mandibles. Fire ants employ swarming tactics similar to ordinary giant ants and possess a notable resistance to fire.

topic_desc: Guardian Drones are the principal robotic defense and utility units deployed throughout the alien vessel Mothership Zeta. Manufactured in the ship's Robot Assembly, they serve the alien crew in combat, personal assistance, and weapons-testing roles. Each drone travels on a hovering platform and carries a Drone Cannon that fires an arcing explosive projectile capable of rolling across surfaces before detonating. In the Weapons Lab, drones fire on brahmin emerging from a Teleportation Matrix, suggesting that the aliens study weapon effects on terrestrial organisms. Dormant Guardian Drones are stored inside Alien Robot Pods around the vessel, and a Drone Control Device can reactivate compatible units. Their construction differs substantially from terrestrial robotics: even pulse grenades and pulse mines, normally effective against machines, have little discernible effect on these alien constructs.
topic_desc_basic: Guardian Drones are alien robots used by the aliens aboard Mothership Zeta for a variety of tasks, including combat, personal use, and weapons testing. They are manufactured at the ship's Robot Assembly and can be found stationed throughout the vessel, sometimes resting deactivated within Alien Robot Pods. Each Guardian Drone is equipped with a Drone Cannon, a weapon that fires an arced projectile which rolls along surfaces before exploding. In the Weapons Lab, drones are used to fire at brahmin that emerge from a Teleportation Matrix as part of alien experimentation.

topic_desc: Mirelurks are a dominant aquatic predator species of the Capital Wasteland, occupying a niche shaped by the region's pervasive water contamination. Their heavy natural armor renders most conventional attacks ineffective, with the unarmored face serving as the primary vulnerability. The species appears physiologically dependent on irradiated water: when Project Purity begins distributing purified water following the Battle of Project Purity in 2277, mirelurks in the vicinity of the Jefferson Memorial begin dying off. Brotherhood of Steel personnel stationed at the memorial observe this die-off firsthand, with one initiate burning dead specimens and a patrolling knight noting that soldiers are encouraged to shoot the dying creatures. This dependency suggests a mutated biology adapted to—or reliant upon—contaminated environments, raising questions about the species' long-term viability should the Capital Wasteland's water supply be broadly purified. Culturally, mirelurk meat holds significant value among wastelanders. Grandma Sparkle considers it "the best meat you can get out here," with the softshell variety being especially prized. A mirelurk cakes recipe exists at the Anchorage War Memorial, indicating some pre-war or early post-war culinary tradition surrounding the species. Mirelurks cannot attack while swimming, and white noise—such as that found in Vault 92—proves instantly lethal to them, suggesting sensory fragility beneath their armored exterior.
topic_desc_basic: Mirelurks are giant mutated creatures that inhabit the waters and shores of the Capital Wasteland. They are heavily armored, making them difficult to harm, though their faces are a known weak point. Wastelanders such as Grandma Sparkle prize mirelurk meat, especially the softshell variety, as a valuable food source. They appear to require contaminated water to survive, as they begin dying off when exposed to pure water.

topic_desc: Mirelurk Kings represent an apex variant within the mirelurk species hierarchy of the Capital Wasteland, distinguished by a potent ranged sonic attack capable of instantly crippling a target's head at considerable distance. This sonic capability appears to function through water as a medium, penetrating aquatic environments even though the kings themselves cannot attack while swimming and remain stationary when approached. The sonic attack is disabled if the king's own head is crippled, suggesting a centralized sensory or vocal organ responsible for generating the attack. Torso shots against mirelurk kings inflict only two-thirds of normal damage, indicating a secondary layer of natural armor beyond what standard mirelurks possess. Their melee attack, however, deals more damage than the ranged sonic attack, making close-range engagement particularly hazardous. The related Swamplurk Queen variant, encountered in the Point Lookout swamplands, substitutes the sonic attack with a spit projectile that deals greater damage and possesses higher overall resilience. Both variants share the head-crippling vulnerability, suggesting a common anatomical weakness across mirelurk evolutionary branches. The existence of distinct regional variants—kings in the Capital Wasteland and queens in Point Lookout—implies adaptive divergence shaped by local environmental conditions.
topic_desc_basic: Mirelurk Kings are mutated creatures found in the Capital Wasteland. They are known for a ranged sonic attack that can cripple a target's head from afar, though they also possess a more damaging melee attack. Mirelurk Kings cannot attack while swimming and will remain stationary when approached, though their sonic attack can penetrate water. A related variant, the Swamplurk Queen, possesses a spit attack instead of the sonic attack and is more resilient.

topic_desc: Swampfolk are a population of mutated humans endemic to the Point Lookout swamplands, exhibiting severe physical deformities and a deeply territorial social structure that isolates them from outsiders. They mark their territory with hanging dolls and ritualistic fetishes, suggesting a developed if insular cultural practice rooted in superstition or folk tradition. Swampfolk operate in coordinated groups of two to five, typically combining melee chargers with firearm-wielding support, and display tactical behavior such as seeking replacement weapons when their current ones are destroyed. Their combat effectiveness is notably enhanced beyond what their crude weaponry would suggest, inflicting additional damage attributable to object-level modifications in the regional data—a phenomenon that may reflect environmental adaptation or the cumulative effects of Point Lookout's unique mutational pressures. Despite their fearsome reputation, Swampfolk society is not entirely closed. Marguerite lives among them in the bog without severe deformities and is recognized as a local. Haley, likewise lacking Swampfolk features, engages in trade with them and notes their strong odor. Kenny, born to Swampfolk parents without deformities, became an outcast—indicating that physical conformity to the group's mutated phenotype functions as a basis for social inclusion. Swampfolk occasionally gather and dance at Beachview Campsite, a behavior observed nowhere else on Point Lookout, hinting at communal rituals or gatherings tied to that specific location.
topic_desc_basic: Swampfolk are mutated humans inhabiting the Point Lookout swamplands, recognizable by their severe deformities and territorial nature. They mark their territory with hanging dolls and other fetishes, and are known to attack outsiders who wander too close to their grounds. While most Swampfolk are born with their distinctive mutations, rare individuals such as Kenny have been born to Swampfolk parents without deformities and become outcasts as a result. Locals like Marguerite and Haley coexist with or trade alongside the Swampfolk, with Haley noting that they tend to carry a strong smell.

topic_desc: Trogs represent one of the most disturbing consequences of concentrated environmental catastrophe in the post-war world. Troglodyte Degeneration Contagion (TDC) is not infectious in the traditional sense—it cannot be contracted through contact with the infected. Instead, it arises from the synergistic effect of intensively concentrated ambient radiation combined with the unique industrial toxins and pollutants saturating the Pitt, suggesting a region-specific biochemical mechanism unlike standard radiation mutation. The transformation rate among the general populace is approximately twenty percent, but children born in the Pitt face a one hundred percent degeneration rate, becoming feral within weeks of birth. This generational certainty implies that the Pitt's contamination has reached a threshold where prenatal exposure guarantees onset. Transformed individuals lose all recognition of former relationships, attacking friends and loved ones indiscriminately. Yet fragments of cognition persist: injured trogs cry out words like "Why?" and "Pain!," and some murmur "...peace..." or "Thank you..." as they die, hinting that remnants of human awareness remain trapped beneath the feral exterior. The trog phenomenon is geographically isolated to the Pitt, and residents of the Capital Wasteland are unfamiliar with the condition.
topic_desc_basic: Trogs are mutated humans found in the Pitt, transformed by Troglodyte Degeneration Contagion, a condition caused by the region's concentrated ambient radiation combined with unique industrial toxins and pollutants. The disease is not spread through contact with the infected. Roughly twenty percent of the local populace has undergone the transformation, becoming feral creatures that attack anything on sight, even former friends and loved ones. Children born in the Pitt face a one hundred percent degeneration rate and become feral within weeks of birth.
tags: environmental mutation mechanism,feral transformation rate,pitt industrial toxins,pitt isolated contagion,prenatal degeneration certainty,regional radiation mutation,residual human cognition,troglodyte degeneration contagion

topic_desc: Yao Guai are mutated descendants of pre-War bears that roam the Capital Wasteland in craggy, hilly terrain and cavern systems. Concentrated populations inhabit the Yao Guai Tunnels, Yao Guai Cave, and Cliffside Cavern. A notably distinctive specimen named Ruzka dwells in Ruzka's Alcove. Yao Guai possess keen Perception and can detect nearby presence without a direct line of sight, making them difficult to evade. In combat they close distance with running pounces followed by slashes and bites; crippling a hind leg temporarily disrupts their pounce but does not halt their charge. Though less lethal than Deathclaws, they are dangerous predators capable of killing Talon Company mercenaries and Brotherhood Outcast patrols in chance encounters. Some wasteland scavengers have been known to travel alongside tame Yao Guai. Their meat is more irradiated than other wasteland meats but is prized for the temporary vigor it imparts to those who consume it. Three Dog, the radio broadcaster of Galaxy News Radio, famously advises listeners not to feed the Yao Guai.
topic_desc_basic: Yao Guai are mutated bear-like creatures found throughout the Capital Wasteland, typically in craggy, hilly areas or caverns. They are generally encountered in pairs or wandering alone, frequently at night, and are known to inhabit locations such as the Yao Guai Tunnels, Yao Guai Cave, and Cliffside Cavern. Though not as deadly as Deathclaws, Yao Guai are formidable opponents that attack with running pounces followed by slashes and bites. Some wasteland scavengers travel with Yao Guai companions, and these tame specimens will not attack on sight, though they will defend themselves and their ally if threatened.

topic_desc: Bighorners are large herbivorous beasts native to the American Southwest, valued by wasteland communities for their horns, meat, milk, and hides. Domesticated drifts are maintained at settlements including Goodsprings, Jacobstown, Spring Mt. Ranch State Park, and around Cottonwood Cove, where they serve as a vital resource for survival. Wild herds of three to seven roam mountainous regions, typically near banana yucca fruit, making them useful for tracking edible flora. A large contingent of wild bighorners congregates northwest of Snyder Prospector Camp, and malnourished specimens with calves can be found at Matthews Animal Husbandry Farm. Bighorners are communal animals; distressing a single member provokes the entire herd. Despite their size and strength, they cannot serve as pack animals, as Easy Pete of Goodsprings explains that they simply lie down until any load is removed. In combat, unprovoked bighorners rarely pursue aggressors, preferring to graze peacefully, but will charge and ram anything that approaches them or their young too closely. All bighorners grow horns regardless of sex.
topic_desc_basic: Bighorners are large herbivorous creatures native to the American Southwest, commonly found in the Mojave Wasteland and Zion Canyon. Humans have domesticated them for their horns, meat, milk, and hides, with settlements such as Goodsprings and Jacobstown keeping herds for survival. Wild bighorners travel in herds of three to seven, often near banana yucca fruit, while domesticated drifts are kept in settlements. They are generally docile but become aggressive if a herd member is distressed or if approached too closely.

topic_desc: Cazadores are large mutated flying insects originating from DNA splicing experiments conducted in 2003 at the Z-14 Pepsinae DNA Splicing Lab within Big MT. Their creator, Doctor Borous, denies both that they escaped the crater and that they are capable of breeding, but evidence contradicts both claims. Swarms have spread into the Mojave Wasteland and Zion Canyon in recent years, establishing large basket-shaped nests at locations such as Bonnie Springs, the road toward Jacobstown, north of Goodsprings, the Tribal Village, and the Callville Bay boathouse. Cazadores hunt in swarms of four or more, using quick and erratic flight patterns that make them exceedingly difficult to evade. Their venom is remarkably potent, causing more poison damage over a longer duration than a giant radscorpion's sting. They possess among the highest Perception of any wasteland creature, exceeding even the common Deathclaw, and compete with nightstalkers for prey. Crippling a wing grounds them temporarily, and damaging their antennae can send them into a frenzy. Specimens remaining within Big MT are notably tougher than their Mojave counterparts. The name derives from the Spanish word for hunter.
topic_desc_basic: Cazadores are large mutated insects created in 2003 at Big MT through DNA splicing experiments conducted in the Z-14 Pepsinae DNA Splicing Lab. Doctor Borous, their creator, denies that they escaped the Big MT crater or are capable of breeding, though both claims are false. In recent years, swarms of cazadores have spread from Big MT into neighboring regions such as the Mojave Wasteland and Zion Canyon. They are most commonly found in mountainous areas, where they build large basket-shaped nests, and they compete with nightstalkers for prey.

topic_desc: Cyberdogs are cybernetically enhanced canines that blend biological and mechanical components, including braincases that house and protect their augmented brains. Despite their robotic elements, they are universally classified as animals rather than robots and do not share the electromagnetic pulse vulnerabilities of true machines. The X-8 Research Center at Big MT serves as a primary facility for cyberdog development, where specimens are educated and trained, though observations suggest the dogs may spend time engaged in activities such as playing poker rather than strictly following their curriculum. A Police Cyberdog designated Roxie was created at the X-8 facility by splicing a robot and a dog together; she remains within the facility and does not venture beyond its entrance. Notable cyberdogs include Rex, associated with the King in Freeside, and Gabe. Antony, a member of Caesar's Legion, has noted that cyberdogs are an uncommon sight in Denver. Three variants are known: standard, Police, and Military cyberdogs, with the latter two appearing primarily at Big MT. The single-word spelling is commonly used in conversation, though the creatures themselves carry the two-word designation.
topic_desc_basic: Cyberdogs, also spelled cyber dogs, are cybernetically enhanced canines found in Big MT and the Mojave Wasteland, with Antony noting they are an uncommon sight in Denver as well. Notable individual cyberdogs include Rex, who is associated with the King in Freeside, Gabe, and Roxie, a Police Cyberdog created at the X-8 Research Center in Big MT by splicing a robot and a dog together. Despite their mechanical components, cyberdogs are generally considered animals rather than robots. Variants include standard, Police, and Military cyberdogs, with Police and Military variants appearing in Big MT.

topic_desc: Geckos are among the most widespread mutated animals of the Mojave Wasteland, living from the scrublands around Goodsprings to irradiated slopes near the Mojave Outpost. They travel in small packs and attack with bites and lunges. Some varieties developed more dangerous adaptations: fire geckos expel flame, while other specimens spit poisonous liquid. Fire Root Cavern is widely regarded as an origin point for the fire-gecko population, suggesting a localized mutation source. Golden geckos are hardier than common green geckos, and a separate green population inhabits Zion Canyon. Some Zion geckos remain unusually calm around the Sorrows' camp. Gecko hides are valuable to survivalists, who tan them for protective clothing suited to heat, poison, and radiation. Their temperament varies, but travelers should not mistake a motionless or solitary gecko for a harmless one.
topic_desc_basic: Geckos are mutated animals found throughout the Mojave Wasteland, commonly encountered in small packs in areas such as around Goodsprings, along the I-15 toward Primm, and near the Mojave Outpost. Several varieties exist, including the common green gecko, the golden gecko, and the fire gecko, the latter of which is believed to originate from Fire Root Cavern and is capable of breathing fire. A separate population of green geckos is also found in Zion Canyon. Fire geckos are generally hostile to travelers, while other varieties are less aggressive.

topic_desc: The Ghost People of the Sierra Madre are a tragic product of pre-war corporate ambition and Big MT experimentation. Before the war, construction workers building the Sierra Madre Villa encountered an unidentified airborne toxin leaking from pipes that caused severe lung and tissue damage. Work was halted until protective gear arrived, but the hazmat suits, designed at Big MT, were themselves part of a follow-up experiment. The suits grew stiff with use, their locking mechanisms corroding on contact with the Cloud until they could only be opened with a Cosmic Knife, and even then they failed to provide adequate protection. Over time, the trapped workers underwent profound biological change. Dean Domino, a survivor familiar with the Sierra Madre, questions whether the term "alive" even applies to them, noting that they carry pockets of pressurized gas within their bodies and taste of plastic and copper. They congregate in hordes beneath the villa's streets, gathering anywhere the Sierra Madre's holograms are absent. Their primary hunting grounds include Salida and Puesta del Sol, particularly where the Cloud is thickest. They are notably resistant to conventional harm, only falling when their limbs are dismembered. Their corpses continue to breathe through their masks even after losing all other limbs, issuing periodic green mist.
topic_desc_basic: Ghost People are mutated inhabitants of the Sierra Madre, transformed by prolonged exposure to the Cloud, a corrosive toxin created at Big MT. They originated as construction workers who were issued bulky hazmat suits to protect against the airborne poison, but the suits' locking mechanisms corroded on contact with the Cloud, trapping the workers inside as the gas slowly changed them. They are the only beings able to move freely through the Cloud, and they gather in hordes beneath the Sierra Madre's streets, hunting in areas thick with the toxic haze such as Salida and Puesta del Sol. Dean Domino questions whether they can even be considered alive, and they are known to carry pressurized gas within their bodies.

topic_desc: Giant mantises trace their origins to the horticultural experiments conducted within Vault 22, where pre-war scientists engineered accelerated plant growth and, inadvertently, oversized insect life. The mantises have since spread beyond the vault, establishing populations along the routes to Jacobstown and around Spring Mt. Ranch State Park, where they are encountered in scattered groups. A separate population exists in Zion Canyon. Their primary mode of attack is a leaping strike, using their oversized forelegs to slice targets in mid-air. A notable vulnerability exists in their antennae; if these sensory organs are damaged, the mantis enters a frenzied state, attacking anything within reach indiscriminately. Mantis oothecae, when disturbed, release dozens of nymphs at once. Within Vault 22, the research scientist Keely observed an ecological relationship between the mantises and the vault's spore plants, noting that mantises feed some of their prey to the plants. However, both mantises and spore plants appear disinclined to prey upon ghouls, leaving ghoul inhabitants largely undisturbed. Wastelanders harvest mantis eggs and forelegs from carcasses, and the creatures are known to clean their mouths and flutter their wings when at rest.
topic_desc_basic: Giant mantises are mutated insects found in the Mojave Wasteland and Zion Canyon, originally created by horticultural experiments in Vault 22. Ranch State Park, as well as inside Vault 22 itself.

topic_desc: Lakelurks are among the most dangerous aquatic predators in the Mojave Wasteland, dominating the waters of Lake Mead and the cave systems beneath Camp Guardian. Their keen perception allows them to detect potential prey at considerable distance, making ambushes difficult to avoid. Their signature attack is a shrieking sonic pulse that travels through both air and water with equal effect, stunning victims and dulling their senses before the lakelurk closes to tear them apart with powerful claws. This sonic assault passes straight through water as it does through air, placing submerged prey at a severe disadvantage. Lakelurks are fiercely territorial, attacking nearly anything near their nests, and congregate in groups ranging from pairs to gatherings of five to eight. Significant populations inhabit Blue Paradise Vacation Rentals, Ruby Hill Mine, the Scavenger Platform, and Lakelurk Cove, where as many as fifteen specimens may gather. Before attacking, lakelurks emit a roar that briefly exposes them to retaliation. They possess two sets of teeth, one resembling human dentition and another front set akin to a piranha's. Cass of the Mojave once compared fish to lakelurks, describing them as slimy and scaly but without legs. Their bodies sink rather than float when killed in water, though their viscera sometimes rise to the surface.
topic_desc_basic: Lakelurks are mutated aquatic creatures native to the Mojave Wasteland, commonly found around Lake Mead and other watery areas. They are fiercely territorial and aggressive, attacking nearly anything that approaches them or their nests. They typically travel in small groups of two to three, though larger gatherings of five to eight are not uncommon. Lakelurks use sonic pulse shrieks to stun prey from a distance before closing in to tear victims apart with their claws.

topic_desc: Lobotomites are the product of medical experiments conducted at Big MT. An Auto-Doc, programmed by Doctor Mobius, removed their brains via laser incision and replaced them with Tesla coils; their hearts and spines were likewise extracted and substituted with cybernetic components, a measure taken to address complications arising from brain removal. Doctor Dala supervised the procedures, after which subjects were sutured with lasers and their organs placed in storage tanks. The routine was designed to keep all Big MT inhabitants confined: only a brain inside a functioning body can bypass the facility's radar fence, and without one, subjects wandering beyond the perimeter are rendered unconscious and compelled back inside. A pacification field within the Dome further prevents Lobotomites from attacking the Think Tank. The procedure left most mentally impaired and mute, some hearing only static or reduced to gibbering wrecks. The Think Tank automates their bodies for clean-up duties and experiments, including splicing at the X-8 Research Center. Lobotomites retain the capacity for simple tasks—opening doors, walking, and fighting with firearms or melee weapons—and show a proclivity for collecting random objects at their base, the Cuckoo's Nest. Though largely without comprehensible speech, fragments such as "die" or "stop" are occasionally audible. Their cybernetic modifications render them tougher and more damage-resistant than ordinary humans despite wearing almost no armor.
topic_desc_basic: Lobotomites are surgically-altered and cybernetically-enhanced humans found at Big MT. Their brains, hearts, and spines were removed and replaced with cybernetics by an Auto-Doc programmed by Doctor Mobius, under the supervision of Doctor Dala. The procedure left them mentally impaired, mute, and hostile to non-Lobotomites. The Think Tank uses them for clean-up duties and experiments.

topic_desc: Marked Men are the remnants of New California Republic soldiers and Legion frumentarii and scouts who were present in the Divide when catastrophic storms tore through the region. The violent winds flayed their flesh while residual radiation triggered mutation, leaving them alive yet fundamentally altered. Ulysses observed that the radiation "marked them, made them equal in history's eyes," erasing the distinctions of their former allegiances. They continue to wear damaged NCR and Legion armor patched together with road signs, license plates, and other scrap metal. Some among them fashioned crude versions of Legate Lanius's helmet, described by Ulysses as shaped from Divide metal "not with care and strength, but with hate," serving as distant mirrors of their Legate and a symbol they could cling to. Rumors of the Marked Men spread throughout the West Coast wasteland, alongside legends of the Sierra Madre and the Big Empty. They carry a variety of melee and ranged weapons and are known to use Stealth Boys. When near sources of radiation, they regenerate health. Notable individuals among them include Blister, a former NCR ranger wielding a flamer; Beast, who carries a shoulder-mounted machine gun; Bonesaw, a former legionary with a nearly intact Legate helmet and a chainsaw; Blade, who guards the entrance to Ulysses's Temple with a Blade of the West; Gaius Magnus, a centurion found in Dry Wells; and Colonel Royez of the NCR army, stationed on Long 15.
topic_desc_basic: Marked Men are mutated survivors of NCR and Legion forces trapped in the Divide, scarred by radiation and storms. They wear patched armor and carry weapons forged from Divide metal, including helmets inspired by Legate Lanius. Rumors of them spread across the West Coast wasteland.

topic_desc: Mongrels are aggressive canines encountered across the Mojave Wasteland and Zion Canyon. They chase and circle their targets while attacking, and will assault those with low standing among associated factions. Within Caesar's Legion, Houndmasters tend packs of Mongrels at the Fort; the current matriarch of the Fort's pack is a female named Lupa. Antony, a Legion Houndmaster, notes that some Mongrels fight in the area and typically do not welcome visitors. In Zion Canyon, White Legs Mongrels accompany members of the White Legs tribe and attack outsiders on sight. Mongrels display pack behavior and are used by both the Legion and the White Legs as guard and attack animals, reflecting the tribal and militarized cultures that employ them.
topic_desc_basic: Mongrels are aggressive canine creatures found in the Mojave Wasteland and surrounding regions. Caesar's Legion keeps Mongrels tended by their Houndmasters, with the current mother of the Fort's pack being a female named Lupa. According to Antony, some of these Mongrels fight in the area and generally do not welcome visitors. White Legs Mongrels are also found throughout Zion Canyon, accompanying members of the White Legs tribe.

topic_desc: Nightstalkers are pre-War genetic hybrids of coyote and rattlesnake DNA created by Dr. Borous at Big MT. Borous reportedly sought to preserve rattlesnake DNA, which he believed was nearing extinction, though his memory was unclear and he also suggested the project may have stemmed from a dare with Dr. Calis at X-13. The creatures caused significant fatalities in the X-8 Research Center shipping department, where all but one employee were killed. Dr. Adam Figgis subsequently ordered the nightstalkers released into the X-8 testing area for behavioral study. After the Great War, many escaped and spread across the Mojave and beyond, with some reaching as far as Baja. They occasionally clash with Cazadores—another Big MT creation—over territory. Nightstalkers display traits of both parent species: they growl, howl, and whimper like coyotes while hissing, rattling, and injecting venom like rattlesnakes. Their bodies are mostly dog-like, covered in fur and scales, with rattlesnake-like heads, fangs, forked tongues, and tails. Their right eyes are blue with round pupils; their left eyes are yellow with elliptical pupils. They lay eggs like snakes but nurse their young in cave nests like coyotes. Nocturnal pack hunters, they prey on the unaware or sleeping, though daytime encounters are possible. Their venom is less potent than that of their main competition but can be dangerous with multiple untreated bites. Nightstalker blood is used in Antivenom, Hydra, and Nightstalker Squeezin's, and their eggs can be used to prepare Mushroom Cloud. Specimens in the Charleston Cave developed natural cloaking abilities from chewing on Stealth Boys, while those in the X-13 testing facility were granted invisibility by an unknown scientist. Nightstalkers at Big MT are notably tougher than their Mojave counterparts.
topic_desc_basic: Nightstalkers are genetic hybrids of coyote and rattlesnake DNA created by Dr. Borous at Big MT before the Great War. They escaped into the Mojave Wasteland and beyond after the bombs fell, hunting in nocturnal packs and nesting in caves. Their bodies combine fur and scales, with dog-like forms, rattlesnake heads and tails, and mismatched eyes.

topic_desc: Ravens are among the most ubiquitous and least threatening avian species in the Mojave Wasteland, observed frequently near settlements and along major highways. Their behavior is notably carrion-associated: they congregate wherever dead or crucified bodies are present, making them a grim but reliable indicator of recent violence, particularly at Legion-raided sites such as Nipton. Despite possessing a capacity for hostility when harmed, ravens never actually attack, instead fleeing when approached or injured. They are commonly seen in pairs along roads and may gather in notable numbers around the Big Horn Saloon and Boulder City Ruins, at Goodsprings Cemetery, near the entrance to Primm, and within Red Rock Canyon. The first raven many newcomers to the Mojave encounter is one that takes flight upon exiting the local clinic in Goodsprings. Their tendency to remain near civilized areas and grow scarcer in the deep wasteland suggests some dependence on human activity, whether through scavenging opportunities or the shelter of built structures.
topic_desc_basic: Ravens are small birds found throughout the Mojave Wasteland, commonly gathering near dead or crucified bodies at sites like Nipton and other Legion-raided locations. They tend to be more prevalent around civilized areas and settlements, becoming scarcer the further one travels from towns. Ravens are harmless creatures that will fly away if approached too closely and will never attack even if harmed. They are often seen in pairs along highways and may gather in places such as Goodsprings Cemetery, the Boulder City Ruins, and near the entrance to Primm.

topic_desc: The PDQ-88b Securitron, designated the RobCo security model 2060-B, was created through a joint effort between RobCo Industries and the H&H Tools Factory, charged with protecting the New Vegas Strip. Each unit is powered by a fusion core and armed with a Glastinghouse X-25 Gatling Laser in its left arm and a 9mm submachine gun in its right. Concealed shoulder compartments house M-235 missile launchers and a G-28 grenade launching system, available only when the Mk II operating system is enabled. Mr. House estimated that the Mk II upgrade raises each unit's combat effectiveness by approximately 235%, primarily through the addition of the missile and grenade systems and an auto-repair capability. Securitron AI personalities such as Victor and Yes Man distribute their programming across every Securitron in the network, allowing transfer from one chassis to another. At Big MT, several Securitrons were acquired for reverse engineering; Doctor 0 developed a Mk VI operating system and created the miniature unit Muggy, though many Big MT units became berserk and hostile, their faces distorted into an angry expression. Berserk units retain use of their missile launchers and arm laser but lose access to the grenade launcher and machine gun, while damaged units exhibit the inverse limitation.
topic_desc_basic: The PDQ-88b Securitron, also known as the RobCo security model 2060-B, is a security robot created by RobCo Industries and the H&H Tools Factory and charged with protecting the New Vegas Strip. A standard unit is armed with a Gatling laser and a 9mm submachine gun, while the upgraded Mk II operating system enables shoulder-mounted missile launchers, a grenade launching system, and an auto-repair capability that raises combat effectiveness by roughly 235%. Securitrons display a face on a monitor screen and can dispense printed material such as obituaries. Several units were acquired by Big MT for reverse engineering, leading Doctor 0 to create the miniature variant Muggy and to develop a Mk VI operating system, though many Big MT units became berserk and hostile.

topic_desc: Spore carriers are the reanimated remains of humans colonized by Beauveria mordicana, a mutated fungus originally developed at the X-22 Botanical Garden in Big MT and subsequently used in pest control experiments at Vault 22. The fungus was engineered as part of Vault 22's agricultural mission, one of several initiatives intended to sustain the Vault's population through plant cultivation. After the fungus became airborne, spores spread gradually through the ventilation systems, infecting inhabitants who developed a pronounced cough before dying within ten to twenty days. The first confirmed fatality was Dr. Harrison Peters, whose corpse reanimated and alarmed the remaining scientific staff. Attempts to contain the outbreak by igniting gas in the Vault's lower levels triggered a defensive response from the carriers, who attacked the scientists. In 2096, a group of over one hundred survivors organized an expedition to Zion Canyon, but many were already infected and eventually became spore carriers themselves. A unique specimen, Patient Zero, still roams the X-22 Botanical Garden at Big MT. Spore carriers are fast, attack at close range, and can burst upon death, releasing damaging radiation and spore-laden debris.
topic_desc_basic: Spore carriers are reanimated human corpses colonized by the mutated fungus Beauveria mordicana, originally developed for pest control in Vault 22. The fungus became airborne and spread through the Vault, killing inhabitants within ten to twenty days before reanimating their bodies. Survivors of the Vault 22 outbreak fled to Zion Canyon in 2096, where many succumbed to the infection. Spore carriers can also be found in the X-22 Botanical Garden at Big MT, the original source of the fungus, including a unique specimen known as Patient Zero.

topic_desc: Tunnelers are subterranean predators that inhabit the collapsed tunnel networks beneath The Divide, a region devastated by nuclear detonations that ruptured the earth and allowed them to reach the surface. They reproduce rapidly, hunt in coordinated packs, and are formidable enough to overwhelm even Deathclaws. Ulysses, who has studied the region extensively, suspects they predate the nuclear catastrophe and that radiation may have shaped their current form. The NCR's Bravo Team conducted a sweep-and-clear operation of the Collapsed Overpass Tunnel Entrance before the main NCR force entered The Divide. Early intelligence described the tunnels as sparsely populated by subterranean semi-humanoids frightened by bright light and loud noises, and Bravo Team was issued flash bang grenades accordingly, expecting minimal resistance. Tunnelers are indeed susceptible to sudden illumination and concussive noise, which causes them to flee temporarily. Exposure to daylight or intense heat, such as from a flamer, causes them to burrow underground and resurface elsewhere. While burrowed, they are effectively unreachable. Their emergence from the ground gives no immediate hostile indication, making them dangerous ambush predators in the dark, confined spaces they prefer.
topic_desc_basic: Tunnelers are subterranean predators that emerged when nuclear explosions created The Divide, allowing them to hunt prey on the surface. They reproduce quickly, hunt in large groups, are capable of killing other predators such as Deathclaws, and may even pose a threat to the Mojave Wasteland in the future. The bite of Venomous Tunnelers can be just as lethal as a sting from a Bark Scorpion. As for their origin, Ulysses suspects that they have been around for a long time, and that Radiation might have had an effect on them.

topic_desc: The Alaskan Reclamation Operation was the United States military's response to the Chinese invasion of Alaska in 2066, a pivotal escalation of the Sino-American War and the broader Resource Wars. General Constantine Chase commanded the campaign, which marked the first major combat deployment of T-45 power armor units, giving American infantry a decisive advantage against entrenched Chinese forces in harsh arctic conditions. Airships provided logistical and tactical support, while genetically engineered deathclaws were fielded as living weapons. The operation spanned over a decade of grinding warfare across frozen terrain, culminating in January 2077 with the Battle of Anchorage and the full liberation of Alaska. The campaign's success restored control of the vital Alaskan Pipeline but came at enormous human cost. In the Capital Wasteland, the Anchorage Memorial in Washington, D.C. commemorates the soldiers who fought and died, and the Museum of Freedom maintained historical exhibits on the conflict before the Great War reduced both to ruins.
topic_desc_basic: The Alaskan Reclamation Operation was a pre-War military campaign launched by the United States Armed Forces in response to the Chinese invasion of Alaska in 2066. Commanded by General Constantine Chase, the operation saw American forces deploy airships, T-45 power armor units, and deathclaws against Chinese troops. The campaign lasted until January 2077, concluding with the Battle of Anchorage and the full liberation of Alaska. The operation is remembered as one of the most significant conflicts of the Sino-American War.

topic_desc: The Automation Riots erupted across pre-War America during the Resource Wars as corporations replaced human labor with advanced robotic systems produced by companies such as RobCo Industries. Labor-intensive sectors like mining and factory work were devastated, and specialized models such as the Strikebreaker Protectron were explicitly designed to suppress striking workers. In Pittsburgh, a supply plant manager named Tom McMullin attempted to delay the replacement of his workforce by reporting equipment problems to management, but when terminations were announced over loudspeakers, the remaining employees rioted and vandalized the protectrons, only to be suppressed by the machines themselves. The unrest reflected deep structural tensions in American society: conglomerates pursued total automation with government backing, while displaced workers faced homelessness and destitution. Ballot measures were proposed to accelerate the replacement of human government workers with automated systems. The riots demonstrated how corporate power, military force, and robotic technology converged to crush organized labor, foreshadowing the broader social collapse that culminated in the Great War of October 2077.
topic_desc_basic: The Automation Riots were pre-War conflicts caused by widespread unemployment as advanced robots replaced human workers during the Resource Wars. Mining, manufacturing, and other labor-intensive industries were hit especially hard. Displaced workers organized strikes, roadblocks, and violent protests, while corporations and government forces responded with security robots, troops, and riot-control weapons. The unrest became one sign of the severe economic and social instability that preceded the Great War.

topic_desc: The Battle of Anchorage was the climactic engagement of the Alaskan Reclamation Operation and one of the defining conflicts of the Resource Wars. Chinese forces invaded Alaska in the winter of 2066, seizing the strategically critical Alaskan Pipeline and threatening American energy supplies. General Constantine Chase led the U.S. Army in a protracted ten-year campaign to retake the territory. The battle saw the introduction of the T-51 series power armor, the most advanced infantry combat system of its era, which proved instrumental in overcoming Chinese fortifications. Following the liberation of Anchorage in January 2077, the T-60 power armor was subsequently deployed. The battle was commemorated in Washington, D.C. with the Anchorage Memorial honoring fallen soldiers, and the Museum of Freedom featured exhibits documenting the campaign. The conflict represented the peak of Sino-American military escalation and demonstrated the transformative role of power armor in modern warfare, less than a year before nuclear annihilation ended the war entirely.
topic_desc_basic: The Battle of Anchorage, also known as the Liberation of Anchorage, the Anchorage Campaign, and the Anchorage Reclamation, was a major military conflict of the Resource Wars fought between the United States and China. It began when Chinese forces invaded Alaska in the winter of 2066, threatening the Alaskan Pipeline. Under the leadership of General Constantine Chase, the U.S. Army deployed the newly introduced T-51 series power armor and ultimately liberated Anchorage after ten years of fighting.

topic_desc: The Brotherhood of Steel has experienced internal schisms throughout its history, but the Capital Wasteland civil war is among the most significant. Elder Owyn Lyons, dispatched from the West Coast to the East, deviated from the Brotherhood's core mission of technology recovery by redirecting his chapter toward protecting local wasteland inhabitants. This ideological shift was viewed by traditionalists as a betrayal of the Brotherhood's founding principles. Paladin Henry Casdin led a faction of dissenters who departed the Citadel and adopted the name Brotherhood Outcasts, retaining the original mission of preserving and securing advanced technology. Hostility between Lyons' loyalists and the Outcasts escalated into open violence, with both sides patrolling the Capital Wasteland and clashing over resources, technology, and territory. Despite their enmity, both factions continued to wear Brotherhood insignia and uphold elements of the organization's martial traditions. The schism weakened the chapter's overall strength, leaving it less capable of projecting power across the region and more vulnerable to threats from super mutants and other hostile forces.
topic_desc_basic: A Brotherhood Civil War is an internal armed conflict between Brotherhood of Steel factions. In the Capital Wasteland, a serious schism formed after Elder Owyn Lyons redirected his chapter toward protecting local people instead of concentrating solely on recovering technology. Paladin Henry Casdin and other dissenters left the Citadel as the Brotherhood Outcasts. Relations between the two groups became hostile and sometimes violent, though both continued to identify with Brotherhood traditions.

topic_desc: The Brotherhood War stemmed from a fundamental ideological clash over the control and regulation of technology, escalating into a prolonged series of violent confrontations across the former American Southwest. The conflict's duration is evidenced by NCR commanders such as Colonel Cassandra Moore completing four tours against Brotherhood forces. In 2274, the NCR moved into the Mojave to occupy Hoover Dam, encountering a Brotherhood chapter that had been conducting reclamation missions in the area for several years without opposition. Open hostilities began in 2275, extending beyond the Mojave as NCR platoons attacked six Brotherhood bunkers, four of which self-destructed. In 2276, the NCR launched Operation Sunburst against HELIOS One. The Brotherhood had been attempting to refurbish the facility, but Elder Elijah refused to order a retreat despite senior paladins like Hardin advising a fighting withdrawal, insisting he needed more time. The Brotherhood lost over half its paladins and knights, and Elder Elijah disappeared. Survivors retreated to a nearby bunker under new Elder McNamara, who restricted all outside activity. The NCR subsequently increased its military presence in the Mojave fivefold over the next few years.
topic_desc_basic: The Brotherhood War is a major conflict between the Brotherhood of Steel and the New California Republic, rooted in their disagreement over how technology should be controlled. The conflict spans the former American Southwest and the Mojave Wasteland, with NCR commanders such as Colonel Cassandra Moore having completed multiple tours against the Brotherhood. In 2275, fighting broke out in the Mojave between the NCR and the local Brotherhood chapter, extending to attacks on several Brotherhood bunkers across the region. The following year, the NCR launched Operation Sunburst, attacking and occupying the Brotherhood's fortifications at HELIOS One, where Elder Elijah had refused to retreat despite the location being indefensible.

topic_desc: The Exodus began on October 27, 2077, when Captain Roger Maxson led the remnants of the United States Army garrison from Mariposa Military Base toward a bunker at Lost Hills. The caravan of soldiers and their families faced repeated attacks by marauders throughout the journey. While the soldiers' Power Armor afforded them protection, the civilians and family members had no such defense, resulting in heavy casualties. Among the dead was Maxson's own wife. A group of soldiers broke away and headed south, disappearing from recorded history. A more significant split occurred when a separatist faction led by D. Allen departed against Maxson's wishes, setting out for the Glow in hopes of recovering advanced technology stored at that pre-war facility. Upon reaching Lost Hills, Maxson formally established the Brotherhood of Steel, using the bunker as the organization's headquarters. The Exodus thus marked the transition from military mutiny to the founding of one of the post-war wasteland's most distinctive organizations, with the losses suffered during the journey shaping the Brotherhood's insular culture and its emphasis on self-reliance.
topic_desc_basic: The Exodus was the post-War journey in which Captain Roger Maxson led the surviving United States Army soldiers and their families away from Mariposa Military Base on October 27, 2077, toward the Lost Hills bunker. The caravan was repeatedly attacked by marauders throughout the trek, and while the soldiers' Power Armor protected them, the unprotected civilians and families suffered high casualties, including Maxson's own wife. A group of soldiers broke off and headed south, never to be heard from again, while a separatist faction led by D. Allen split from the main body against Maxson's wishes and set out for the Glow in hopes of recovering technology stored there.

topic_desc: The food riots were a wave of civil unrest that swept the United States as dwindling food supplies and government rationing pushed civilians to desperation. The federal government's response was characterized by dismissiveness; White House officials belittled the protesters, claiming the president himself was suffering by substituting cube steak for prime rib and drinking what they called the detestable Chateau Montrose 2043 wine. The crisis turned deadly in Roxbury, Boston, where a hungry crowd stormed a food bank. Soldiers guarding the facility opened fire on unarmed civilians, killing four and injuring eight. Witnesses reported that the soldiers appeared to be selecting targets in advance and laughing as they did so, suggesting a disturbing level of premeditation. The food crisis also presented an opportunity for the Vault-Tec Corporation, which sought technological solutions through facilities such as the Vault-Tec Agricultural Research Center, designed to test agricultural automation, and Vault 22, which served as a research center for experimental fertilizer and genetically modified plant organisms.
topic_desc_basic: The food riots were incidents of civil unrest and protests that swept across the United States in response to dwindling food supplies and government rationing. The White House dismissed the protesters, with officials claiming the president himself was suffering by substituting cube steak for prime rib and drinking what they called the detestable Chateau Montrose 2043 wine. In Roxbury, Boston, tensions turned deadly when a hungry crowd stormed a food bank and the soldiers guarding it opened fire on the unarmed civilians, killing four and injuring eight. Witnesses reported that the soldiers appeared to be picking out targets in advance and laughing as they did so.

topic_desc: Following the Exodus from Mariposa Military Base to the Lost Hills bunker, Captain Roger Maxson formally established the Brotherhood of Steel. Drawing on the model of knights and scribes who preserved knowledge after the fall of Rome, Maxson intended the new organization to serve as a guardian of technical knowledge and dangerous technology in the aftermath of the Great War. The Brotherhood's founding represented a deliberate break from the collapsed United States military structure, adopting new ranks and traditions designed to endure in the post-war world. Maxson communicated by radio with surviving military contacts, expressing his vision of building something new to reclaim what had been lost. The organization's purpose was the preservation of knowledge rather than conquest or governance, a mission that would shape its culture for generations. From its headquarters at Lost Hills, the Brotherhood grew into a disciplined order with a hierarchy of paladins, knights, and scribes, each role dedicated to different aspects of the organization's mission to secure and protect advanced technology from misuse.
topic_desc_basic: The Brotherhood of Steel grew from the soldiers who followed Captain Roger Maxson after his revolt at the Mariposa Military Base shortly before the Great War. Maxson condemned the human experiments conducted there and led the survivors to the Lost Hills bunker. In the years that followed, he shaped them into a disciplined order devoted to preserving dangerous technology and technical knowledge. The new organization adopted ranks and traditions intended to outlast the fallen United States.
