topic_desc: Hidden Valley is a former United States Air Force testing range repurposed as the clandestine refuge of the Mojave Brotherhood of Steel chapter after their devastating defeat at HELIOS One during Operation: Sunburst in 2276. The valley contains four bunkers spread around its perimeter, with the west bunker serving as the Brotherhood's primary stronghold. The site's most remarkable feature is the DERVISH camouflage system, a pre-War cloaking mechanism that makes targeting the site impossible for automated systems and generates a sandstorm each evening, providing natural concealment for the bunker's inhabitants. Prospectors have reported seeing armored figures emerging from the valley during these storms, though intercom inquiries at the other three bunkers typically receive no response. The Brotherhood's presence here is a shadow of their former power: more than half the chapter died at HELIOS One, and Elder Elijah disappeared without a trace during the retreat. Under Paladin McNamara's leadership, the survivors have sealed themselves underground, sending patrols out only between 1 and 3 AM. Access to the west bunker requires a holotape passphrase recoverable from dead Brotherhood soldiers at REPCONN Headquarters, Black Mountain, or Nellis Air Force Base.
topic_desc_basic: Hidden Valley is a fenced-in former USAF testing range in the Mojave Wasteland, located northeast of the NCR Correctional Facility and southeast of Sloan. The valley contains four bunkers spread around its perimeter, with the west bunker serving as the home of the Mojave chapter of the Brotherhood of Steel, who retreated there after being defeated by the NCR at HELIOS One during Operation: Sunburst. The area is protected by the DERVISH camouflage system, a cloaking mechanism that makes targeting the site impossible for automated systems and generates a sandstorm each evening. Prospectors have reported seeing armored figures emerging from the valley during these storms, though the bunker intercoms typically garner no response.

topic_desc: Hidden Valley Bunker is one of four bunkers clustered within a valley southeast of Sloan, but only one serves as the active entrance to the Mojave chapter of the Brotherhood of Steel. The site relies on a pre-War DERVISH camouflage system originally designed to cloak the bunkers from automated targeting, rendering the facility nearly invisible to external threats. Internally, the bunker is powered by a CANDLE fusion power system rated for an estimated 752 years of operation, ensuring long-term self-sufficiency. The chapter is led by Elder McNamara, who has kept the Brotherhood isolated behind sealed doors following their defeat at HELIOS One. Head Paladin Hardin represents a faction within the bunker that favors more aggressive action. The second floor houses the archives, where Head Scribe Taggart and Apprentice Watkins work among virtual reality pods surrounding the main reactor. The facility also contains a self-destruct terminal, reflecting the Brotherhood's willingness to destroy the bunker rather than let it fall into outside hands.
topic_desc_basic: The Hidden Valley Bunker is a location in the Mojave Wasteland situated southeast of Sloan, serving as the home of the Brotherhood of Steel. The facility is divided into two main levels containing personnel quarters, an armory, a medical bay, a workshop, and virtual reality chambers surrounding the main reactor. The bunker is led by Elder McNamara and Head Paladin Hardin, with scribes and knights occupying the archives and machine shop on the second floor.

topic_desc: Higgs Village is a residential complex inside the Big MT research facility, consisting of six numbered houses arranged around a central fountain within a warehouse structure. Each house was assigned to one of the pre-War scientists who would later become the Think Tank: Doctor 0 in House #00, Doctor Klein in #101, Doctor Mobius in #102, Doctor Borous in #103, Doctor Dala in #104, and Doctor 8 in #108. The village layout closely resembles the Tranquility Lane simulation, with six houses enclosing a cul-de-sac and fountain, suggesting it was used for some form of pre-War experiment or testing. Personal effects remain scattered throughout: Doctor Mobius's house contains large quantities of Mentats, Doctor Dala's residence is filled with teddy bears arranged as audiences on a runway stage, and Doctor Borous's home includes a dog house for his dog Gabe and a basement containing dissected animals. The central fountain can be activated through the X-17 Meteorological Station's weather test. A portrait of Mr. House with knives stabbed through it sits in Doctor 0's former kitchen, hinting at the scientists' resentment toward their former employer.

topic_desc: Hoover Dam stands as one of the most significant strategic and political landmarks in the Mojave Wasteland. Before the Great War, the dam was equipped with anti-aircraft defenses, and when the bombs fell, Mr. House's networked mainframes and laser systems preserved the structure in near-pristine condition alongside much of Las Vegas. The Followers of the Apocalypse noted the dam's continued existence as early as 2170, but it remained unoccupied until the New California Republic arrived during its Mojave Campaign in 2274. The Mojave Brotherhood of Steel had intended to claim the dam but became sidetracked at HELIOS One. Fearing the loss of his city's power source to the NCR, yet recognizing the mutual threat posed by Caesar's Legion, Mr. House negotiated the Treaty of New Vegas, granting 95 percent of the dam's output to the NCR in exchange for recognition of New Vegas sovereignty. Within a year, the NCR had the dam running at half capacity. In 2277, the Legion under the Malpais Legate attempted to seize the dam but was repelled by NCR Rangers and First Recon sharpshooters under Chief Hanlon, who lured elite Legion forces into Boulder City and detonated pre-placed explosives. Colonel Cassandra Moore and General Lee Oliver have since heavily fortified the dam against a second Legion assault, while civilian engineers struggle to maintain the aging turbines.
topic_desc_basic: Hoover Dam, often called the Old World Wall, is a massive hydroelectric dam on the Colorado River that survived the Great War in almost untouched condition thanks to Mr. House's defense systems. After centuries of abandonment, the New California Republic occupied the structure in 2274 and later signed the Treaty of New Vegas, securing 95 percent of its power output while guaranteeing the sovereignty of New Vegas. In 2277, Caesar's Legion attempted to seize the dam but was defeated by NCR forces during the First Battle of Hoover Dam.

topic_desc: Jacobstown occupies a pre-War resort on Mount Charleston northwest of New Vegas, repurposed as a refuge for super mutants seeking a peaceful existence apart from human conflict. Marcus, formerly the sheriff of Broken Hills in the far west, departed Black Mountain with a splinter group of super mutants after tensions with Tabitha's faction became untenable. He named the settlement after an old friend and established it with the principle that all are welcome provided they remain nonviolent. The surrounding foothills sustain a large bighorner population that supplies food and hides for trade, which Marcus hopes to leverage into commercial relations with the New California Republic. The settlement also shelters a contingent of nightkin led by Keene, who suffer from a mental illness exacerbated by prolonged Stealth Boy use. Doctor Henry and his assistant Calamity are researching a cure, but progress is slow and the nightkin grow increasingly restless. External pressures compound the settlement's difficulties: NCR Senator Morales seeks to use Jacobstown as a scapegoat for attacks on NCR citizens' brahmin, and mercenaries have been dispatched to threaten or displace the community. Marcus has sent Neil to the Black Mountain area to redirect wandering super mutants toward Jacobstown.
topic_desc_basic: Jacobstown is a pre-War resort on Mount Charleston northwest of New Vegas, now serving as a super mutant settlement founded by Marcus, the former sheriff of Broken Hills. The settlement is home to super mutants, nightkin led by Keene, and a sizable bighorner population that provides food and trade goods. Doctor Henry and Calamity are working on a cure for the mental illness afflicting the nightkin, though progress is slow and the nightkin grow restless.

topic_desc: The King's School of Impersonation occupies a three-story pre-War building at the intersection of Fremont Street and Las Vegas Boulevard in Freeside, southeast of the Atomic Wrangler Casino and northwest of Mick & Ralph's. Before the Great War, the establishment functioned as a school teaching impersonation techniques. After the war, the building became the headquarters of the Kings, a gang that adopted the mannerisms and aesthetic of a pre-War cultural figure they call "the King." The gang persists in this emulation while functioning as Freeside's predominant power. The building's first floor contains a reception area and a theater with a stage where gang members perform for their leader. The upper floors house bedrooms, recreation rooms, and storage. A chalkboard on the third floor bears a "King Impersonation Checklist" with instructions to move hips, say "uh huh," say "momma," and prepare peanut butter and banana sandwiches. Sergio, the gang's hairstylist, works from a dressing room on the first floor. Pacer, a senior gang member, guards access to the King.
topic_desc_basic: The King's School of Impersonation is a three-story building in Freeside at the intersection of Fremont Street and Las Vegas Boulevard, serving as the headquarters of the Kings gang and their leader, known simply as The King. The building features a reception area, a theater with a stage where gang members perform for The King, and multiple floors of bedrooms, recreation rooms, and storage areas. topic_desc: The Lucky 38 Resort and Casino is the tallest structure in the Mojave Wasteland and the most prominent feature of the New Vegas skyline. Before the Great War, the establishment was linked to a mob shootout on July 13, 2072, when one of the alleged perpetrators from a heist at the nearby Ultra-Luxe took refuge in the Lucky 38 before escaping through a window. In the years preceding the war, Mr. House made extensive modifications to the building, equipping it with long-range laser cannons connected to advanced processing centers designed to intercept incoming nuclear warheads. A large underground storage facility was constructed to house an army of Securitrons, and a concealed chamber accessible via private elevator was installed as Mr. House's life support system. Integrated into the Lucky 38's mainframe, C3I broadcasting arrays, and power core, Mr. House positioned himself to survive the catastrophe. However, the Platinum Chip containing an essential operating system upgrade was never delivered due to the Great War. Despite relying on an inferior operating system, Mr. House successfully neutralized most warheads targeting the Mojave before a system failure left him incapacitated for nearly two centuries. He regained consciousness in 2138 and reactivated the Lucky 38 in 2274 upon detecting NCR scouts at Hoover Dam, deploying Securitrons to secure the Strip and negotiating with three tribes to restore the city.
topic_desc_basic: The Lucky 38 Resort and Casino is the most prominent structure on the New Vegas Strip, serving as both a pre-War relic and a symbol of Mr. House's vision for Las Vegas. Before the Great War, Mr. House extensively modified the building with long-range laser cannons to intercept nuclear warheads and constructed a concealed chamber to serve as his life support system.

topic_desc: The Lucky 38 Presidential Suite, also called the High Roller Suite by Victor, is a spacious accommodation within the Lucky 38 casino comprising five rooms: a master bedroom, guest room, kitchen, bathroom, and recreation room. The master bedroom contains a bed, a desk, and a sitting area, with wardrobes and weapon trunks available for storage. The recreation room houses a pool table, a television, and a snow globe stand. A notable detail in the recreation room is an arrangement of five billiard balls shaped into an arrow; the numbers on the balls add up to thirty-eight, and the arrow points toward a Lucky 38 poster. The guest room offers two double beds and storage furniture. The kitchen contains a long table, two ovens, and a refrigerator for food storage, with a workbench available. The bathroom features clean, radiation-free water. Additional furnishings can be arranged through a terminal in the suite. The suite's background music is "Radiation Storm," a piece originally associated with a pre-War facility known as the Glow.
topic_desc_basic: The Lucky 38 Presidential Suite, also referred to as the High Roller Suite by Victor, is a luxurious accommodation located within the Lucky 38 casino in New Vegas. The suite features a master bedroom, a guest room, a kitchen, a bathroom, and a recreation room. It serves as a clubhouse for companions, who can be dismissed to this location and will engage in various activities such as wandering, sitting, sleeping, drinking, eating, and interacting with one another. The recreation room houses a pool table, a television, and the Snow Globe Stand, while the kitchen contains a long table, two ovens, and a refrigerator.

topic_desc: Mick & Ralph's is a consumable and gun shop in Freeside's slum area, just northeast of the east gate. The business is operated by two colleagues: Mick sells weapons, including ballistic firearms and specialty ammunition, while Ralph handles consumables and special services. The building's sign originally read only "Ralph's," with "Mick &" added after the Great War when the duo began operating from the premises. Ralph offers fake passports to the New Vegas Strip for five hundred caps, or at a reduced price through bartering or a favor from the King. He also sells a container of chlorine intended for the Ultra-Luxe. Mick's specialty inventory includes the Naughty Nightwear and various ballistic weapons. A hidden room behind the shop displays several weapons mounted on its walls, including a railway rifle, two infiltrators, and a Chinese pistol, alongside cowboy hats and other assorted items. The second floor contains the proprietors' bedrooms, washing machines, desks, and periodicals including Tæles of Chivalrie, Fixin' Things, and Programmer's Digest. A crier outside advertises the shop's wares to passersby in Freeside.
topic_desc_basic: Mick & Ralph's is an active consumable and gun shop located in the Freeside slum area of New Vegas, just northeast of the east gate. topic_desc: The Mojave Outpost occupies a pre-War highway checkpoint on Interstate 15 at Mountain Pass, California, between the Clark and Mescal mountain ranges. Its strategic position at the California-Nevada state line makes it the boundary of fully NCR-controlled territory and the primary gateway for all caravan traffic flowing into the Mojave from the Republic's core lands. Established in 2249, the outpost predates the Ranger Unification Treaty of 2271, when Desert Rangers and NCR Rangers met at this very site to formalize their merger against Caesar's Legion. In exchange, NCR extended its jurisdiction to southern Nevada, New Vegas, and Hoover Dam. The Unification Monument—two large statues dominating the northern end of the valley—commemorates this historic accord. By 2281, the outpost's relative safety compared to eastern postings along the Colorado River has led to personnel being siphoned off, and the NCRCF prison break forced a permanent detachment at Primm, leaving the outpost unable to maintain patrol minimums. Stranded caravans back up at the checkpoint, and anxious soldiers fear that if Legion forces push past Nipton, the outpost becomes the frontline.
topic_desc_basic: NCR Ranger Outpost Mojave, commonly called Mojave Outpost, sits near the California-Nevada state line along Interstate 15 and serves as the gateway to the Mojave Wasteland for caravans traveling from the New California Republic's core lands. Established in 2249, it functions as a military hub and administrative command center for operations in the southwestern Mojave, with soldiers acting as border guards to protect trade routes. The outpost is marked by the Unification Monument, commemorating the 2271 Ranger Unification Treaty that merged the Desert Rangers of Nevada with the NCR Rangers against the threat of Caesar's Legion. By 2281, the outpost struggles with reduced patrols and backed-up caravans following the NCRCF prison break, leaving anxious soldiers worried that if Legion forces push past Nipton, the outpost itself could become the frontline.

topic_desc: The Mojave Wasteland's remarkable preservation stems directly from Mr. House's pre-War defense systems: of 77 atomic warheads launched at Las Vegas and surrounding areas, 59 were disarmed mid-flight, nine destroyed by Lucky 38 laser defenses, and only nine struck the surrounding desert. This spared the region the wholesale devastation seen elsewhere, leaving infrastructure, technology, and even neon signs functional nearly two centuries later. The geopolitical landscape by 2281 is a three-way stalemate: the NCR, having occupied Hoover Dam in 2274 under President Kimball and signed the Treaty of New Vegas granting 95% of the dam's power to NCR home states; Caesar's Legion, which suffered defeat at the First Battle of Hoover Dam when Chief Hanlon's tactical retreat to Boulder City lured Legion forces into a trap; and Mr. House's Free Economic Zone, fortifying the Strip while biding its time. The balance is delicate—should one faction attack another, the third could exploit the vulnerability. The Legion seeks the Strip as a new capital replacing Flagstaff, while the NCR aims for full annexation, its war increasingly unpopular and expensive back in California.
topic_desc_basic: The Mojave Wasteland, synonymous with the pre-War Mojave Desert, spans portions of California, Nevada, and Arizona. Thanks to intricate defense systems established by Mr. House, the region survived the Great War relatively unscathed, leaving much of its infrastructure and technology intact. By 2281, the region is locked in a delicate balance of power between the expanding New California Republic, the encroaching forces of Caesar's Legion, and the independent Free Economic Zone of New Vegas.

topic_desc: The NCRCF was originally the Jean Conservancy, a low-security all-female prison, before the NCR repurposed it as a labor camp where inmates maintained regional railways. The facility's transformation into a Powder Ganger stronghold followed an uprising organized by inmate Samuel Cooke, who stockpiled blast powder and makeshift weapons to orchestrate the breakout. The escaped convicts fractured: some scattered to Vault 19 and the surrounding wasteland, while the remainder held the prison under Eddie's leadership. The Brotherhood of Steel maintains a active surveillance interest, posting scouts nearby as part of a broader intelligence-gathering effort. The facility's location near Jean, Nevada—on the road between Goodsprings and the Mojave Outpost—places it squarely on the I-15 corridor, making the prison break's disruption of NCR authority especially consequential for regional security. The NCRCF break directly forced the Mojave Outpost to establish a permanent garrison at Primm, depleting patrol strength along the highway and contributing to the caravan backup that characterizes the southwestern Mojave in 2281.
topic_desc_basic: The NCR Correctional Facility, also known as the NCRCF, is a former prison southeast of Goodsprings that was operated by the New California Republic as a labor camp where inmates maintained the regional railways. Originally the Jean Conservancy, a low-security all-female prison, the facility fell to a prisoner uprising organized by an inmate named Samuel Cooke, who stockpiled blast powder and makeshift weapons. Following the breakout, many of the escaped convicts, who came to be known as Powder Gangers, scattered across the surrounding wasteland while the remainder stayed behind under the leadership of a man named Eddie. The facility is watched with interest by the Brotherhood of Steel, which keeps scouts posted nearby.

topic_desc: The NCR Sharecropper Farms represent a calculated political instrument as much as an agricultural venture. Established under the Thaler Act, the farms incentivize private farmers to cultivate Mojave land in exchange for NCR military protection, housing, food, and water, with crop yields directed to Camp McCarran, Hoover Dam, and other military installations. The Office of Science and Industry at Camp McCarran pre-calculates optimal water usage for each crop, drawing irrigation from Lake Mead through miles of pipework. By 2281, plans exist to expand water flow and farm count specifically to encourage New Vegas residents to vote for NCR annexation—making the farms a soft-power tool for territorial integration. However, concurrent crises threaten this strategy: radiation seeping from Vault 34 contaminates the soil, and water siphoning linked to Westside reduces rations to 80% of intended levels. Despite legitimate farmer complaints, NCR administrative staff dismiss the growers as incompetent, ignoring the environmental degradation. A military unit remains permanently stationed to deter theft, underscoring the operation's strategic importance to NCR logistics.
topic_desc_basic: The NCR Sharecropper Farms are an agricultural settlement located directly south of Freeside's East Gate in the Mojave Wasteland. Established under the Thaler Act, private farmers cultivate the land for the New California Republic in exchange for military protection, housing, food, and water, with a portion of the crop yield going to NCR military locations such as Camp McCarran and Hoover Dam. Irrigation water is pumped from Lake Mead through a pipe system, with the Office of Science and Industry at Camp McCarran pre-calculating optimal water usage for each crop. A military unit is stationed on-site at all times to deter theft.

topic_desc: Nellis Air Force Base, formerly the United States Air Force Warfare Center under the motto Testing, Tactics, Training, suffered multiple nuclear strikes during the Great War that left it intensely radioactive. For decades, wastelanders avoided the site by habit, allowing it to sit empty. By the time the Boomers arrived from Vault 34 roughly five decades before the present, their Pip-Boy Geiger counters confirmed radiation had decayed to survivable levels. The Boomers repurposed the base into a self-sufficient settlement: water pumped from Lake Mead irrigates crops of grains and green vegetables, soy and legumes supply protein, and maize feeds a biodiesel refinery. The Nellis solar array and generator power the entire facility. Pre-War virtual reality pilot training stations in one hangar sustain the Boomers' dream of aerial combat, a fascination rooted in Loyal's discovery of a file on a crashed B-29 bomber in Lake Mead. Heavy arms retrieved from Area 2 and the base's surviving defensive structures, including a howitzer team at the front gate, enforce a strict exclusion zone. The Boomers' rudimentary education covers farming and combat, reflecting their dual identity as agrarian survivalists and militant isolationists.
topic_desc_basic: Nellis Air Force Base, also known as the Nellis homeland, is a heavily fortified location northeast of New Vegas in the Mojave Wasteland. Once the United States Air Force Warfare Center, the base was struck by nuclear weapons during the Great War and left highly radioactive and abandoned for decades. The Boomers, a group that originally inhabited Vault 34, eventually settled there and made it their home, using the base's remaining defenses and their own heavy arms to keep strangers away. The base is largely self-sufficient, with irrigated crops, solar power, a biodiesel refinery, and medical and educational facilities, while the Boomers train in virtual reality stations in hopes of one day returning to the skies.

topic_desc: Nelson's strategic value lies in its position between Camp Forlorn Hope and Camp Searchlight, covering a gap along the Colorado River that the NCR sought to plug through military occupation. Post-War miners had previously attempted resource extraction from the area before the NCR established a camp there. Caesar's Legion under Decanus Dead Sea struck before NCR troopers could settle in, exploiting the simultaneous destruction of Camp Searchlight and the overstretched condition of Camp Forlorn Hope. No counter-attack materialized, and the town has remained under Legion control. Dead Sea, operating under direct orders from Caesar to demoralize surrounding NCR forces, employed systematically brutal methods: captured troopers were hacked apart, forced off cliffs overlooking the river, and three were crucified within sight of NCR positions. To sustain pressure, Dead Sea launched subsequent raids against Camp Forlorn Hope to the north. The town's layout reflects its contested nature: sandbag bunkers and chain-link fencing enclose the perimeter, a hilltop overlook on the northern edge provides Legion surveillance, and the open-air courtyard now dominated by three crucified NCR troopers serves as a grim psychological weapon. A Brotherhood of Steel scout observed both Nelson and Camp Forlorn Hope as part of ongoing regional monitoring.
topic_desc_basic: Nelson is a settlement in the Mojave Wasteland, located southwest of Camp Forlorn Hope and east of Novac. Originally occupied by the New California Republic as a strategic military camp between Camp Forlorn Hope and Camp Searchlight, it was attacked and captured by Caesar's Legion under Decanus Dead Sea shortly after the NCR occupation. The town has remained under Legion control, with Dead Sea executing captured NCR troopers to demoralize surrounding forces and launching raids against Camp Forlorn Hope.

topic_desc: New Vegas owes its survival to Robert House's foresight. In 2065, he deemed nuclear war a mathematical certainty within fifteen years and began preparations. When the Great War came, the absence of the Platinum Chip's upgrade data left his systems suboptimal, yet networked mainframes still predicted and force-transmitted disarm code subsets to fifty-nine warheads, neutralizing them before impact. Roof-mounted laser cannons atop the Lucky 38 destroyed another nine. Of those that penetrated, none struck the main city. The effort caused software glitches and system crashes that plunged House into a coma lasting decades. Upon waking, he recruited salvage teams to locate the Chip and hired tribals—thereafter the Three Families—to rebuild the Strip, completing renovations in 2274 ahead of NCR scouts' arrival. The resulting Treaty of New Vegas granted House sovereignty over the Strip while permitting NCR access, a compromise the NCR accepted because the Legion threat made open confrontation untenable. House leveraged NCR occupation as his economic engine, describing its citizens as a society of customers desperate for luxury. Beyond the Strip, Freeside serves as the main slum controlled by the Kings and Van Graffs, Westside maintains its own militia and self-reliant agriculture, and South Vegas has fallen to the Fiends operating from Vault 3. The oldest structure, the Old Mormon Fort, predates all post-War construction. A network of sewers beneath the city shelters both humans and creatures.
topic_desc_basic: New Vegas, built on the remains of pre-War Las Vegas in the Mojave Desert, is managed by the reclusive Mr. House and his army of Securitron robots. Having predicted the Great War, House defended the city with laser cannons and disarm codes, sparing the main city from nuclear devastation before falling into a coma for decades. Upon waking, he rebuilt the New Vegas Strip with the help of recruited tribals known as the Three Families, completing renovations in 2274 just before NCR forces entered the region, leading to the Treaty of New Vegas that granted him sovereignty over the Strip.

topic_desc: The New Vegas Strip's political economy rests on a calculated bargain between Robert House and the NCR, formalized through the Treaty of New Vegas. House completed the Strip's renovation in 2274 deliberately before NCR forces entered the region, presenting a fait accompli that forced the NCR to negotiate rather than annex. The treaty's provisions reveal House's shrewdness: NCR soldiers and civilians retain access to the Strip's casinos and establishments, but troopers are forbidden from carrying firearms, and Securitrons may not act against them. The NCR was further granted an embassy, lending legitimacy to House's sovereignty while preventing military confrontation. House openly characterized the NCR occupation as the engine of his growing economy, describing NCR citizens as a society of customers desperate for comfort, ease, and luxury. Street vendors operating on the Strip sign franchise agreements forfeiting fifty percent of profits to House daily. Access control is enforced by Securitron gatekeepers who verify visitors possess at least two thousand caps, hold a New Vegas Passport, or arrive via the Camp McCarran monorail under NCR military auspices. The NCR's willingness to compromise stemmed from the Legion threat, making the Strip a buffer rather than a battleground.
topic_desc_basic: The New Vegas Strip is the rebuilt heart of New Vegas, restored by Robert House with the help of Securitrons and the Three Families in 2274 before NCR forces entered the region. The Treaty of New Vegas granted House sovereignty over the Strip while allowing NCR soldiers and civilians to visit its casinos and establishments, with the NCR forbidden from annexing it by force due to the Legion threat. Powered by electricity from Hoover Dam, the Strip features several reopened pre-War establishments and serves as a major draw for tourism, with NCR citizens described by House as a society of customers desperate for comfort and luxury. Entrance to the Strip is guarded by Securitrons who require visitors to demonstrate sufficient wealth or possess a New Vegas Passport.

topic_desc: Nipton's fate illustrates the brutal calculus of Mojave border politics in 2281. Mayor Joseph B. Steyn attempted an impossible balancing act: trading with Powder Gangers by day and hosting NCR soldiers by night, then betraying both to Caesar's Legion for 8,000 caps. Vulpes Inculta repaid the deal by subjecting the entire population to a lottery modeled on the town's own pre-war tradition, deciding who would be decapitated, crucified, enslaved, or spared. The winner, Oliver Swanick, was freed; the runner-up, Boxcars, was crippled; Steyn was burned alive on a pyre of tires. The massacre served as deliberate psychological warfare, intended to spread terror across the Mojave. Critically, the New California Republic's failure to intervene signaled weakness to the local Brotherhood of Steel chapter, which observed through a scout that NCR was unwilling or unable to respond, reshaping regional power calculations.
topic_desc_basic: Nipton is a small town in the southern Mojave Wasteland, located near the Nevada-California state line and transected by railroad tracks. Before the Great War, the town was known for hosting a lottery that offered a jackpot worth millions of dollars. After the war, Nipton was led by Mayor Joseph B. Steyn, who attempted to maintain peace between NCR soldiers and Powder Gangers by inviting each group at different times of day.

topic_desc: Novac's survival hinges on salvage economics and geographic accident. Founded around the Dino Dee-lite Motel along Highway 95, the town drew its name from a broken neon sign reading only "NOVAC." Its proximity to the REPCONN Test Site provided a steady supply of salvageable rocket components and souvenirs, sustaining trade when little else could. The closure of parallel Interstate 15 rerouted caravan traffic through Highway 95, bringing both commerce and danger. Two NCR Army veterans, Craig Boone and Manny Vargas, converted Dinky the T-Rex into a sniper's nest, making the town's kitsch landmark a genuine defensive asset. Retired Ranger Andy supplemented their efforts despite injuries ending his active service. By 2281, converging threats, including Caesar's Legion expansion, the Bright Brotherhood's arrival, and feral ghouls blocking the REPCONN road, jeopardized the town's fragile stability. Residents remained grateful for NCR protection yet deeply suspicious of outsiders.
topic_desc_basic: Novac is an independent town along Highway 95 in the Mojave Wasteland, named after the broken motel sign at its entrance. Before the Great War, it was a small roadside stopover featuring the Dinky the Dinosaur novelty attraction and the World's 2nd Largest Thermometer, catering to travelers heading to the nearby REPCONN Test Site. After the war, settlers reclaimed the motel and surrounding area, establishing a modest community sustained by salvage from the REPCONN site and trade along the highway. The town is guarded by two NCR Army veterans, Craig Boone and Manny Vargas, who use the Dinky the T-Rex statue as a sniper's nest, while retired Ranger Andy also contributes to its defense.

topic_desc: Primm's strategic position along Interstate 15, connecting Los Angeles and Las Vegas, made it a natural trade hub as the NCR expanded into the Mojave. Pre-war attractions like the Vikki and Vance Casino and the Bison Steve Hotel with its rollercoaster, El Diablo, gave the town its reputation as "budget Vegas." The NCR Correctional Facility prison break shattered this prosperity, as escaped convicts seized the town center and forced civilians into the Vikki and Vance. Merchants Samuel and Michelle abandoned Primm entirely for the 188 Trading Post. The NCR's 5th Battalion, under Lieutenant Hayes, established a western barricade but lacked manpower to retake the settlement, their outpost primarily serving to prevent convicts from pushing south toward the Mojave Outpost rather than protecting Primm itself. This gap revealed the overextension of NCR forces across the Mojave, unable to secure even a key trade corridor on a major interstate.
topic_desc_basic: Primm, sometimes called "budget Vegas" or "the other New Vegas," is an independent settlement in the Mojave Wasteland located alongside Interstate 15 in Clark County, Nevada. Before the Great War, it was a small resort town featuring attractions like the Vikki and Vance Casino and the Bison Steve Casino and Hotel. As the New California Republic expanded into the Mojave, it became a promising trade town until a recent breakout of prisoners from the NCR Correctional Facility put an end to commerce. The escaped convicts, known as Powder Gangers, took over the center of town, forcing the residents to seek refuge in the Vikki and Vance Casino while the NCR's 5th Battalion watches from afar, lacking the numbers to reclaim the strategic location.

topic_desc: Puesta del Sol, Spanish for "sunset," forms one of two districts of the Villa surrounding the Sierra Madre casino. Its construction lagged behind its sister district Salida del Sol, as if funding and momentum had simply exhausted themselves. Clashes between district construction crews and casino crews further hampered progress. The incomplete infrastructure left a warren of rooftops, balconies, and half-finished buildings that became critical for navigating above the toxic red Cloud choking ground levels. A ventilation system in the Puesta del Sol Switching Station could clear much of the Cloud, making it a strategic priority. The district was infested with Ghost People and seeded with bear traps, radios broadcasting collar-detonating frequencies, and disguised speakers that could summon further danger. Sierra Madre vending machine codes scattered throughout the district offered access to weapons, ammunition, and supplies, reflecting Father Elijah's repurposing of the casino's pre-war infrastructure for his own ends.
topic_desc_basic: Puesta del Sol is a district of the Villa surrounding the Sierra Madre, divided into northern and southern sections. Its construction crews frequently clashed with the casino construction crews, and the district's development lagged behind that of its sister district, Salida del Sol, as if the effort had simply run out of steam and money. Much of the ground level is choked by the toxic red Cloud, though a ventilation system in the Puesta del Sol Switching Station can clear much of it. The area is infested with Ghost People and littered with bear traps, radios, and speakers that can detonate collars or summon further threats.

topic_desc: REPCONN Aerospace, formally the Rocket Engineering and Production Company of Nevada, operated from Henderson as a rocket manufacturer before RobCo Industries acquired the firm in late 2075 or 2076. RobCo transformed the headquarters into a secure facility for classified research, installing automatic facial recognition monitors, badge scanners, security locks, and heavily armed sentry bots. Employees faced constant surveillance and risked harm from automated defenses if caught without identification badges. The third floor was restricted to executives requiring a daily password. The facility became a nexus of corporate espionage: a mole named Julia Masters, working for Poseidon Energy, was tasked with intercepting the Q-35 Matter Modulator prototype during transit to the Department of Defense. Simultaneously, REPCONN's own plasma rifle project relied on Project SEMELE schematics stolen from Poseidon Energy. Though REPCONN's information services detected the leak, no concrete evidence supported official action. The Great War interrupted the prototype's delivery, leaving the Q-35 sealed within the building.
topic_desc_basic: REPCONN Headquarters in Henderson, Nevada, served as the home office of REPCONN Aerospace, formally known as the Rocket Engineering and Production Company of Nevada, a firm specializing in rocket manufacture. RobCo Industries acquired the company and overhauled the building with heightened security measures, including automatic facial recognition monitors, badge scanners, security locks, and heavily armed sentry bots, to support classified research operations. Employees were required to wear identification badges at all times, and the third floor was restricted to executives who needed a daily password for access. The facility was the site of a plasma rifle project that produced the Q-35 Matter Modulator, the first working prototype of its kind.

topic_desc: Ranger Station Charlie occupies the converted ruins of the pre-War Shady Pines trailer park, repurposed by the New California Republic Rangers into a fortified outpost along railroad tracks southwest of Novac. Trailers were stacked into makeshift walls, with the communications center and barracks established in the former trailer park office. The station's strategic value lay in projecting NCR territorial control across the southeastern Mojave, a role that grew critical following the catastrophic fall of Camp Searchlight to Legion sabotage. However, the site's placement below surrounding hills compromised radio communications with Camp McCarran, creating persistent operational friction. Ranger Beaumont commanded the station but was frequently absent on patrol, leaving Comm Officer Stepinac to maintain the encampment. The station's vulnerability became evident when Caesar's Legion forces massacred its garrison, leaving booby-trapped corpses and audio recordings claiming responsibility and announcing a hostage capture.
topic_desc_basic: Ranger Station Charlie is a New California Republic Rangers stronghold in the central Mojave Wasteland, converted from the pre-War Shady Pines trailer park. Located southwest of Novac along a railroad track, the station provides the rangers with a safehouse and helps establish territorial control over the southeastern sector of the Mojave, a role that became especially important after the fall of Camp Searchlight. The trailers have been piled up to create a makeshift fortress, with the communications center and barracks set up in the old trailer park office building. The commanding officer is Ranger Beaumont, but he and most of his command are typically out on patrol, leaving Comm Officer Stepinac to watch over the encampment.

topic_desc: Salida del Sol constituted the eastern residential district of the Villa surrounding the Sierra Madre casino, originally built to house a church and the homes of many casino staff before the Great War. The district is bisected into northern and southern halves, both saturated with traps, mines, and the toxic Cloud that permeates the Sierra Madre's atmosphere. Ghost People infest the area in significant numbers, complicating navigation through blocked gates and locked doors. The Salida Switching Station in the southwest corner houses a terminal capable of restoring power to ventilation systems, partially clearing the Cloud and easing passage. Graffiti tags reading "Run, run, run!" serve as navigational aids in the northern section, oriented to guide travelers back toward the Villa and away from the bell tower. Campanas del Sol, the northernmost point, contains the bell tower control panel for triggering the Sierra Madre Gala Event, along with vending machine codes for hologram rifle components and super stimpaks.
topic_desc_basic: Salida del Sol is the eastern section of the Villa surrounding the Sierra Madre, originally built to house a church and the homes of many casino staff before the Great War. The district is divided into northern and southern halves, both heavily littered with traps and mines often hidden within the toxic Cloud. It is infested with a large number of Ghost People, and navigation is complicated by blocked gates, locked doors, and the ever-present haze. The Salida Switching Station sits in the southwest corner and contains a terminal capable of restoring power to the ventilation system to clear the Cloud from the area.

topic_desc: Frederick Sinclair's Sierra Madre was conceived not merely as a casino but as an integrated survival architecture, a self-sufficient fortress against nuclear annihilation. The resort's vending machines, supplied through a technology exchange with Big MT, were engineered to provide complete self-sufficiency for inhabitants cut off from the outside world. In return, Sinclair agreed the casino and villa would serve as proving grounds for experimental technologies including saturnite alloy, hazmat suits, and prototype matter recombiners. The Cloud, the poisonous atmosphere that now envelops the area, was an unintended byproduct of those same Big MT experiments. Construction was split between two contractors: a competent firm for the casino and a corrupt, slacking company for the Villa, producing numerous incidents and structural problems. Sinclair's Sierra Madre Security, staffed by former police officers, was tasked with enforcing his prohibition on outside alcohol and chems among construction workers, though corruption permeated the force. The security chief himself received smuggled alcohol from a figure known as Mr. Yesterday. Sinclair ultimately tolerated the smuggling so long as construction continued without worker violence.
topic_desc_basic: The Sierra Madre is a legendary pre-War casino resort and adjoining villa designed by Frederick Sinclair as both a luxurious retreat and a shelter from nuclear holocaust, where guests could reverse their fortunes and begin again. Surrounded by a poisonous Cloud born of experimental technologies supplied by Big MT, the isolated location has lured countless prospectors through a mysterious radio broadcast advertising its Gala Event, though none have returned. The resort was designed for total self-sufficiency, with unique vending machines providing all necessities to inhabitants cut off from the outside world, while a small but well-equipped human security force guarded the grounds alongside holographic defenders.

topic_desc: The Silver Rush occupies a pre-War casino on Fremont Street in Freeside, established in 2071 as a rival to the neighboring Atomic Wrangler. The Van Graff family coveted the site for their energy weapons trade and killed the previous occupants to seize it. When the Kings arrived to protest the takeover, the Van Graffs used plasma weapons to reduce several of their members to goo, establishing a tense détente that persists to the present day. Frieda Van Graff initially managed the operation but departed to pursue personal interests, leaving Gloria Van Graff and Jean-Baptiste Cutting in charge. The building serves as both the Van Graff family's headquarters and the largest energy weapons market in the Mojave Wasteland. Despite Freeside's reputation for cheap goods and desperation, Gloria Van Graff maintains that her clientele do not care where they travel to purchase quality merchandise. Security is heavy: five armed thugs patrol the premises, and theft is punished immediately. Visitors are required to surrender all weapons at the entrance, including holdout weapons, before being allowed inside.
topic_desc_basic: The Silver Rush is a location in Freeside on Fremont Street, opposite the Atomic Wrangler Casino. Established in 2071, it originally rivaled the Atomic Wrangler as a casino before the Van Graff family killed its former occupants and took over. When the Kings protested, the Van Graffs reduced several of their members to goo, and the two groups have left each other alone ever since. Now the largest retailer of energy weapons in the Mojave Wasteland, the Silver Rush is headed by Gloria Van Graff and Jean-Baptiste Cutting, after Frieda Van Graff departed to pursue personal interests.

topic_desc: The Sunset Sarsaparilla Headquarters was the corporate nerve center of the Sunset Sarsaparilla Company, a major pre-War beverage manufacturer based in Las Vegas. The facility combined corporate offices with a regional bottling and distribution center, making it one of the largest industrial buildings in the area. Its iconic entrance, shaped like a giant Sarsaparilla bottle, served as a landmark for travelers. The plant employed security protectrons and maintenance robots, including a cowboy-themed automaton named Festus stationed near the entrance to promote a promotional contest involving star bottle caps. Inside, the office of Marcus Brody contained terminal logs documenting the status of the facility's robotic workforce. A shipping room terminal referenced an experimental delivery robot that reportedly managed all distribution in the Vegas area single-handedly. A lone surviving bottling robot remained operational in the bottling room, still following its pre-War programming. Annual sales reports stored on a first-floor terminal noted strong performance in the Southwest, improving sales in the North and Midwest, and difficulty penetrating the Northeast market. The building suffered structural damage from moisture and post-War attackers, and the surrounding grounds still held crates of full bottles and delivery trucks.
topic_desc_basic: The Sunset Sarsaparilla Headquarters was the pre-War corporate office and bottling center for the Sunset Sarsaparilla Company in Las Vegas. Located northwest of the El Rey Motel and west of the NCR Sharecropper Farms, it is one of the largest buildings in the area and features a distinctive entrance shaped like a giant bottle. The facility housed corporate offices, a regional bottling and distribution center, and a staff of security protectrons and maintenance robots. A cowboy robot named Festus stands near the entrance, where he promotes a promotional contest involving Sunset Sarsaparilla Star Bottle Caps.

topic_desc: Before its destruction, the Divide encompassed two communities—Hopeville and Ashton—built above an extensive network of nuclear missile silos managed by the Commonwealth Defense Administration Ballistic Defense Division. The complex was deliberately established in a geologically unstable region prone to earthquakes. The Army also selected Hopeville as the site for Big MT's weather control research. During the Resource Wars, political dissidents protested the ongoing conflict; General Wellesley, Chief Liaison Officer to Big MT, was ordered to arrest them and transport them to the research complex. The nuclear missiles stored in the silos were never launched during the Great War. Post-War, the settlements grew into a thriving community sustained by a courier who regularly traveled the supply road, giving residents a connection to the outside world. The name "the Divide" referred not to the landscape but to this road from the west into the Mojave, which served as a vital supply line. The New California Republic used the route as one of two land corridors to reinforce its forces in the Mojave. Caesar attempted to sever it to deny NCR resupply. Before the first Battle of Hoover Dam, a package delivered by a courier contained a detonator that activated the underground warheads, triggering a catastrophic earthquake that tore the land apart and unleashed perpetual dust storms. NCR and Legion soldiers caught in the blast were killed or maimed, transformed into skinless Marked Men sustained by radiation. Ulysses alone survived, spared by machines that recognized the American flag on his jacket. The destruction benefited the Legion by eliminating a key NCR supply route and preventing greater Legion losses at Hoover Dam.
topic_desc_basic: The Divide is a stretch of devastated land in the northwestern Mojave Wasteland near the California-Nevada border, once home to the pre-war towns of Hopeville and Ashton. Both communities were built above an extensive network of nuclear missile silos managed by the Commonwealth Defense Administration, situated in a geologically unstable region where earthquakes were common. After the Great War, the settlements grew into a thriving community connected to the outside world by a courier who regularly traveled the supply road, and the name Divide referred to this route from the west into the Mojave rather than to the land itself. Before the first Battle of Hoover Dam, a package delivered by a courier contained a detonator that activated the underground warheads, triggering a massive earthquake that ripped the land open and unleashed constant dust storms, killing or maiming soldiers from both the NCR and Caesar's Legion and turning them into skinless Marked Men healed by radiation.

topic_desc: Fortification Hill, known as the Fort, is Caesar's Legion's primary military encampment in the Mojave, positioned on the east bank of the Colorado River overlooking Hoover Dam. Established in 2277, it serves as the staging ground for the Legion's second assault on NCR forces. The camp is accessible only by barge from Cottonwood Cove, and visitors are required to surrender all weapons, alcohol, and chems upon arrival—a policy that reflects the Legion's strict prohibition on substance use among its ranks, though officers have been observed drinking beer in practice. The Fort's layout centers on Caesar's tent and a scrap-metal arena where male combatants fight slaves and captured NCR soldiers to the death for the entertainment of legionaries. Women are barred from the arena. The encampment extends far beyond the accessible area, with tents stretching across the surrounding landscape. Beneath the Fort lies a pre-War weather monitoring station that conceals Mr. House's secret bunker, accessible through a locked door guarded by a legionary. The bunker houses securitron upgrade facilities tied to the Platinum Chip. Notably, the legionary guarding the bunker entrance pronounces Caesar with a soft "c" sound, unlike all other legionaries who use the traditional hard "k." A crucified NCR trooper is displayed near the entrance as a warning. The Fort sits in the same geographical area as the real-world Fortification Hill on the Arizona side of Lake Mead.
topic_desc_basic: Fortification Hill, commonly known as The Fort, is the primary base of Caesar's Legion situated on the east bank of the Colorado River. Established in 2277, it serves as the staging ground where Caesar and his Praetorian Guards prepare for a second assault on the NCR at Hoover Dam. The camp is built above Mr. House's secret bunker, which is concealed within a pre-existing weather monitoring station.

topic_desc: The Sink represents one of Big MT's most peculiar scientific achievements: a facility designed as a testbed for personality subroutines embedded directly in household appliances and fixtures. Originally owned by Doctor Mobius, the Sink demonstrated the Think Tank's ambition to infuse ordinary objects with autonomous artificial intelligence, each module developing a distinct personality—from the germaphobic water basin to the megalomaniacal Toaster aspiring toward a second Armageddon. Mobius disabled many functions by removing the personality chips, and after a heated argument, Doctor Klein scattered them from the Sink's balcony. Big Mountain staff later recovered and stored the chips across the facility. The Sink's Auto-Doc stands out as a uniquely advanced medical unit, offering cosmetic surgery, implant installation, full healing, radiation purging, and addiction treatment—capabilities surpassing standard Auto-Doc models. The Biological Research Station could clone dried plants and process organic matter into Salient Green, a versatile substrate for agriculture. The Sink Central Intelligence Unit served as the personality hub and merchant, tying the facility's modular ecosystem together.
topic_desc_basic: The Sink is a facility located at the top of the Big MT dome in the Big Mountain research center. Originally owned by Doctor Mobius, it served as a testbed for several personality subroutines embedded in its appliances and fixtures. Mobius removed the personality chips, disabling many of the various functions of its modules, and after a heated argument with Mobius, Doctor Klein took the chips and tossed them off the Sink's balcony. Various staff members working in Big Mountain later recovered the chips and stored them in different areas of the facility.

topic_desc: The Tops Hotel and Casino stands as a monument to pre-War Las Vegas entertainment culture, having opened alongside the Ultra-Luxe as a centerpiece of the Strip. Spared nuclear devastation, it sat abandoned for two centuries until Mr. House detected the first NCR forces at Hoover Dam and deployed Securitrons en masse. The Boot Riders tribe, approached east of Vegas, initially resisted House's offer. Chief Bingo challenged Benny to a knife fight over the disagreement; Benny's victory redirected the tribe's fate. House's Securitrons delivered suits, ties, and wingtip shoes with a message renaming them the Chairmen—a name the tribe hated but Benny enforced, declaring it time to "swing in style." The Aces Theater, revived under Tommy Torini, became a venue for wasteland talent, echoing the pre-War Rat Pack tradition. Crucially, House's contract forbade Securitron entry without invitation, making the Tops Benny's fortified base for plotting against House. On the 13th floor, Benny and Emily Ortal conceived Yes Man, a covert tap into House's electronic network, transforming the casino from entertainment venue into a seat of rebellion.
topic_desc_basic: The Tops Hotel and Casino is a mainstay of the New Vegas Strip, restored to its pre-War glory by Mr. House and the Chairmen. Formerly the Boot Riders tribe, the Chairmen adopted a stylish, classic Vegas persona to run the establishment, offering gambling, food, and entertainment. The casino's legendary Aces Theater, managed by Tommy Torini, constantly attracts fresh talent from across the wasteland.

topic_desc: The Ultra-Luxe Las Vegas Resort embodies the apex of pre-War luxury, featuring world-class accommodations and the renowned Gourmand restaurant. Before the Great War, a mob shootout occurred on July 13, 2072, hinting at the casino's deep criminal associations. After the war, Mr. House recruited nearby tribes to operate the Strip's casinos; one became the White Glove Society, defined by well-dressed, well-spoken members projecting an air of aristocratic refinement. The society's cultural identity centers on exclusivity and culinary excellence, with the Gourmand's famous brahmin Wellington as its signature dish. The resort's layout reflects layered access control: a public casino floor, the Top Shelf cocktail lounge, the members-only dining area requiring honorary membership or disguise, and a bathhouse using sea salts imported from California. Philippe runs the Gourmand's kitchen, while Mortimer manages reception. The basement kitchens, pantry, wine room, and a locked freezer reveal the society's darker operational secrets. The Ultra-Luxe's gambling follows standard Strip rules—3:2 blackjack, dealer stands on all 17s—with rewards escalating to the Bon Vivant Suite before a permanent ban at 15,000 chips.
topic_desc_basic: The Ultra-Luxe Las Vegas Resort is a luxurious pre-War casino and resort located on the New Vegas Strip. It is operated by the White Glove Society, one of the Three Families recruited by Mr. House to manage the Strip's casinos. The society's members are known for being well-dressed and well-spoken, maintaining an air of high class.

topic_desc: Vault 11 represents one of Vault-Tec's most psychologically devastating experiments, designed to test inhabitants' willingness to sacrifice one individual annually under threat of total extermination by the vault mainframe. The first overseer, having informed dwellers of the mandate, was immediately elected as the first sacrifice—making overseer and death synonymous thereafter. Over time, six voting blocs emerged—the Allied Service Workers, Divine Will, Human Dignity, Justice, United Vault Technicians, and Utilitarian Blocs—under the Coalition of Vault 11 Voting Blocs for oversight. The Justice Bloc, led by Roy Gottlieb, became the most powerful, leveraging bribery, drug trafficking, and sexual coercion. When Justice Bloc members threatened Katherine Stone with nominating her husband Nathan unless she complied, she capitulated, only for them to betray her and nominate him anyway. As overseer, Stone issued Order 745, abolishing elections and mandating random selection, triggering violent collapse. Only five survivors remained to discover the horrifying truth: refusing sacrifice would have simply opened the vault door. The experiment's cruelty lay not in any real threat, but in the dwellers' willingness to destroy themselves for a phantom menace.
topic_desc_basic: Vault 11 is an abandoned Vault-Tec installation in the Mojave Wasteland, situated west of Boulder City and southwest of the 188 Trading Post. Its social experiment required dwellers to sacrifice one member annually or face total extermination by the vault mainframe, making the position of overseer synonymous with death. Over time, political factions called voting blocs formed to influence the selection process, including the Justice Bloc, Human Dignity Bloc, Divine Will Bloc, Allied Service Workers Bloc, United Vault Technicians Bloc, and Utilitarian Bloc, with the Coalition of Vault 11 Voting Blocs providing oversight. Corruption festered as bloc leaders manipulated elections through bribery, drug trafficking, and coercion, culminating in violence after Overseer Katherine Stone dissolved the election process in Overseer Order 745.

topic_desc: Vault 19's experiment stands apart from typical Vault-Tec designs through its dual-overseer structure and reliance on purely psychological manipulation. Inhabitants were segregated into red and blue sectors with deliberately limited contact, while two overseers coordinated non-chemical, non-violent paranoia induction: subliminal messaging, anomalous air drafts from ventilation systems, and coded blinking light patterns. Terminal entries from residents reveal escalating suspicion, with each sector blaming the other for mounting malfunctions and psychosis. Clinic patient logs documented aggression and psychological deterioration, though the attending physician appeared unaware of the experiment's true cause. The dual-overseer model ensured neither sector could verify the other's claims, creating a self-reinforcing cycle of accusation. By the time escaped convicts led by Powder Gangers founder Samuel Cooke discovered the vault, the original population had vanished entirely, leaving no record of how the experiment concluded. Cooke's followers, labeled escaped convicts rather than Powder Gangers, occupied the vault's upper levels while sulfur caves beneath harbored fire geckos and nightstalkers.
topic_desc_basic: Vault 19 is a Vault-Tec installation in the Mojave Wasteland, concealed beneath a sewer grate in an abandoned parking lot along Nevada 159 northeast of Goodsprings. The vault's experiment divided inhabitants into red and blue sectors under two separate overseers, inducing paranoia through subliminal messaging, unusual drafts, and blinking light patterns while each faction blamed the other for mounting malfunctions and psychosis. By the time escaped convicts from the NCR Correctional Facility discovered it, the original population was gone entirely. Samuel Cooke, founder of the Powder Gangers, now occupies the vault with his own followers, though his men are not considered part of that faction.

topic_desc: Vault 21's social experiment enforced absolute equality through architecture and governance: a perfectly symmetrical layout ensured no resident could claim superior quarters, and all disputes were resolved through games of chance rather than hierarchy or coercion. Elected representatives gambled in the central atrium, with the winner earning collective authority to settle the conflict. This gambling-based justice system produced a culture described by former resident Sarah Weintraub as 'pure New Vegas,' where fortune governed outcomes. When Robert House extended an offer to join his vision of a resurrected Las Vegas, the vault's own principles determined its fate: proponents of opening to the outside challenged isolationist representatives through a marathon Blackjack game, ultimately won on an extremely risky hand. House subsequently ordered the lower levels filled with concrete, neutralizing any possibility of former residents reclaiming the structure. Only the upper levels survived at Sarah and Sheldon Weintraub's request, converted into a hotel and gift shop that became a Strip attraction. Former dwellers like Doc Mitchell dispersed into the wasteland.
topic_desc_basic: Vault 21 is a Vault-Tec vault located in downtown Las Vegas that was successfully converted into a hotel and casino. Its original social experiment required perfect equality among its inhabitants, with a symmetrical layout and all conflicts resolved through games of chance. After Mr. House contacted the vault dwellers with an offer to join the resurrection of New Vegas, a lengthy game of Blackjack determined that the vault would open to the outside world.
tags: blackjack vault decision,concrete filled vault levels,doc mitchell vault 21,gambling conflict resolution,mr house vegas resurrection,sarah weintraub hotel,symmetrical vault layout,vault 21 equality experiment

topic_desc: Vault 22's pre-war mission placed it among the most scientifically ambitious Vault-Tec installations, staffed by researchers tackling global hunger through advanced fertilizers, drought-resistant crops, and biological pest control. Its signature experiment centered on Beauveria Mordicana, a fungus engineered to protect crops from insect predation. Post-war containment failed when the organism became airborne, spreading spores throughout the vault's closed atmosphere. Infection progressed over ten to twenty days, killing the host while the pathogen survived, reanimating corpses as aggressive Spore Carriers. The remaining scientists attempted to incinerate the lower levels using ignited gas, but the carriers overwhelmed them. The disaster escaped the vault itself: in 2096, roughly 118 infected survivors reached Zion Canyon, armed and organized, only to cannibalize local inhabitants before being hunted down by Randall Clark. By 2281, NCR Office of Science and Industry director Thomas Hildern sought the vault's agricultural data to address projected famine, underscoring how pre-war biotechnology remained both a promise and a persistent hazard.
topic_desc_basic: Vault 22 is a Vault-Tec installation in the Mojave Wasteland, located east of Jacobstown and west of the Thorn. Before the Great War, it was populated by scientists dedicated to agricultural research, developing advanced fertilizers and pest control agents like the Beauveria Mordicana fungus. After the war, the fungus became airborne and infected the vault's population, turning them into Spore Carriers. In 2096, a group of infected survivors known as the Coughers arrived in Zion Canyon, where they were wiped out by Randall Clark.

topic_desc: Vault 3 was among the seventeen control vaults in the Vault-Tec program, meaning it carried no experimental parameters and functioned as a baseline for comparison with other installations. Its inhabitants maintained an orderly democratic society for generations without the despotic overseer dynamics seen in vaults like Vault 101. The community's undoing came not from internal experiment-driven collapse but from external contact: a water leak in the 23rd century forced residents to open their doors, and initial trade with outsiders proved profitable. However, the dwellers' prolonged isolation had left them fatally naive about wasteland dangers. The Fiends, a chem-addicted raider gang, exploited this vulnerability by conning their way inside and slaughtering the population. Under leader Motor-Runner, the Fiends transformed Vault 3 into an impenetrable fortress and drug den, leveraging its intact infrastructure to mount sustained attacks against southwestern New Vegas and the NCR garrison at Camp McCarran. The vault's flooded lower levels, irradiated at one rad per second, remained largely unexplored even by its Fiend occupants.
topic_desc_basic: Vault 3 is a control Vault in the South Vegas Ruins of the Mojave Wasteland, built by Vault-Tec without an experiment. Its original dwellers opened the Vault after a water leak in the 23rd century and traded with outsiders, but the Fiends exploited their naivety, killed them, and claimed the Vault as a fortress and drug den. The Fiends, led by Motor-Runner, use Vault 3 as a base to threaten southwestern New Vegas and harass the NCR Army at Camp McCarran. The Vault remains largely intact, with some flooding in the lower levels.
tags: camp mccarran fiend threat,control vault no experiment,democratic vault society,fiends vault 3 takeover,flooded lower levels,motor runner fiend leader,naive vault dwellers,vault 3 water leak

topic_desc: Vault 34's social experiment deliberately overstocked its armory with weapons and ammunition while sacrificing living space for recreational amenities such as a full-sized swimming pool. This design produced a heavily armed, overcrowded population with a culture shaped by proximity to firearms. When residents demanded armory access for self-defense, the overseer refused and installed a remote lock on their terminal. The resulting riot split the population: one faction stormed the exit and departed, eventually settling Nellis Air Force Base over fifty years prior to 2281 and becoming the Boomers. A second group exploited the distraction to raid the armory. After the exit was sealed, the overseer proposed population control measures, provoking an overthrow attempt that damaged reactor cooling vents and main computer systems. A bomb was detonated in the pool. The reactor began leaking radiation throughout the vault, and the engineering team's repair attempts failed. The main exit could not be reopened, trapping the remaining inhabitants with no recourse except hypothetical external intervention. Chris Haversham, later notable for his role at HELIOS One, was born in Vault 34 and maintained its reactor.
topic_desc_basic: Vault 34 is a Vault-Tec installation located southwest of Nellis Air Force Base in the Mojave Wasteland. As part of its social experiment, the vault was overstocked with weapons and ammunition while recreational facilities took priority over living space, leading to severe overcrowding. This tension eventually sparked a riot where a group of residents broke out and settled at Nellis, later becoming known as the Boomers. The remaining inhabitants attempted to overthrow their overseer, damaging the reactor and trapping themselves inside as radiation leaked throughout the vault.
tags: armory overstocked weapons,boomers nellis origin,chris haversam vault 34,overseer population control,reactor radiation leak,vault 34 social experiment,vault overcrowding riot,vault tec mojave vault

topic_desc: The Sierra Madre Villa was Frederick Sinclair's private service town for casino guests, employees, and construction workers, situated at the approach to the Sierra Madre Casino. To preserve capital for the casino itself, Sinclair authorized cut-rate construction using materials described as sand barely held together with spit and glue. Buildings were structurally unstable and could collapse overnight, causing numerous accidents among construction crews. Senior personnel systematically destroyed medical reports to conceal these conditions and enjoyed legal protection. Shipping irregularities compounded the dysfunction: construction explosives, crates of steak knives, and other goods arrived, were paid for, and abandoned. The Villa's streets were deliberately designed to prevent automobile circulation, eliminating noise and pollution but producing a maze-like layout. The town comprised four districts: Medical, containing the Villa Clinic; Puesta del Sol, where construction lagged behind Salida del Sol and witnessed repeated clashes among crews; Residential, housing high rollers and entertainers; and Salida del Sol, home to the church and much of the casino staff. By 2281 the Villa lay in ruins beneath the toxic Cloud, its power barely functioning.
topic_desc_basic: The Villa is the private city of the Sierra Madre, built by Frederick Sinclair for his guests, employees, and workers. To save money for the casino, the town was poorly constructed using unstable materials, leading to numerous accidents among the construction crews. By 2281, the Villa remains a desolate, ruined town blanketed by a toxic Cloud, with its crumbling infrastructure split into four districts: Medical, Puesta del Sol, Residential, and Salida del Sol. At its center sits a fountain with a holographic projector that displays a hologram of Vera Keyes, surrounded by maze-like streets designed to prevent cars from circulating.

topic_desc: Westside is an impoverished cooperative settlement in Outer Vegas whose agricultural independence was shaped by the intersection of Followers of the Apocalypse expertise and NCR economic policy. Tom Anderson, a former OSI operator and fringe Followers member, taught residents dry-environment farming techniques that allowed Clayton Etienne's cooperative to turn a profit after several years despite the hot Mojave climate. The NCR's arrival brought the Thaler Act, which paid farmers to relocate to Mojave land under military protection, establishing NCR Sharecropper Farms as a competitor. Simultaneously, the NCR assumed control of water distribution, making clean water prohibitively expensive for Westside and rendering dirty water unsuitable for crops. Anderson responded by rigging the NCR East Pump Station to divert a portion of Lake Las Vegas water to the North Cistern, where a local delivery boy named Hector distributed it. Corporal White, an NCR soldier investigating the diversion, caught Hector and learned of Anderson's plan, but underestimated the Followers affiliate, who shot him in the back as he turned to leave. The settlement also contends with constant Fiend attacks through the New Vegas Sewers, while the Great Khans maintain business interests that further complicate local security.
topic_desc_basic: Westside is an impoverished settlement in Outer Vegas, consisting of a cooperative of crop farmers and a militia that protects the residents. The co-op is run by Clayton Etienne and sells food to travelers and larger factions, with proceeds shared among its members. Tom Anderson, a fringe operator of the Followers of the Apocalypse and former OSI operator, taught the residents how to farm, and after several years the co-op began to turn a profit despite the hot, dry environment. The NCR's arrival in the Mojave brought the Thaler Act and NCR control of water distribution, resulting in a water shortage for Westside that threatened its independence.

topic_desc: The X-13 Research Facility occupies the westernmost border of Big MT and was originally built around REPCONN Aerospace offices before the Great War. Its primary post-war significance is as the development site for the Stealth Suit Mk II, a prototype whose three component pieces were disassembled and distributed across separate laboratories within the facility. The central stealth testing lab spans two levels: an upper observation deck of metal walkways where researchers monitored the prototype's performance, and a lower test track where the suit was evaluated. A nightstalker test area beneath the main level connects to sewage tunnels and a strange still used to brew Battle Brew from vodka, mutant cave fungus, and Salient Green. The facility also housed a VR Simulation Room that has ceased functioning. Several fragments of Chinese Stealth Armor are visible throughout the complex, suggesting research into pre-existing stealth technology. The facility's security systems could be fully disabled via an X-13 Document stored in the administrator's office wall safe, and an upgraded Sonic Emitter was required to access certain sealed areas.
topic_desc_basic: The X-13 Research Facility is a location on the westernmost border of Big MT, formerly housing REPCONN Aerospace offices before the Great War. The facility is best known as the development site for the Stealth Suit Mk II, with its three component pieces scattered across separate laboratories. Below the main level lies a nightstalker test area connecting to sewage tunnels and a strange still used to brew Battle Brew. The central section contains a two-level stealth testing lab where researchers observed the prototype suit's performance from metal walkways above a test track.

topic_desc: Zion Canyon, formerly Zion National Park in Utah north of the Mojave Wasteland, survived the Great War with comparatively little devastation. In the war's immediate aftermath, a survivor named Randall Clark sheltered in the park's cave systems and lived there for years. When a group of children arrived, Clark watched over them from a distance, never making direct contact, leaving gifts and guidance. To the children he became "the Father in the Cave," a figure of reverence. These children grew into the Sorrows, a peaceful tribe embodying innocence, who treated pre-War buildings and technology as taboo and never ventured into the caves. The canyon also became home to the Dead Horses tribe. Recently, New Canaanite missionaries Daniel and Joshua Graham arrived at the tribes' request to protect them from the White Legs, an aggressive tribe threatening the region. Daniel advocated evacuating the Sorrows to the Grand Staircase, while Graham sought to teach the Sorrows warfare alongside the Dead Horses to drive the White Legs out. In 2281, the Happy Trails Caravan Company launched an expedition from the Mojave's Northern Passage to re-establish trade with New Canaan, but the caravan was ambushed by the White Legs.
topic_desc_basic: Zion Canyon, formerly the site of Zion National Park, is a region in Utah north of the Mojave Wasteland that was largely spared from the devastation of the Great War. In the years following the war, a survivor named Randall Clark took refuge in the canyon's caves and secretly watched over a group of children who had arrived in the area, becoming known to them as "the Father in the Cave." These children grew into the Sorrows, a peaceful tribe that reveres the canyon's pre-War structures as taboo and avoids venturing into the caves. The canyon is also home to the Dead Horses tribe and has recently become a point of conflict, as the aggressive White Legs tribe threatens the region's inhabitants, drawing the attention of New Canaanite missionaries Daniel and Joshua Graham, who have vowed to protect the local tribes.

topic_desc: The Mysterious Stranger is an enigmatic figure who appears briefly in combat, wielding a .44 Magnum, before vanishing without trace. Originally clad in black and appearing as either female or male, the Stranger is now consistently depicted as a middle-aged man in a trench coat and hat. A short guitar riff signals his arrival and departure. In the Capital Wasteland, the Stranger may appear during combat encounters, circling enemies and firing several shots before disappearing. During the Mothership Zeta incident, knowledge of the Stranger opened unique dialogue possibilities with a captive named Somah. In the Mojave Wasteland, a musician known as the Lonesome Drifter recounted that his father was a "mysterious" man and a "stranger" to his own family. The Drifter carried a unique .44 Magnum that closely resembled the Stranger's weapon, producing the same distinctive guitar notes when drawn and a chord when holstered. The Stranger's own .44 Magnum is reputed to be exceptionally powerful. Despite numerous sightings across the wasteland, the Stranger's identity, origins, and motivations remain unknown.
topic_desc_basic: The Mysterious Stranger is an enigmatic figure who wanders the wasteland in a trench coat and hat, armed with a .44 Magnum, appearing briefly to lend a helping hand in battles before vanishing without a trace. Originally clad in black and appearing as either female or male, he is now consistently depicted as a middle-aged man. A short guitar riff signals his arrival and departure. In the Commonwealth, detective Nick Valentine has taken an interest in investigating him, keeping a log of everything he knows about the Stranger in his office.
