topic_desc: Colonel James Hsu occupies a pivotal but politically constrained role within the NCR's Mojade operations. As commander of Camp McCarran and the New Vegas garrison, he is the nexus of the NCR Army's military efforts in the region, yet his diplomatic temperament places him at odds with the Kimball administration's war hawks. Unlike Colonel Cassandra Moore and General Lee Oliver, Hsu favors negotiation and is sympathetic to locals, overseeing water and power distribution in Freeside and dealing diplomatically with groups such as the Kings. His high competence and modesty have made him well-liked by troops; Craig Boone remarks that without Oliver's interference Hsu would already be a general. Oliver reportedly sees him as an up-and-coming rival. Hsu previously served seven years alongside Nathan, the future warden of the NCR Correctional Facility, who once helped him in Modoc. Nathan attempted to call in that favor to secure new guards for NCRCF but was killed in the prison break before he could. Despite holding the same rank as Colonel Moore, Hsu possesses greater authority as overall commander of NCR Army operations in the Mojave Desert.
topic_desc_basic: Colonel James Hsu is the commanding officer of the New California Republic Army garrison at Camp McCarran and oversees most NCR military operations in the Mojave Wasteland. A level-headed and competent officer, he is known for favoring diplomacy over force of arms, caring deeply for the soldiers under his command, and being sympathetic to local populations, including his management of water and power distribution in Freeside. His modesty and competence have made him well-liked by his troops, though this has drawn the ire of General Lee Oliver, who views him as a potential rival. Hsu previously served alongside Nathan, the future warden of the NCR Correctional Facility, for seven years and still owed him a favor from an incident in Modoc.
tags: camp mccarran,freeside diplomacy,general oliver rival,mojave command,ncr colonel
editorial_note: Hsu's post-Second Battle of Hoover Dam promotion outcome is referenced in cut/unused dialogue; treat as uncertain rather than confirmed.

topic_desc: Corporal Betsy's situation illustrates the psychological toll of the NCR's protracted conflict with the Fiends on the western flank of the Mojave. As a sniper in First Recon's Alpha Team, she has spent six months manning Camp McCarran's towers under Lieutenant Gorobets, head-shotting Fiends on drugs. Her partnership with 10 of Spades is defined by mutual loyalty: she volunteered when no one else would, and she discreetly lets him wear corrective lenses disguised as "training shades" to mask his poor eyesight. The sexual assault by Cook-Cook left her with anger and behavioral issues; 10 of Spades was knocked unconscious during the attack and blames himself. Gorobets recognizes her behavior is inappropriate but prefers treatment over punishment, noting Betsy may not want to look bad before the rest of First Recon. She initially refuses to acknowledge the trauma's impact. Doctor Usanagi is identified as well-qualified to treat mental trauma and agrees to clear her schedule to assist. Betsy is a lesbian and will flirt with a female Courier of sufficient Charisma. After the Driver Nephi bounty, Alpha Team relocates to Camp Forlorn Hope to assist against the Legion at Nelson.
topic_desc_basic: Corporal Betsy is a sniper serving in Alpha Team of the New California Republic Army's First Recon, stationed at Camp McCarran under Lieutenant Gorobets. She works in a sniper pair with 10 of Spades, having volunteered to partner with him when no one else would due to his lack of experience, and she allows him to wear eyeglasses she calls his training shades to cover for his poor eyesight. Betsy struggles with anger and behavioral issues stemming from trauma after being sexually assaulted by the Fiend leader Cook-Cook, an incident that left her partner knocked unconscious and blaming himself. Her commanding officer recognizes her behavior is inappropriate but would prefer she seek treatment rather than face punishment, though Betsy is initially reluctant to acknowledge the experience has affected her or that seeing a doctor would help.
tags: camp mccarran,cook-cook assault,first recon sniper,ten of spades partner,trauma treatment
editorial_note: Betsy's recovery depends on player actions; do not assert a fixed outcome. Her relocation to Camp Forlorn Hope follows specific quest progress.

topic_desc: Corporal Sterling embodies the transition from NCR Ranger to Army trooper forced by the brutal realities of the Mojave frontier. In 2273 he was among the first Rangers sent east to scout the Mojave, walking the ground between Shady Sands and the Colorado and learning about local tribes to pave the way for the Mojave Campaign. His capture by Legionaries near Malpais ended his Ranger career: they smashed bones in his hands and feet but failed to tie him, allowing him to crawl to a cliff and tumble into the Colorado, where fellow Rangers rescued him from drowning. The lasting damage prevented proper sidearm control and long-range patrols, which would have warranted a medical discharge. Instead, Sterling demonstrated his marksmanship and was accepted into the Army alongside raw recruits. Lieutenant Gorobets transferred him to First Recon to keep him as an asset. Sterling continued using his old lever-action La Longue Carabine rather than the hunting rifles standard to First Recon, and wore a Ranger Hat instead of a 1st Recon Beret, making him the only Alpha Team member with a lever-action weapon and the only active First Recon member using a scoped rifle.
topic_desc_basic: Corporal Sterling is a member of NCR First Recon's Alpha Team stationed at Camp McCarran and is one of the outfit's oldest members. Formerly an NCR Ranger, he was among the first to scout the Mojave Wasteland in 2273, walking vast stretches of territory between Shady Sands and the Colorado River and learning about local tribes to pave the way for the Mojave Campaign. His Ranger career ended after Legionaries captured him near Malpais and smashed the bones in his hands and feet, though he escaped by crawling to a cliff and tumbling into the Colorado, where fellow Rangers rescued him from drowning. Although the lasting damage prevented him from handling a sidearm or conducting long-range patrols, Sterling's persistence and marksmanship earned him a place in the Army, and Lieutenant Gorobets transferred him to First Recon.
tags: first recon,former ncr ranger,la longue carabine,legion captivity,malpais capture,mojave scouting
editorial_note: Sterling's scouting began in 2273; his First Recon service is contemporary to 2281. Avoid asserting quest-dependent relocation outcomes.

topic_desc: Camp McCarran, the NCR's primary military hub in the Mojave Wasteland, depends on Corporal William Farber to sustain its garrison through daily meal service. The logistical strain of feeding an army in occupied territory is evident in Farber's predicament: without reliable access to meat or spices, his menus are reduced to whatever vegetables can be sourced, a situation that erodes both trooper morale and digestive health. Compounding the crisis, the base's food processor—a critical piece of pre-War kitchen technology—has broken down and requires replacement parts that are not readily available. Farber's vulnerability to corruption is illustrated by his encounter with a fraudulent NCR health inspector, from whom he paid a fifty-cap bribe. Separately, the researcher Keely, operating inside the overgrown ruins of Vault 22, has theorized that a biological sample derived from the vault's mutated spore plants could hold relevance for Farber's culinary challenges, suggesting a potential link between the vault's agricultural experiments and the NCR's food supply problems.
topic_desc_basic: Corporal William Farber serves as a mess officer for the NCR Army at Camp McCarran, where he is responsible for cooking, preparing, and serving meals to the troopers stationed there. His ability to produce quality food is hampered by a lack of meat and spices, leaving him limited to vegetables such as corn, beans, and onions, which affects both morale and digestion among the soldiers. The base's food processor is also in need of repair and replacement parts, further complicating his duties. Farber was once tricked by an NCR health inspector, from whom he bribed 50 caps, and the researcher Keely in Vault 22 suspects that a sample derived from the vault's spore plants might be of interest to him.
tags: camp mccarran food,food processor repair,keely research sample,ncr mess officer,vault 22 spore plants

topic_desc: Craig Boone's military career with the NCR First Recon Battalion placed him at the center of two defining events in the Mojave conflict. At the First Battle of Hoover Dam, he served on the front lines at Camp Golf as Legion forces hammered NCR positions. More traumatically, he participated in the Bitter Springs Massacre, where First Recon was ordered to seal Canyon 37 and shoot on sight. When the Great Khans fleeing down the pass turned out to be largely non-combatants—women, children, the sick, and elderly—NCR command, failing to grasp the situation, ordered the troopers to fire until ammunition was exhausted. Boone carried out the order, an experience that poisoned his faith in military authority and drove him from the service at the end of his tour. He married Carla, a woman he met on the New Vegas Strip, and settled in Novac alongside his spotter and best friend Manny Vargas. Carla's discontent with small-town life strained Boone's relationship with Vargas. When Legion slavers abducted the pregnant Carla—timing their raid to slip past Boone's watch—Boone suspected betrayal. He tracked her to a Legion outpost near the Colorado River but, finding the area swarming with legionaries and rescue impossible, chose to mercy kill her rather than let her endure slavery. This act cemented his hatred of Caesar's Legion and his determination to identify whoever had set him up.
topic_desc_basic: Craig Boone is a retired New California Republic First Recon sharpshooter who currently works as the night-shift town guard in Novac. During his military service, he fought in the First Battle of Hoover Dam and participated in the Bitter Springs Massacre, where he was ordered to fire on fleeing non-combatants. After leaving the army, he settled in Novac with his wife Carla and his former spotter Manny Vargas. Following Carla's kidnapping by Caesar's Legion, Boone tracked her to a Legion outpost and chose to mercy kill her rather than let her be enslaved, leaving him embittered and determined to find whoever was responsible for her abduction.
tags: bitter springs massacre,carla boone kidnapping,first battle hoover dam,mercy killing legion,ncr first recon sharpshooter,novac night guard

topic_desc: Daniel's missionary work among the Sorrows tribe reflects the complex intersection of New Canaanite faith and indigenous tribal spirituality in the post-War American West. Sent to Zion Canyon by Bishop Mordecai, Daniel initially focused on conversion, but the destruction of New Canaan—a Mormon settlement wiped out by the White Legs under pressure from Caesar's Legion—transformed his mission into one of protection and atonement. He carries guilt for what he perceives as the New Canaanites' role in drawing hostile attention to the Sorrows, having previously witnessed other tribes such as the Crazy Horns and Tar Walkers completely eradicated by slavers, raiders, and exploitative prospectors. Daniel's theological instruction inadvertently syncretized with Sorrows spiritual heritage: the tribe's Father in the Cave and the New Canaanite God became indistinguishable in their understanding. His strategy for the Sorrows' survival centers on evacuation to the Grand Staircase, driven by a conviction that armed resistance would corrupt the tribe's innocence and replicate the cycle of militarism that destroyed the old world, produced Joshua Graham as the Malpais Legate, and created figures like the warlord Salt-Upon-Wounds. Despite his pacifist convictions, Daniel remains willing to kill if the White Legs force his hand.
topic_desc_basic: Daniel is a New Canaanite missionary operating among the Sorrows tribe in Zion Canyon. Originally dispatched by Bishop Mordecai to spread the word of God, Daniel's mission shifted after he witnessed the destruction of New Canaan and the death of his bishop. He now dedicates himself to protecting the Sorrows from the White Legs, a hostile tribe responsible for attacking New Canaan, and fears that war would corrupt their innocent nature. Daniel's teachings blended New Canaanite theology with the Sorrows' existing spiritual beliefs, causing their Father in the Cave and the New Canaanite God to become one and the same.
tags: bishop mordecai death,father in the cave,new canaanite missionary,sorrows tribe zion,white legs conflict,zion canyon evacuation

topic_desc: Dean Domino's pre-War celebrity as the King of Swing masked a deep narcissism and vindictiveness that defined his trajectory from entertainer to would-be thief. Performing across the United States and Europe—including Paris and an ill-fated engagement in Madrid—Domino was invited to headline at the Sierra Madre, Frederick Sinclair's grand casino project. Sinclair's unwavering optimism despite severe financial losses in the 2070s provoked Domino's jealousy into obsession. He resolved to ruin Sinclair by looting the casino vault, enlisting his former lover, the starlet Vera Keyes—whom Sinclair had fallen for—by blackmailing her over a Med-X addiction, unaware she was terminally ill. The Great War transformed the Sierra Madre's Gala Event into a massacre as security holograms activated, trapping Domino inside. Over two centuries of ghoulification, he relentlessly mapped the casino's defenses, unaware that Sinclair had already discovered the plot and prepared a trap in the vault. Captured by Dog and collared by Father Elijah, Domino continued scheming, killing previous collared victims to study their explosive mechanisms. He also dragged an unconscious Christine Royce to the Villa clinic, programming an Auto-Doc to alter her vocal cords to mimic Vera Keyes's voice, intending to use her as a key to the vault. Remarkably, ghoulification left his singing voice clear and smooth, unlike the gravelly tones typical of other ghouls.
topic_desc_basic: Dean Domino, also known as the King of Swing, was a famous pre-War lounge singer who performed across the United States and Europe, including the Las Vegas Strip. He was invited to perform at the Sierra Madre casino, where he became consumed with jealousy toward the casino's founder, Frederick Sinclair, and plotted to break into the vault using his former lover Vera Keyes. When the bombs dropped, the Gala Event became a massacre and Dean was trapped in the Sierra Madre, undergoing ghoulification over the next two hundred years while obsessively mapping the casino's security system and plotting his grand heist. He was eventually captured by Dog, fitted with an explosive collar, and forced to work for Father Elijah.
tags: father elijah collar,frederick sinclair rivalry,ghoulified entertainer,pre-war lounge singer,sierra madre casino,vera keyes blackmail

topic_desc: Deputy Beagle earned his badge through family ties rather than merit, deputized by Sheriff McBain approximately two and a half months before escaped convicts overran Primm. Rather than confront the Powder Gangers directly, Beagle adopted a policy of observation, taking notes and audio logs of their activities. During one such surveillance session, he witnessed a meeting between Benny, Great Khans, and Powder Gangers discussing a delivery taken from a courier, with the group indicating they would travel through Nipton to Novac to meet a contact. Beagle was spotted and forced to flee. Shortly afterward, escaped convicts infiltrated Primm at night and murdered Sheriff McBain and Beagle's sister in their sleep. Beagle, hiding in the corner of the office, was captured and thrown into the kitchen as a hostage. Sergeant McGee, on scout duty, witnessed the event but declined to intervene, citing lack of a long rifle and proper orders. The Powder Gangers tortured Beagle, who could not resist and revealed what little he knew about the town. He remained their hostage for a ransom no one in Primm could pay. Primm's inhabitants do not take Beagle seriously, and he is widely considered a lazy coward who avoids proactive law enforcement and leaves tasks unfinished.
topic_desc_basic: Deputy Beagle is the deputy of Primm, deputized by Sheriff McBain roughly two and a half months before the convict attack on the town, largely on account of being the sheriff's wife's brother. He is widely regarded by Primm's inhabitants as lacking in common sense, intelligence, and general usefulness, a reputation he attempts to offset with a gentlemanly demeanor and sophisticated vocabulary that he frequently mispronounces. Beagle is also known as a lazy coward who avoids proactive law enforcement and leaves tasks half-finished, having earned his position through family ties rather than merit. During the convict takeover of Primm, Beagle was taken hostage after witnessing the murder of Sheriff McBain and his own sister, and was tortured into revealing what little he knew about the town before being held for a ransom that no one in Primm could afford to pay.
tags: benny great khans,bison steve hotel,convict hostage,law enforcement failure,powder ganger surveillance,primm deputy

topic_desc: Doc Mitchell was born and raised in Vault 21, the vault beneath the New Vegas Strip whose residents resolved disputes through games of chance. When Mr. House initiated the Strip renovations in 2274, he contacted Vault 21's residents with the prospect of participating in the city's resurgence. Most refused, but House's supporters challenged the dissenters to a game of Blackjack, winning in what Mitchell described as an extremely risky and fateful gambit. The vault was opened, stripped, and filled with concrete, leaving only part of the top level untouched. Mitchell was among the residents forced into homelessness. He became a traveling doctor, noting that most people in the wasteland lacked education, making his medical skillset rare. He eventually returned to Vault 21 to marry his childhood sweetheart, and the two planned to travel to California. They only reached Goodsprings before his wife fell ill from germ infection caused by years of isolation in the vault. After her death, Mitchell remained in Goodsprings to stay close to her. He later developed a bum leg. In 2281, after a courier was shot in the head and buried in Goodsprings Cemetery, the robot Victor recovered the body and brought it to Mitchell, who removed most of the lead shrapnel from the courier's brain and nursed them back to health over several days.
topic_desc_basic: Doc Mitchell is a surgeon and doctor living in Goodsprings. He grew up in Vault 21 beneath the New Vegas Strip, where younger residents gave him the nickname mole-butt. When Mr. House opened and filled Vault 21 with concrete during the Strip renovations beginning in 2274, Mitchell was forced into homelessness and worked as a traveling doctor, finding his medical expertise rare and valuable in the wasteland.
tags: courier rescue,goodsprings doctor,mr house renovations,new vegas strip,vault 21 resident,wasteland surgeon

topic_desc: Doctor Henry is a former Enclave scientist specializing in human and canine neuroscience, as well as canine cyber-genetics. During his tenure with the Enclave, he developed a mutagenic serum intended to cure super mutants, opposing the Enclave's initiative to simply kill the afflicted. His theories on correcting mutations in the wasteland were unpopular with other Enclave scientists. Henry departed the Enclave before the destruction of the oil rig, a decision he later described as the right one. He integrated into the New California Republic, setting up a clinic in NCR town. While there, he spoke about the Enclave at length while drunk, and his research attracted the attention of Merk, a local crime lord who sought to steal Henry's blueprints for cybernetic canine guard units. Henry later spent time traveling with caravans, where he met Gibson, before relocating to the Mojave Wasteland to join other Enclave Remnants fleeing persecution by the NCR and Brotherhood of Steel. He settled in Jacobstown, establishing a lab in the lodge to research the effects of prolonged Stealth Boy Mark II Prototype usage by Nightkin, with the primary objective of curing their schizophrenia. He noted that his Jacobstown lab was not as impressive as the facilities he had access to with the Enclave. He is also capable of performing brain transplants for cyberdogs, though he had not worked in that field recently.
topic_desc_basic: Doctor Henry is a physician and former Enclave scientist who eventually settled in Jacobstown within the Mojave Wasteland alongside other Enclave Remnants. During his time with the Enclave, he specialized in human and canine neuroscience and worked on canine cyber-genetics, though he left the organization after disagreeing with their initiative to simply kill super mutants instead of curing them. After departing before the destruction of the Enclave oil rig, he spent time in the New California Republic and traveling with caravans before relocating to Jacobstown. There, he established a lab in the lodge to research the effects of prolonged Stealth Boy Mark II Prototype usage by Nightkin, aiming to cure their schizophrenia.
tags: canine cyber-genetics,enclave scientist,jacobstown lab,mutagenic serum,nightkin schizophrenia,stealth boy research

topic_desc: Doctor Klein is a pre-War scientist who served as the Chief Head Researcher of Logistical Operations and Idea-ology at Big MT, the pre-War research facility in the Big Empty. After the Great War, Klein became a Think Tank, a disembodied brain housed in a robotic chassis, allowing him to continue his work indefinitely alongside his colleagues. He functions as the leader of the Think Tank, exhibiting a stuffy, authoritative demeanor reminiscent of a college dean. Klein frequently refuses to confer with his colleagues on decisions, asserting unilateral authority over the group's direction. Despite his general hostility toward Doctor Mobius, a former colleague who departed the Think Tank under contentious circumstances, Klein retains some willingness to consider Mobius as a partner under specific conditions. Among the Think Tank members, Klein is notable as the only genuine threat, as he remains relatively sane and capable of acting with a level of authority that the other members lack. His colleagues include Doctors Dala, O, Borous, and 8, each housed in similar robotic chassis. The Think Tank's collective research at Big MT continued in isolation for over two centuries after the Great War, with Klein overseeing operations from his position as chief researcher.
topic_desc_basic: Doctor Klein is a pre-War scientist and the Chief Head Researcher of Logistical Operations and Idea-ology at Big MT. After the Great War, he became a Think Tank, a disembodied brain housed in a robotic chassis, to continue his work alongside his colleagues. He serves as the leader of the Think Tank, acting with a stuffy, authoritative demeanor reminiscent of a college dean, and often refuses to confer with his peers on decisions. Despite his general hostility toward Doctor Mobius, he retains some willingness to consider him a partner under certain circumstances.
tags: big empty facility,big mt researcher,doctor mobius rival,pre-war scientist,robotic brain chassis,think tank leader

topic_desc: Doctor Mobius was among the pre-war scientists of the Big MT research facility, one of the brightest minds assembled to push the boundaries of science without ethical restraint. After the Great War, he and his colleagues were converted into Think Tank brains—disembodied consciousnesses housed in robotic bodies, continuing their experiments in the irradiated wasteland. A bitter dispute with Doctor Klein led Mobius to remove the personality chips from the Sink, the facility's automated intelligences, and depart for the X-42 robo-warfare facility, which he renamed the Forbidden Zone. There he invented the Robo-Scorpions that patrol the surrounding wasteland and created most of the Sink's robotic intelligences, save Muggy, who was the work of Doctor 0. Mobius also programmed the Sink Central Intelligence Unit to accept bottle caps as currency, correctly predicting that caps would become the dominant post-war medium of exchange—a foresight that puzzled his colleagues. Despite his reputation as the Think Tank's antagonist, Mobius retains a wistful awareness of what his colleagues have forgotten: friendship, discovery, and love. His faculties have been eroded by prolonged chem use, particularly Psycho, and he struggles with memory and coherence, yet he remains one of the most powerful entities in the Big MT.
topic_desc_basic: Doctor Mobius is a Think Tank operating in the Big MT and the leader of the Robo-Scorpion army. He is the nemesis of Dr. Klein and the team to which he belonged. Mobius was part of the Big MT Think Tank before the Great War and became a think tank after the War to continue his work.
tags: big mt think tank,bottle cap prediction,doctor klein nemesis,forbidden zone x-42,old world blues,robo-scorpion inventor,sink personality chips
editorial_note: Chronology: Mobius was part of the pre-war Think Tank; post-war developments at Big MT are ongoing by 2281.

topic_desc: Dog's origins trace back to the Master's army at the Mariposa Military Base, where Nightkin served as elite stealth troopers under the Master and his Lieutenant. Dog was conditioned for absolute obedience, tasked with hunting, killing, and gathering humans for the Forced Evolutionary Virus vats. He recalls hiding at both Mariposa and the Cathedral, and harbors a nostalgic attachment to those places—particularly the memory of removing his Stealth Boy at nightfall and staring at the Cathedral ceiling. After the Master's fall, Dog wandered until the Sierra Madre Broadcast drew him to the casino. There, Father Elijah's commanding presence reopened the psychological conditioning the Master had instilled, making Elijah Dog's new master. God, the second identity, claims to have always existed but only began speaking when Elijah arrived. God describes himself as Dog's conscience and the voice of reason, struggling to restrain Dog's childlike destructive impulses. The two identities do not share all experiences, creating friction. God's control of the body is physically awkward—he lacks Dog's instinctive combat coordination. Dog self-harms by carving his name into his chest and clamping a bear trap on his arm, attempting to silence God's voice, which only enrages God further. Elijah exploited this fractured psyche, fitting Dog with an explosive collar and commanding him to gather victims for the Sierra Madre heist.
topic_desc_basic: Dog and God are two distinct identities sharing the body of a single Nightkin, a product of trauma-induced dissociative identity disorder. Dog, the childlike and perpetually hungry persona, served in the Master's army as a stealth trooper before following the Sierra Madre Broadcast to the Sierra Madre casino, where Father Elijah became his new master. God, the intelligent and controlling persona, acts as Dog's conscience, attempting to restrain his destructive instincts. The two identities take turns controlling their shared body, with the dormant one confined to a mental cage where they can hear but not witness outside events.
tags: dead money nightkin,dog childlike hunger,father elijah master,god conscience persona,master army stealth trooper,nightkin dissociative identity,sierra madre broadcast
editorial_note: Chronology: Dog served in the Master's army (circa 2155-2162); Sierra Madre events occur around 2281.

topic_desc: ED-E represents the pinnacle of the Enclave's duraframe eyebot program, a combat-oriented evolution of the standard eyebot platform. Under Dr. Whitley's direction, the project produced a unit with superior sensor arrays, armored vacuum tube protection, and a miniaturized Tesla cannon—features that distinguished it from the reconnaissance-focused standard models. The Enclave's decision to halt duraframe production in favor of Hellfire armor manufacturing and the systematic destruction of all remaining units made ED-E uniquely irreplaceable. Whitley, recognizing the unit's value, loaded it with Poseidon Energy research data and dispatched it toward Navarro, the Enclave's West Coast stronghold. The eyebot's journey took it through Chicago, where an Enclave outpost provided repairs and upgrades, and where it briefly stayed with a civilian family—an encounter that humanized the machine in unexpected ways. Crossing the Mojave, a raider's hand-loaded .308 round disabled ED-E near Primm, where it was recovered by a Mojave Express courier and left on Johnson Nash's counter. The unit carries Enclave intelligence data of significant interest to multiple factions: the Brotherhood of Steel and the Followers of the Apocalypse both offered upgrades, reflecting the enduring value of pre-war Enclave technology. Arcade Gannon noted that ED-E's journey from Adams Air Force Base on the eastern seaboard to the Mojave covered over two thousand miles, a testament to the duraframe's durability.
topic_desc_basic: ED-E (Eyebot Duraframe Subject E, pronounced "Eddie" or "E-D-E") is a prototype duraframe eyebot manufactured by the Enclave for combat use, featuring enhancements over standard eyebots including additional sensor dishes, armor plating for side-mounted vacuum tubes, and a miniaturized Tesla cannon. When the Enclave halted duraframe production to focus on Hellfire armor and destroyed all remaining units, ED-E became the last surviving model. Dr. Whitley, the head researcher of the duraframe project, uploaded Poseidon Energy data and his research into ED-E's logs and dispatched it toward Navarro, but it stopped at an Enclave outpost in Chicago for repairs before crossing the Mojave Wasteland, where a raider sniper shot and damaged it.
tags: chicago enclave outpost,dr whitley research,enclave duraframe eyebot,mojave express primm,navarro dispatch,poseidon energy data,tesla cannon prototype
editorial_note: Chronology: ED-E's post-war journey and arrival in the Mojave occur in the lead-up to 2281.

topic_desc: Easy Pete embodies the archetype of the Mojave prospector—a scavenger who combed pre-war ruins for salvageable technology, weapons, chems, and components before age and danger drove him to settle. His aborted claim near the Colorado River illustrates the perilous frontier where prospectors risked Legion and raider violence for valuable finds. Goodsprings offered refuge from both the NCR's expansionist policies and the lawless periphery; Pete settled there explicitly to distance himself from NCR influence, yet he acknowledges the republic contains "a lot of decent folk" even as he criticizes its habit of absorbing settlements regardless of local consent. Pete's regional literacy is notable: he understands the strategic centrality of Hoover Dam, recognizing that whoever controls the Dam controls the territory through its power generation and access to Lake Mead's clean water. He correctly identifies the Legion as a slaver army led by Caesar, notes the NCR's failure to destroy the Legion at the First Battle of Hoover Dam, and observes Legion incursions on the Nevada side of the river. His willingness to share dynamite only with those versed in explosives reflects a prospector's practical caution. Notably, Pete pronounces Caesar with the classical Latin /ˈkaisar/, a distinction shared by very few outside the Legion itself.
topic_desc_basic: Easy Pete is a former prospector living in Goodsprings who earned his nickname by "taking it easy" and helping tend to the town's brahmin and bighorners. Before settling down, he scoured old buildings for tech, weapons, chems, and spare parts, and once found a promising claim near the Colorado River before raiders chased him off. He is experienced with dynamite, which he keeps buried for safekeeping, and refuses to share it with anyone who doesn't know explosives. Pete is knowledgeable about the broader regional conflict, describing Caesar's Legion as slavers led by Caesar and noting that the NCR beat them back at the First Battle of Hoover Dam but failed to finish the job.
tags: caesar legion slavers,colorado river claim,dynamite explosives expert,goodsprings prospector,hoover dam strategy,mojave scavenger lifestyle,ncr expansion criticism
editorial_note: Chronology: Pete's prospecting career predates his settlement in Goodsprings; his observations on regional conflict reflect the 2281 situation.

topic_desc: McNamara's rise to elder was unconventional: he was a head paladin who took command only because Father Elijah abandoned the chapter during the NCR's Operation Sunburst at HELIOS One. His breakout through NCR lines saved the Brotherhood from annihilation and cemented his authority, but the extended lockdown he imposed afterward has eroded that support. The bunker's isolation has caused attrition of the Brotherhood's sphere of influence, and Head Paladin Hardin now seeks to usurp him, representing a conservative faction that believes in traditional Brotherhood ideals without question. McNamara, by contrast, is described by Veronica as one of the Brotherhood's most progressive members and may even support the NCR under the right circumstances. His leadership also maintained an unusual neutrality with the Black Mountain super mutants, a policy established while the settlement was under the benevolent Marcus, though Tabitha's violent takeover has rendered that stance questionable. McNamara's fear of NCR pursuit is largely unfounded, as the Republic is overburdened on multiple fronts and not actively hunting the Brotherhood.
topic_desc_basic: Elder Nolan McNamara is the leader of the Mojave Chapter of the Brotherhood of Steel, operating from the Hidden Valley Bunker. He earned the respect and loyalty of his chapter by breaking through NCR lines at HELIOS One during the failed Operation Sunburst, leading surviving Brotherhood forces to safety. When Father Elijah vanished during that battle, McNamara assumed command and the rank of elder, credited with saving the Mojave chapter from complete eradication. Fearing continued NCR pursuit, he placed the Hidden Valley bunker on lockdown, restricting movement to small scouting parties and barring entry to outside members, though the NCR is actually overburdened on multiple fronts and not actively hunting the Brotherhood.

topic_desc: Emily Ortal's decision to work in the Mojave reflects a broader tension within NCR territory: the Office of Science and Industry and other Republic-aligned organizations fund research only when it has military applications, while inflation and taxation make life difficult for civilians. As a Followers of the Apocalypse physician, Ortal sought to do practical medical good outside that system. Her technical skills extend beyond medicine, however. She reprogrammed the Securitron known as Yes Man for Benny, modifying it to connect to Mr. House's network so that House could not remotely disable the unit. This act gave Benny a covert asset on the Strip. Ortal later sought to intercept data from Mr. House's network by providing the Courier with a packet sniffer, hoping to analyze his encrypted data feeds. Her proximity to the Lucky 38 and her involvement with both Benny and the Courier place her at the intersection of several major power struggles in the Mojave, though her primary motivation remains the Followers' humanitarian mission.
topic_desc_basic: Doctor Emily Ortal is a physician and member of the Followers of the Apocalypse who works in the Mojave Wasteland. She chose to operate there because neither the OSI nor other NCR-aligned organizations funded medical research unless it had military applications, and inflation and taxation in Republic territories further motivated her decision. She is responsible for reprogramming the Securitron known as Yes Man for Benny, modifying it to connect to the network so that Mr. House could not remotely disable it.

topic_desc: Fantastic's presence at HELIOS One is a study in institutional failure. The NCR, desperate for technical experts to operate the solar power plant, accepted his claim of a "theoretical degree in physics" without verification. Since then, Fantastic has spent months working on what he assumes is the most important console because it is the largest, when in fact it controls the intercom system. The plant runs at one percent efficiency, partly due to misaligned outside mirrors he has identified but not fixed. This dysfunction suits Ignacio Rivas, who is far more knowledgeable but deliberately keeps Fantastic and the NCR in the dark to protect the secret of ARCHIMEDES, the experimental weapon system hidden within the facility. Fantastic's opportunism extends beyond mere laziness: if the NCR is wiped out at HELIOS One, he switches allegiance to Caesar's Legion, donning legionary armor and remarking "when in Rome." Alternatively, if the NCR retains control, he receives a promotion at Hoover Dam, though chief engineer Mike Lawson ensures anything Fantastic attempts must be approved first. His drug addiction and self-serving nature make him a purely mercenary figure with no loyalty to any faction.
topic_desc_basic: Fantastic is an incompetent and egotistical con artist employed by the NCR as a technician at HELIOS One, having talked his way into the job by claiming to have a "theoretical degree in physics." Since arriving, he has done virtually nothing to repair the plant, instead convincing NCR personnel that he is essential so he can keep drawing pay to fuel his drug addiction. He works alongside Ignacio Rivas, who is far more knowledgeable but whom Fantastic ignores, and he has spent months working on what is actually the intercom console while the plant runs at one percent efficiency. Most NCR soldiers and Rivas have little respect for him, and anyone who spends time around him quickly sees through his fraud.

topic_desc: Elijah's trajectory from Brotherhood elder to isolated obsessive traces a path through the Mojave's most dangerous pre-War sites. After abandoning the Brotherhood at HELIOS One, he traveled to Big MT, where he was briefly captured by the Think Tank before escaping by overriding their containment systems. At the abandoned Little Yangtze prison facility, he experimented with explosive collars on surviving prisoners, refining their operating frequencies and isolating the Sierra Madre broadcast signal. He suffered neurological strain from excessive Mentats use during this period. After escaping Big MT by seizing control of the train network, he traveled to the Sierra Madre, where he envisioned a new society built on three pillars: the Cloud as population control, holograms for defense, and the Sierra Madre Vending Machines for provisioning food, medicine, ammunition, and currency. Unable to access the casino vault alone, he lured treasure seekers via broadcast and coerced them with explosive collars, modifying the system so that one death triggered all collars. His final plan involved scouring Hoover Dam with the Cloud and an army of holograms, reshaping the Mojave into a world "nothing like what happened at HELIOS One." He was mentioned by Ulysses, who directed him to the Sierra Madre, and left a final message for Veronica before entering the casino.
topic_desc_basic: Father Elijah is a former Elder of the Brotherhood of Steel, notable for being a Scribe promoted to a rank typically reserved for Paladins due to his exceptional aptitude for advanced technology. Unlike traditional Brotherhood leadership, Elijah emphasized the enhancement and development of pre-War technology rather than mere preservation, a philosophy that brought him into conflict with the organization's leadership and led to his reassignment to the Mojave region. There he redirected Brotherhood operations to HELIOS One, a solar energy facility, where he sought to activate the experimental ARCHIMEDES II weapon system to counter the New California Republic. When the NCR overran the facility during Operation: Sunburst, Elijah disappeared, abandoning the Brotherhood and its remaining forces.

topic_desc: General Lee Oliver's command of NCR forces in the Mojave reflects the deep political currents shaping the republic's military leadership. His close relationship with President Aaron Kimball secured his appointment over more qualified officers such as Colonel James Hsu, whom Oliver actively hindered from promotion. This cronyism has bred widespread resentment among the rank and file. Oliver's strategic vision has been criticized as tunnel vision: while the Legion established an increasingly strong foothold on the western bank of the Colorado south of Hoover Dam, he diverted few resources to that pressing threat, instead focusing on building up the garrison at the dam itself after leaving his administrative post at Camp McCarran. His plan to defeat the Legion through mass confrontation and attrition stands in stark contrast to the Rangers' guerrilla tactics that proved decisive at the First Battle of Hoover Dam four years earlier. Oliver's grudge against Chief Hanlon and the Rangers stems from their outsized role in that victory, which he views as diminishing the Army's prestige. He is determined that the second battle be won entirely through conventional military force under his direct command.
topic_desc_basic: General Lee Oliver is a career New California Republic Army soldier and an outspoken supporter of President Aaron Kimball who serves as the commander of the republic's forces in the Mojave Wasteland. He is responsible for the overall strategy of NCR forces in the region and is preparing for the Second Battle of Hoover Dam, where he intends to confront Caesar's Legion en masse and destroy the enemy through attrition. Many lower-ranking officers and soldiers hold a low opinion of him, believing he obtained his post largely through cronyism, and his cautious approach has earned him the defamatory moniker General Wait-and-see. Oliver holds a grudge against the NCR Rangers and Chief Hanlon over the role they played in the First Battle of Hoover Dam, and he is determined to win the second battle entirely through his own methods.
tags: general wait and see,hoover dam battle,kimball political ally,mojave campaign strategy,ncr army commander,ranger rivalry

topic_desc: Gloria Van Graff oversees the Silver Rush energy weapons enterprise in Freeside as part of a sprawling family operation directed from Redding by her mother. The Van Graff matriarch expanded into the Mojave by placing Gloria and her brother Jean-Baptiste Cutting in charge of the Freeside branch, one of ten branches each managed by a different sibling, all from different fathers. Gloria's predecessor, her sister Frieda, departed to pursue what was called the opportunity of a lifetime. Despite Gloria's acknowledged intelligence, her strained relationship with her mother consigns her to remote, undesirable postings far from the family's power center. The Van Graffs' arrival in Freeside was violent: they forcibly evicted the previous occupants of the Silver Rush, killing members of the Kings who objected, creating a lasting enmity between the two groups. Gloria's business acumen extends beyond retail into aggressive competitive strategy. She has orchestrated secretive deals with Alice McLafferty of the Crimson Caravan Company aimed at destroying rival operations such as the Gun Runners and Cassidy Caravans. She also brokered a lucrative arrangement with the NCR military, luring Legion soldiers into a trap disguised as a weapons transaction in exchange for a lucrative NCR supply contract that earned the Van Graffs five times what they had made dealing with the Legion.
topic_desc_basic: Gloria Van Graff, also known as Glory, is the manager of the Silver Rush energy weapons store in Freeside, a position she holds alongside her older brother Jean-Baptiste Cutting. The Van Graff family expanded from Redding into the Mojave Wasteland under their mother's direction, and Gloria is one of ten siblings who each run different branches. Despite her sharp intellect, she receives undesirable assignments because she and her mother do not get along. Gloria took over the Silver Rush after her sister Frieda left, and the Van Graffs seized the location by force, killing members of the Kings who resisted.

topic_desc: Edgar Hardin serves as head paladin of the Mojave Brotherhood of Steel chapter, a position making him the chapter's most experienced warrior and a central figure in its internal power struggle. During the disastrous defense of HELIOS One under Elder Father Elijah, Hardin was among the senior paladins who advised a tactical retreat, counsel that Elijah ignored while obsessively pursuing an unknown technological objective. When the NCR finally overran the perimeter and Elijah vanished, Hardin followed acting elder Nolan McNamara in the retreat to the Hidden Valley Bunker. The subsequent lockdown has weighed heavily on Hardin. McNamara's refusal to lift it or even send scouts beyond the bunker has left the chapter sealed away for years, with many current paladins never having seen real combat outside training simulations. Hardin views this safety as a betrayal of the Brotherhood's core mission and believes McNamara's leadership has become paralyzed, particularly after the disappearance of patrol teams. His plans for the chapter call for resuming patrols, sending out reconnaissance, and reestablishing a Brotherhood presence in the region. His uncompromising temperament would preclude any cease-fire or alliance with Mojave factions. Only his lingering respect for McNamara's conduct during the HELIOS One retreat has prevented him from openly challenging the elder's authority.
topic_desc_basic: Head Paladin Hardin, also known as Edgar Hardin, is the head paladin of the Mojave chapter of the Brotherhood of Steel and its most experienced veteran. He was a key advisor to Father Elijah and attempted to convince the elder to abandon HELIOS One before the NCR overran the perimeter. After retreating to the Hidden Valley Bunker under acting elder Nolan McNamara, Hardin grew disillusioned with the ongoing lockdown and McNamara's refusal to send out scouts or patrols. Convinced that the chapter is stagnating and failing its mission, Hardin has considered ways to remove McNamara from leadership, restrained only by his respect for the elder's actions at HELIOS One.
tags: brotherhood mojave chapter,brotherhood stagnation,head paladin hardin,helios one retreat,hidden valley lockdown,mcnamara leadership challenge

topic_desc: Jas Wilkins operates the Mess Hall kitchen in the quarry settlement of Sloan, serving meals to the workers who extract limestone and other materials from the nearby quarry. Born and raised in California, she left NCR territory deliberately, finding the republic's ordered safety stifling and dull. She was drawn east by the reputation of New Vegas as a place where anything goes and the NCR cannot interfere. Her culinary heritage traces back to her great-aunt Rose, who ran a Bed and Breakfast in the northern California town of Modoc. Rose was known for keeping a live female Deathclaw confined in a shed, harvesting its eggs as a steady ingredient supply for her signature Deathclaw Omelets. According to Jas, a stranger eventually killed the creature by shooting it directly in the eye, but the omelet recipe was passed down through the family. Jas has attempted to recreate the dish using eggs from the Deathclaw population inhabiting Quarry Junction near Sloan, though the quarry workers are more vocal about their dissatisfaction with her coffee than her cooking. Her presence in Sloan reflects the broader pattern of NCR citizens drifting into the Mojave seeking opportunity and freedom absent in the republic's controlled territories.
topic_desc_basic: Jas Wilkins is a food merchant and cook operating the Mess Hall at Sloan in the Mojave Wasteland. Originally from California, she traveled east because she found life under the NCR too safe and boring, drawn by the freedom of New Vegas. Her great-aunt Rose ran a Bed & Breakfast in Modoc and kept a female Deathclaw in a shed to harvest eggs for Deathclaw Omelets, a recipe passed down to Jas. The quarry workers at Sloan complain about her coffee.

topic_desc: Jeannie May Crawford presides over the Dino Dee-lite Motel in Novac, a settlement whose survival hinges on salvage recovered from the nearby REPCONN Test Site. She presents herself as a hospitable innkeeper and staunch defender of Novac's hardworking community, dismissing outside criticism of the frontier town. Her fear of the ghouls occupying REPCONN stems from economic anxiety—if the ghouls drive salvagers away, Novac's livelihood collapses. Beneath her civic pride, however, lies a darker truth: she orchestrated the kidnapping of Carla Boone, wife of former NCR sharpshooter Craig Boone, selling her to Caesar's Legion slavers. A bill of sale documenting the transaction exists as evidence of her crime. She publicly expresses sympathy for Boone's loss while privately suggesting Carla may have simply run off, deflecting suspicion from herself.
topic_desc_basic: Jeannie May Crawford is the owner-operator of the Dino Dee-lite Motel in the frontier town of Novac. She is a proud businesswoman who defends her town and its hardworking citizens against criticism. She fears the ghouls inhabiting the nearby REPCONN Test Site, believing they threaten the salvage-based economy that sustains Novac. Despite her welcoming demeanor, she is secretly responsible for selling Craig Boone's wife Carla into slavery to Caesar's Legion.

topic_desc: Jerry was among the Great Khans who traveled east from New California Republic territory as a child, settling in Red Rock Canyon roughly fourteen years before the present day. When the Followers of the Apocalypse made contact with the tribe's camp, they brought Pre-War books on science, history, and poetry. Jerry immersed himself in these texts, reading Pre-War poetry for hours and developing a talent for verse that sets him apart from his warrior kin. He has attempted the Great Khan initiation five times and failed each, unsuited to the tribe's martial expectations. His poems blend romantic longing with the indignities of Khan life—rejection by women, beatings at the hands of their brothers, and the sting of radscorpion bites. He dreams of leaving Red Rock Canyon for the Old Mormon Fort in Freeside, where the Followers of the Apocalypse might appreciate his sensitive nature and literary inclinations.
topic_desc_basic: Jerry the Punk is a young Great Khan living at Red Rock Canyon who harbors an unusual passion for poetry, a talent he developed after reading Pre-War books provided to the tribe by the Followers of the Apocalypse. Though he considers the Great Khans his family, he feels out of place among them and has failed the tribe's initiation five times. His poems often blend romantic longing with the harsh realities of Khan life, including rejection by women and beatings at the hands of their brothers. Jerry dreams of leaving the canyon to join the Followers of the Apocalypse at the Old Mormon Fort in Freeside, where he hopes to find people who better appreciate his sensitive nature.
tags: failed khan initiation,followers of apocalypse,great khan poet,pre-war poetry,red rock canyon

topic_desc: Joshua Graham was born in Ogden, known to its inhabitants as New Canaan. Fluent in several tribal dialects, he was recruited by the Followers of the Apocalypse for an expedition to the Grand Canyon. Along the Long 15 and Highway 89 south, he and his companions encountered Edward Sallow and Calhoun. A translation error led the Blackfoot tribe to take the group hostage. Sallow turned the crisis to his advantage, teaching the Blackfoots warfare; Graham's linguistic skills proved indispensable. When Sallow crowned himself Caesar, Graham became the Malpais Legate, and for thirty years helped conquer tribes across Utah, Colorado, Arizona, and New Mexico. In 2277, Caesar ordered Graham to seize Hoover Dam from the NCR. He underestimated Chief Hanlon's rangers and rigidly commanded his forces, allowing the NCR to spring a devastating trap. As punishment, Caesar had Graham covered in pitch, set ablaze, and cast into the Grand Canyon. He survived, climbed out, and walked three months to New Canaan. The New Canaanites welcomed him without question. Rumors of his survival reached Caesar, who dispatched Frumentarii to hunt him; Graham killed them, confirming Caesar's suspicions. Legionaries were forbidden to speak his name, calling him only the Burned Man. When the White Legs tribe sought entry into the Legion, they were tasked with destroying New Canaan as a rite of passage. They attacked at night, slaughtering the elderly, ill, and children. Only thirty inhabitants escaped. Graham fled with survivors to Zion Canyon, where he lives among the Sorrows tribe and prepares to stand against the pursuing White Legs, aided by the Dead Horses tribe.
topic_desc_basic: Joshua Graham, also known as the Malpais Legate and the Burned Man, is a New Canaanite missionary and former co-founder of Caesar's Legion. After helping Caesar forge his empire for thirty years, Graham led the failed assault on Hoover Dam in 2277, resulting in Caesar having him burned alive and cast into the Grand Canyon. He survived the execution attempt and returned to New Canaan, but a subsequent attack by the White Legs tribe destroyed the settlement and forced him to flee with survivors to Zion Canyon. There, he lives among the Sorrows tribe and prepares to make a stand against the pursuing White Legs, despite fellow New Canaanite Daniel advocating for evacuation.
tags: burned man,caesar legion co-founder,hoover dam defeat,malpais legate,new canaanite missionary,zion canyon

topic_desc: Judah Kreger served as an Enclave officer commanding a squad stationed at Navarro, a position that placed him over Cannibal Johnson, Orion Moreno, Daisy Whitman, Doctor Henry, and Arcade Gannon's father. His leadership kept the volatile Johnson and Moreno from tearing each other apart and served as the bond holding the unit together through years of service. Kreger recalls that the Enclave gave him purpose, and while he acknowledges that those in charge were ruthless, he maintains that his group strove to civilize things during a time when the NCR was young and uncertain. Following the destruction of Control Station ENCLAVE and the NCR's sacking of Navarro, Kreger fled alongside other survivors to avoid violence from both the NCR and the Brotherhood of Steel. He initially found work as a trader but grew weary of the constant travel. He eventually settled in the Westside community of the Mojave Wasteland, where he has lived for several years. Though no longer in command, the other Enclave remnants still follow his direction out of respect rather than obligation.
topic_desc_basic: Judah Kreger is a former Enclave captain living in the Westside community of the Mojave Wasteland. He served as an Enclave officer in command of a squad stationed at Navarro that included Cannibal Johnson, Orion Moreno, Daisy Whitman, Doctor Henry, and Arcade Gannon's father. Kreger's leadership kept Johnson and Moreno from tearing each other apart and served as the bond holding the group together. After the destruction of Control Station ENCLAVE and the NCR's sacking of Navarro, he fled alongside other Enclave survivors to avoid violence at the hands of the NCR and Brotherhood of Steel.

topic_desc: Klamath Bob's life traces a long arc from the northern wasteland town of Klamath to the Mojave's Westside. He recalls his hometown as a place built around gecko hunting and skinning, and references the visit of a tribal from Arroyo—likely the Chosen One—though he notes it was before his time. At some point Bob traveled to The Hub, where he witnessed a Super Mutant from the Master's Unity being abused by locals. He attempted to "buy" the mutant, later known as Mean Sonofabitch, to spare him further harm, though the effort failed. When Bob eventually settled in Westside, Mean Sonofabitch appeared on his own, recognized Bob, and remained as a community protector. Bob's liquor store serves as a modest but vital resource for Westside residents, and his nightly patrols reflect a personal commitment to the settlement's safety despite his admitted inexperience with guns. He holds strong views against chem dealers who prey on decent folk, favoring lethal justice in such cases.
topic_desc_basic: Klamath Bob, often simply called Bob, is a shopkeeper living in the Westside settlement of New Vegas. Originally from the northern town of Klamath, he recalls his hometown as a dull but pleasant place known for hunting, eating, and skinning geckos. He runs a liquor store named after himself, supplying residents who need a drink to face the day, and after hours he patrols Westside to help keep the peace despite his limited skill with firearms. Bob is also known for his friendship with Mean Sonofabitch, a Super Mutant veteran of the Unity, whom he once tried to protect from abuse in The Hub and who later followed him to Westside, where the mutant now performs odd jobs and helps defend the community.
tags: gecko hunting hometown,klamath native,liquor store owner,mean sonofabitch friend,unity super mutant,westside shopkeeper
