topic_desc: Legate Lanius rose to prominence after Caesar recognized the potential in a warrior who had slaughtered fifteen of his own Hidebarks tribesmen in rage at their chief's surrender. Granted an iron-forged helmet and the name Lanius—"butcher" in Latin—he accepted loyalty on the condition he could execute all surviving males of his tribe, sparing only young boys for Legion indoctrination. Before being recalled for the Second Battle of Hoover Dam, Lanius oversaw years of eastern expansion: the conquest of Colorado, the defeat of the Hangdogs in Denver by burning their sacred hounds, and a Utah campaign that assimilated fourteen tribes and exterminated five others. These campaigns strained Legion supply lines and instilled caution about overextension. Lanius regards war as the Legion's only legitimate path, disdaining diplomacy, subterfuge, and Vulpes Inculta's methods. He views the NCR as capable adversaries, respects their Rangers, and considers Chief Hanlon more dangerous than General Oliver. Mr. House describes him as brutal but unsubtle, likely to rely on frontal assault. Lanius's experiences in Colorado lead him to privately doubt whether holding western territory is sustainable, and he is prepared to withdraw if victory seems unlikely.
topic_desc_basic: Legate Lanius, known as the Monster of the East or Terror of the East, serves as the military commander of Caesar's Legion, having replaced Joshua Graham in that role following the Legion's defeat at the First Battle of Hoover Dam. Originally the most formidable warrior of the Hidebarks, an Arizona tribe, Lanius turned on his own people after their chief surrendered to the Legion, slaughtering fifteen warriors before being subdued. Caesar granted him the name Lanius, meaning "butcher," and he pledged loyalty on the condition that he be allowed to execute all surviving males of his tribe. He is loyal only to Caesar himself, caring nothing for battlefield losses so long as the enemy suffers more, and Caesar relies on him to enforce brutal disciplinary measures against underperforming officers.
tags: butcher of arizona,caesar legion legate,colorado campaign conqueror,hidebarks tribe warrior,hoover dam commander,monster of the east

topic_desc: Lily Bowen's transformation from a 75-year-old grandmother of Vault 17 into a Nightkin assassin reflects the Master's indiscriminate conscription of human subjects into his Unity army. Under squad leader Tabitha, Lily served as a spy and killer until the Cathedral's destruction freed her to attempt a return home. Her vertibird-blade sword, salvaged from a crash near Klamath, is a testament to her resourcefulness. At Jacobstown, Marcus provides her refuge while Doctor Henry attempts to treat her schizophrenia—a condition caused by prolonged Stealth Boy overuse that manifests as a hostile alternate personality named Leo. Lily resists full medication dosages because the antipsychotic drugs cause memory loss, and she clings to a holotape recording of her grandchildren, Becky and Jimmy, as an anchor to her pre-transformation identity. Her cooperation with Henry's experimental treatments, despite personal risk, suggests a willingness to help other Nightkin even at potential cost to herself. In combat she may suffer psychotic breaks, counting to ten as a calming mantra while Leo urges aggression.
topic_desc_basic: Lily is an elderly Nightkin residing in Jacobstown, a settlement led by the super mutant Marcus, where she tends to bighorners. Born a human in Vault 17, she was transformed into a Nightkin at age 75 by the Master and served as an assassin and spy in his army under squad leader Tabitha until the Cathedral's destruction, after which she attempted to return home. She carries a sword fashioned from a crashed vertibird blade near Klamath and keeps a holotape of her grandchildren, Becky and Jimmy, whose memories she fiercely protects. Lily suffers from schizophrenia caused by excessive Stealth Boy use, manifesting as a second personality named Leo, and receives treatment from Doctor Henry with antipsychotic drugs, though she resists full dosages due to the memory loss side effects.
tags: bighorner tender,doctor henry patient,jacobstown nightkin resident,master unity assassin,stealth boy schizophrenia,vault 17 survivor

topic_desc: Lieutenant Carrie Boyd functions as the primary military police authority at Camp McCarran, the NCR's forward operating base in the Mojave Wasteland. Operating under Colonel Hsu's command, she manages base security including break-ins, thefts, missing-soldier investigations, and prisoner interrogations. Boyd's approach to law enforcement is pragmatic and aggressive; she has openly expressed a desire to shoot anyone who talks back to her, restrained only by NCR military regulations. She notes that certain restrictions on harsh interrogation methods originate from President Tandi's administration, suggesting a tension between older NCR ideals of justice and the realities of wartime policing in the Mojave. Boyd is willing to leverage non-NCR personnel—such as the Courier—to conduct interrogations that would violate NCR rules if performed by its own soldiers, exploiting the legal ambiguity of using outsiders who are not bound by military regulations. Her office on the second floor's east side serves as her base of operations, and she directs inquiries about missing soldiers, including Corporal White, to Colonel Hsu.
topic_desc_basic: Lieutenant Carrie Boyd is a military police officer stationed at Camp McCarran, where she serves as the officer in charge of policing duties for the base. She handles break-ins, thefts, investigations into missing soldiers, and the interrogation of prisoners. Boyd reports to Colonel Hsu and operates from her office on the east side of the second floor. Known for her sharp tongue and no-nonsense attitude, she has expressed a willingness to use harsher interrogation tactics than NCR regulations typically allow, noting that some restrictions on such methods date back to President Tandi's administration.
tags: base security investigator,camp mccarran mp officer,colonel hsu subordinate,ncr military police,prisoner interrogation,tandi era regulations

topic_desc: Major Knight embodies the tensions of NCR frontier service: competent but bored, stationed at the Mojave Outpost for what he calls ages, logging an ever-growing caravan traffic backlog. The outpost serves as the administrative headquarters for the Primm region, yet bureaucratic red tape prevents Knight from assisting Lieutenant Hayes's undermanned unit near Primm, a restriction that visibly frustrates him. He could be persuaded to bend orders with enough convincing or caps, but the chain of command holds firm. Knight is a master repairman with a full Repair skill, monetizing that expertise by charging steep prices from soldiers and travelers alike. Personally, Knight conceals his homosexuality at the outpost, noting that while same-sex relationships are accepted back in California, what he calls "friendships" do not fare well on the fringes of the Republic. He considers the NCR far preferable to Caesar's Legion and remains professional on duty, though he wistfully admits he would pursue such friendships if circumstances allowed.
topic_desc_basic: Major Knight is an NCR Army officer stationed at the Mojave Outpost, where he has spent a long time logging caravan traffic that keeps building up as more people arrive than leave. He is an expert repairman who fixes soldiers' and travelers' gear in exchange for caps, charging a hefty sum for his services. Although the Mojave Outpost serves as the administrative headquarters for the area around Primm, bureaucratic red tape prevents Knight from offering support to Lieutenant Hayes's unit stationed near Primm, a situation that frustrates him. Knight is homosexual but keeps his sexuality hidden while at the outpost, explaining that while such relationships are accepted back in California, they do not fare well on the fringes of the Republic, and he prefers to stay professional on duty rather than risk the disapproval of his fellow soldiers.
tags: caravan traffic logging,expert repairman,homosexuality ncr frontier,mojave outpost headquarters,ncr army officer,primm bureaucratic red tape

topic_desc: Old Ben's life traces the harsh social geography of the Mojave, from Freeside poverty to the Strip and back. Born and raised in Freeside, he worked his father's butcher shop until a competitor undercut them with cheap "strange meat." Ben suspected human flesh was being sold; residents later suffered the "shakes," and after the vendor died insane, half-buried human remains were discovered in the crawlspace. His father died from the loss of the shop. Ben scraped together caps for a Strip passport when they were cheaper, landing work as a crier at The Tops, where he advertised performers and received a casino apartment. A manager framed him for vault theft, and Ben was fired and expelled. Back in Freeside, he worked as an escort, then a gun-for-hire bodyguard for a decade, and briefly as a courier before quitting over shifty clients. Now retired, he helps around Freeside but finds life dull without action.
topic_desc_basic: Old Ben is a lifelong resident of Freeside who worked at his father's butcher shop until a competitor selling cheap "strange meat" drove them out of business. Ben suspected the rival vendor was selling human flesh, a belief that appeared validated when the vendor went insane, died, and human remains were later found in their crawlspace. Ben eventually earned enough caps to buy a passport into the New Vegas Strip, where he worked as a crier at The Tops casino and was given a casino apartment. He was framed for stealing from the casino vault and was fired, losing his apartment and returning to Freeside.
tags: bodyguard career,casino vault framing,freeside lifelong resident,retired gun for hire,strange meat scandal,the tops crier

topic_desc: Old Lady Gibson is a veteran scavenger and repairwoman operating a scrapyard north of Novac. In her youth she traveled with caravans, during which she became acquainted with Doctor Henry, a connection that later proves relevant to certain technical inquiries. She and her husband settled near Novac and spent the better part of their lives stripping salvage from the REPCONN Test Site, selling what they recovered. Her favorite chair is the "O" from the old REPCONN sign. After her husband's death she continues running the yard alone, offering repair services and selling a variety of goods, including components for weapon repair kits. She carries the unique sawed-off shotgun Big Boomer. Her scrapyard is home to several dogs named Basura, Rey, Reina, Colmillo, Fiel, and Audaz. She takes pride in her nickname, considering longevity an accomplishment. Her knowledge of old technology makes her a useful contact for anyone seeking thrust control modules or information about certain robotic units.
topic_desc_basic: Old Lady Gibson, often called simply Gibson, runs a scrap yard north of Novac. A lifelong scavenger, she traveled with caravans in her youth and became acquainted with Doctor Henry during those years. She later settled near Novac with her husband, and together they spent much of their lives scavenging the REPCONN Test Site for salvage to sell. After her husband's death, she continues to operate the scrapyard, offering repair services and selling various items.
tags: big boomer shotgun,doctor henry acquaintance,lifelong scavenger repairwoman,novac scrapyard operator,pet dogs scrapyard,reconn test site scavenger

topic_desc: Papa Khan leads the Great Khans from Red Rock Canyon, residing in the Great Khan Longhouse, the only concrete structure in the settlement. Despite the Khans' fearsome raider reputation, Jack describes him as "a softie at heart." His leadership is driven by a desire to leave a legacy of greatness and to avenge past defeats by the NCR, particularly the massacres that decimated his people. This hunger for vindication has led him into an alliance with Caesar's Legion, brokered by the Legion's envoy Karl, who flatters Papa Khan with visions of Khan glory. Papa Khan fails to recognize the existential threat the Legion poses to his tribe; Karl privately holds the Khans in contempt. Those close to Papa Khan, including his lieutenant Regis, harbor doubts about the alliance. Breaking the Legion pact requires exposing Karl's duplicity, after which Papa Khan turns on the envoy violently. Alternatively, he can be persuaded to abandon revenge entirely and seek renewed greatness elsewhere, or driven to fatalistic decline.
topic_desc_basic: Papa Khan is the chief and leader of the Great Khans, a raider tribe based in Red Rock Canyon. He resides in the Great Khan Longhouse, the only concrete building in the village, and is described by at least one acquaintance as a softie at heart despite the fearsome reputation of his people. Papa Khan has entered into an alliance with Caesar's Legion, guided by the Legion's envoy Karl, though he fails to recognize the danger this partnership poses to his tribe. His desire to leave a legacy of greatness and seek revenge against the NCR for past conflicts heavily influences his leadership decisions.
tags: caesar legion alliance,envoy karl deception,great khans chief,legacy of greatness,ncr revenge motivation,red rock canyon leader

topic_desc: Philippe is the executive chef of the Gourmand restaurant at the Ultra-Luxe. He has worked there for years and built a reputation for turning brahmin steak into refined cuisine, though his pride and volatile temper make him difficult to work with. Philippe describes a childhood marked by abandonment, a chem-dependent mother, and sisters who shut him inside a shipping crate. His obsessive approach to cooking extends to repeated attempts to imitate the flavor of human flesh with other ingredients. He records these experiments in handwritten recipes, with the dish he calls Sweet Veal receiving the most revisions. Mortimer of the White Glove Society considers Philippe capable of secretly using human flesh, although Philippe's records emphasize his search for substitutes. Philippe enjoys the authority of his kitchen but believes he is underpaid and resents the people who take a share of the Gourmand's earnings.
topic_desc_basic: Philippe is the executive chef of the Gourmand restaurant at the Ultra-Luxe casino in New Vegas, serving the White Glove Society. He is renowned for elevating brahmin steak into a delicacy and considers himself the god of New Vegas brahmin fusion cuisine. Philippe has an intense obsession with fresh ingredients and a notoriously volatile temper, likely rooted in a traumatic childhood involving an absent father, a chem-addicted mother, and abusive siblings who would lock him in a shipping crate. He has spent considerable effort experimenting with substitutes to approximate the taste of human flesh, keeping handwritten recipes of his various attempts, with his "Sweet Veal" recipe undergoing the most revisions.
tags: brahmin fusion cuisine,gourmand restaurant,imitation strange meat,traumatic childhood,ultra luxe chef,white glove society
editorial_note: Source-grounded editorial rewrite.

topic_desc: Davey Crenshaw's career at Camp McCarran is defined by a complete lack of self-awareness and an oblivious disregard for everyone around him. His pranks, while physically harmless, were never motivated by safety concerns and have alienated every soldier who serves alongside him. Beyond the brahmin incident and the firecracker-toilet destruction, Crenshaw sabotaged computer security across the camp and hacked into others' terminals for mischief, forcing personnel to be more vigilant about terminal security. His reputation as a problem child earned him multiple disciplinary hearings, yet he remains unrepentant and treats his notoriety as a badge of honor. His superiors, having no faith in him, assigned him to guard one of the camp's more remote posts. This isolation made him an ideal fall guy for frumentarius Picus, a Caesar's Legion infiltrator operating within Camp McCarran. Picus manipulated Crenshaw's reputation to frame him for the sabotage and bombing of the NCR monorail, planning to have an accomplice plant evidence in Crenshaw's footlocker, kill him at his isolated post, and posthumously turn him in for treason. The plan exploited the fact that Colonel James Hsu and others would readily believe Crenshaw capable of such an act given his history.
topic_desc_basic: Private Davey Crenshaw is an NCR soldier stationed at Camp McCarran, widely regarded as a disciplinary problem and prankster with no regard for those around him. His antics, such as leading a brahmin upstairs in the terminal building and destroying toilets with firecrackers, have made him unpopular among his fellow troopers, though he remains unrepentant and considers his reputation a point of pride. He has also sabotaged computer security and hacked terminals for mischief, prompting personnel to be more mindful of their terminals. Due to his conduct and his superiors' lack of faith in him, he was assigned to guard a remote post at the camp.
tags: disciplinary problem soldier,frumentarius picus,legion infiltration,monorail bombing frame,ncr camp mccarran,prankster trooper

topic_desc: Ranger Andy is a veteran of the NCR Rangers who now lives in Novac, serving as the town's de facto lawman while other residents like Boone and Vargas watch the highway. His retirement was forced by a devastating incident during a raid on Legion slavers: acting on intelligence that slavers were holed up in a burned-out house a few kilometers from their station, Andy led a team of Rangers to the location, only to find it deserted except for a scrawny child hiding in a closet. When Andy tried to pick the child up to bring him to safety, the child retreated into the closet and left a live grenade at his feet. The explosion mangled half his body, permanently damaging his arm and leg and ending his active service. In Novac, Andy developed a reputation for having a good eye for people. He was one of the few residents who did not dislike Carla Boone, whom he considered a sweet girl whose directness about the poor quality of life in Novac was a coping mechanism for frontier existence. Andy maintains contact with active Rangers at Ranger Station Charlie via ham radio, and patrols check on him regularly, joking that they are paying respects. A recent fall down the motel stairs, courtesy of Mayor Jeannie May's establishment, further injured his leg and confined him to his bungalow for weeks, dealing a serious blow to his self-worth.
topic_desc_basic: Ranger Andy is a former NCR Ranger who serves as Novac's closest thing to a lawman, watching over the town while others monitor the highway. He was forced into retirement years ago after a raid on Legion slavers went wrong, when a child hiding in a closet left a live grenade at his feet, mangling half his body and leaving him with lasting damage to his arm and leg. He settled in Novac and took on a informal sheriff role, known for having a good eye for people and being one of the few residents who didn't dislike Carla Boone, viewing her directness as a coping mechanism for frontier life. He stays in touch with active Rangers at Ranger Station Charlie through his ham radio, with patrols checking on him regularly.
tags: carla boone,legion slaver raid,ncr ranger veteran,novac lawman,ranger station charlie,retired ranger

topic_desc: A native of Redding, Ranger Dobson built his career fighting slavers before being stationed at Camp McCarran in 2281. When the NCR Correctional Facility fell to the Powder Gangers, Dobson went off on his own initiative to scout the situation, establishing a safehouse in a Hidden Valley bunker. His primary focus is Samuel Cooke, a terrorist whose gang of roamers Dobson considers the most dangerous faction among the Powder Gangers. However, his contempt extends to all Powder Gangers, whom he views as the lowest of the low for preying on caravans and civilians; he will shoot any Powder Ganger he encounters on sight. The Hidden Valley bunker offers relative safety from predators and troublemakers due to its remote location and the natural sandstorms that sweep the area, though these same phenomena interfere with his radio broadcasts, making communication with McCarran problematic. Dobson's personality is defined by confidence tempered by pragmatism: he knows his limits and is not headstrong. He enjoys joking with anyone, including complete strangers and radio operators at McCarran HQ, but this habit has caused his reports to be taken less seriously. Despite his genial demeanor, Dobson becomes deadly serious when he suspects danger or deception, though he is willing to forgive those who admit wrongdoing unless they persist.
topic_desc_basic: Ranger Dobson is an NCR Ranger originally from Redding who has seen extensive action against slavers during his career. As of 2281, he is stationed at Camp McCarran but has gone off on his own to scout the NCR Correctional Facility lost to the Powder Gangers, setting up a safehouse in a Hidden Valley bunker. His primary target is the terrorist Samuel Cooke and his gang of roamers, whom he considers the most dangerous of the Powder Gangers, though he despises all of them for preying on caravans and civilians and will shoot any on sight. Dobson is confident and takes pride in protecting the innocent of the Mojave Wasteland, but knows his limits and loves to joke around with anyone, even radio operators at McCarran HQ, which has led them to take his reports less seriously.
tags: camp mccarran,hidden valley bunker,ncr ranger scout,powder gangers threat,redding native,samuel cooke terrorist

topic_desc: Ranger Ghost serves as a marksman atop the barracks at Mojave Outpost, the southernmost NCR installation along the I-15 corridor. Her posting places her as the first line of defense against threats approaching from the Mojave Wasteland, but she views the assignment as a bureaucratic sinkhole with no prospect of advancement or meaningful action. Her frustration extends beyond personal circumstance to the broader state of the NCR under President Kimball, whose policies she regards with deep skepticism. NCR command has ordered only a standing force at the outpost rather than an effective one, a distinction that grates on her daily. Ghost possesses an unusual perceptiveness in reading people—she can identify a person's trade by the pattern of their pacing and notices whether someone broadcasts their movements. This skill, honed by long hours of watchful isolation, makes her an astute judge of character. When smoke rises from Nipton and foot traffic along the road ceases, she suspects Powder Ganger activity and seeks someone willing to investigate what the outpost's constrained forces cannot.
topic_desc_basic: Ranger Ghost is an NCR Ranger stationed at the Mojave Outpost, where she serves as a marksman defending against threats approaching from the I-15. She is frustrated with her assignment and the state of the NCR under President Kimball, viewing the outpost as a bureaucratic dead end. She is concerned about a lack of traffic and smoke rising from the nearby town of Nipton, which she suspects may be the result of an attack by Powder Gangers. She is perceptive in reading people and can determine a person's trade by their walking pattern.
tags: bureaucratic dead end,i-15 watch,mojave outpost defender,ncr ranger marksman,nipton smoke concern,perception of people

topic_desc: Ranger Jackson commands Mojave Outpost, the NCR's southernmost garrison positioned at the critical junction where the I-15 enters the Mojave. His orders require him to maintain a standing force at all times, a directive he understands but resents, as it leaves him unable to respond to the caravan attacks that have choked traffic through the Ivanpah valley. Reinforcements that arrive at the outpost are immediately routed onward to Camp McCarran and frontline positions like Camp Forlorn Hope, leaving Jackson with insufficient personnel to patrol or protect the trade routes his garrison ostensibly safeguards. Caravans back up at the outpost, creating a logistical bottleneck that worsens with each attack. Though regulations prevent him from formally contracting mercenaries, Jackson has been known to lose supplies to individuals who take on dangerous assignments—such as clearing hostile forces from the Ivanpah valley—allowing him to address problems without violating his orders. His strict adherence to law is well known; he does not hesitate to chain vigilantes and deliver them to the justice system. Cass trusts him enough to ask him to bring her case before NCR institutions, though she describes him bluntly as a washed-out old fuckup who has served long enough to see only the worst outcome in everything.
topic_desc_basic: Ranger Jackson is an NCR Ranger serving as the commanding officer of Mojave Outpost, where he maintains a standing force in accordance with his orders. He would prefer less bureaucracy and more direct results in the ongoing conflict, but arriving reinforcements are routed to Camp McCarran and frontline outposts like Camp Forlorn Hope, leaving him unable to send patrols to protect caravans that come under attack. While he cannot officially hire mercenaries, he is known to lose supplies to individuals willing to take on dangerous assignments, such as clearing routes through the Ivanpah valley so caravan traffic can resume. Cass, who trusts him enough to ask him to bring her case forward to the relevant NCR institutions, refers to him as a washed-out old fuckup who has served long enough to only see the worst outcome of everything.
tags: caravan protection failure,cass trusted contact,ivanpah valley route,mojave outpost commander,ncr standing force,strict law enforcement

topic_desc: Raul Alfonso Tejada was born in 2047 at Hidalgo Ranch outside Mexico City, where his family raised him with enough discipline to offset his occasional trouble with the law. The ranch survived the Great War at a distance from the city, but within days refugees flooded down the road. The Tejadas shared what they could until food ran short, and Raul's father began turning people away. The situation turned violent—Raul and his father drove off refugees at gunpoint, but that night two dozen men barred the doors and set the house ablaze. Raul escaped through a window with his younger sister Rafaela, but the rest of his family perished. The siblings fled to the radioactive ruins of Mexico City, where Raul began ghoulifying from radiation exposure. He found a vaquero costume in a novelty shop, which made Rafaela laugh for the first time since the bombs fell. When raiders killed Rafaela, Raul hunted them down in a rage. He eventually reached Tucson, Arizona—called Two-Sun by locals—where he lived for seventy-five years under the name Miguel, watching over a prostitute named Claudia who resembled Rafaela. After losing Claudia to Dirty Dave's gang, Raul abandoned his guns and headed west, eventually imprisoned at Black Mountain by the nightkin Tabitha and forced to repair her robot Rhonda.
topic_desc_basic: Raul Alfonso Tejada is a ghoul mechanic and former gunslinger born in 2047 who was living at Hidalgo Ranch outside Mexico City before the Great War. After losing most of his family to refugees who burned their home, he fled with his younger sister Rafaela to the radioactive ruins of Mexico City, where he began ghoulifying from radiation exposure. Rafaela was killed by raiders, prompting Raul to hunt down and kill those responsible. He eventually made his way to Tucson, Arizona, known locally as Two-Sun, where he lived for 75 years under the name Miguel and watched over a prostitute named Claudia who resembled his late sister, only to lose her as well to a gang led by Dirty Dave.
tags: black mountain prisoner,ghoul mechanic gunslinger,hidalgo ranch survivor,mexico city ruins,rafaela tejada,two-sun tucson arizona,vaquero costume

topic_desc: Rex is a Mk. III Support Model cyberdog who served as a police dog in Colorado before the Great War. He survived the war and eventually saw combat duty with Caesar's Legion, a past he still retains memories of; a Legion bull decal remains on his battered, scorched bodywork. The King obtained Rex from a salvager a few years ago and brought him to the Followers of the Apocalypse, who repaired his damaged chassis. Rex has served as the King's loyal companion in Freeside ever since, residing at the King's School of Impersonation. Rex's aging brain suffers from neural degradation, a condition the Followers identified but could not treat—the bio med gel surrounding his brain cannot preserve it perpetually, and the sophisticated cybernetics work required for replacement surgery exceeds their capabilities. Rex displays strong behavioral quirks: he hates rats and mole rats, charging at the scent of one, and dislikes hats and those who wear them for reasons the King cannot explain. Cyberdogs are not uncommon in Denver, and Caesar himself once possessed a similar cyberdog that was lost in battle. Like all cyberdogs, Rex is unaffected by pulse weapons and possesses a unique tackling attack that brings enemies to the ground.
topic_desc_basic: Rex, often called Rexie by The King, is a cyberdog living in Freeside as the loyal companion of the man himself. A Mk. III Support Model, he served as a police dog in Colorado before the Great War and later saw combat duty with Caesar's Legion, a past he still retains memories of. The King obtained him from a salvager a few years ago and had the Followers of the Apocalypse repair his battered, scorched bodywork.
tags: bio med gel,colorado police dog,cyberdog mk iii,freeside king companion,legion combat dog,neural brain degradation

topic_desc: Born June 25, 2020, Robert Edwin House was orphaned young and cheated out of his inheritance by his brother Anthony, who seized control of H&H Tools Company. House attended the Commonwealth Institute of Technology and founded RobCo Industries on his 22nd birthday, building it into one of the world's most profitable corporations within five years. He acquired REPCONN Aerospace and established the House Resort and Country Club. On April 14, 2065, House predicted atomic war within fifteen years and began devising defensive technologies for Las Vegas, commissioning the Platinum Chip to upgrade Securitrons and the city's missile defense grid. He integrated himself with the Lucky 38's subsystems via a cerebral interface. When war came in 2077, his systems neutralized 59 warheads with disarm codes and destroyed nine more with rooftop laser cannons, but software glitches forced him offline. After rebooting with an older operating system, he fell into a coma lasting decades. Upon waking, he recruited tribes into the Three Families, negotiated a treaty granting the NCR Hoover Dam and McCarran while preserving New Vegas independence, and filled Vault 21 with concrete after winning it in a gambling competition. He views autocracy under a technological visionary as mankind's remedy, not democracy.
topic_desc_basic: Robert Edwin House, commonly known as Mr. House, is the founder of RobCo Industries and the sole proprietor of the New Vegas Strip as of 2281. Before the Great War, he predicted the nuclear apocalypse and integrated himself into a life-extension chamber within the Lucky 38 casino to oversee the city's missile defense. Although the loss of the Platinum Chip caused him to fall into a decades-long coma, he awoke to recruit local tribes into the Three Families and establish New Vegas before the New California Republic could claim it.
tags: lucky 38 operator,new vegas proprietor,platinum chip commissioner,pre-war defense planner,robco industries founder,robert house biography

topic_desc: Bitter-Root's upbringing within the Great Khans at Bitter Springs was marked by extreme dysfunction. His father, a sadistic alcoholic, took him on killing raids against NCR military and civilian targets beginning at age three, afterward laughing about the murders with fellow drug addicts. His mother attempted repeatedly to sell him into slavery in exchange for jet. During the Bitter Springs Massacre, NCR forces under then-Captain Major Dhatri overran the Khans' encampment. Bitter-Root claims no memory of the event but admits that blood covering him afterward was not necessarily all spilled by NCR fire, suggesting he may have settled personal scores against some Khans during the chaos. Dhatri took the boy in as his son. Bitter-Root's name follows the Great Khans' rite-of-passage tradition, in which a member reaching adulthood is severely beaten and, upon surviving, chooses their own name. Though too young for the beat-down, he considers the massacre itself his rite of passage. The lingering trauma drove him to seek therapy from Doctor Usanagi of the Followers of the Apocalypse, who helped him work through some of his psychological burdens. He serves as the only active First Recon member who actually sleeps at night.
topic_desc_basic: Sergeant Bitter-Root is a sniper serving with Alpha Team of the NCR First Recon at Camp McCarran. Born to Great Khan parents at Bitter Springs, he endured a grim childhood with a sadistic, alcoholic father who took him killing NCR personnel and civilians from age three, and a mother who repeatedly tried to sell him into slavery for jet. He was liberated during the Bitter Springs Massacre by then-Captain Major Dhatri, who took him in as his son. Bitter-Root chose his name as part of a Great Khans naming tradition, referring both to his bitter upbringing and the massacre he considers his rite of passage.
tags: bitter springs massacre,bitter-root sniper,dhatri adopted son,first recon alpha team,great khans naming tradition,ncr camp mccarran

topic_desc: Contreras operates the Camp McCarran Supply Shack as a front for an extensive black-market operation. He diverts weapons and ammunition from NCR Army inventory, using intermediaries to collect merchandise and communicate with suppliers so that his own hands remain clean. Despite Lieutenant Carrie Boyd's suspicions and weekly inventory checks that consistently come up short on guns and ammunition, Contreras always pawns off the goods before MPs can search his quarters. Beyond arms dealing, he leverages military connections to acquire chemical components nominally intended for Army medical use but suitable for manufacturing potent recreational drugs. His Westside contact, Price, has already been taken into custody, and authorities are closing in on the sergeant for chem trafficking. Contreras is notable among NCR Army personnel for not wearing any uniform. He is one of only two merchants in the Mojave Wasteland who sells Ultrajet, alongside Jack at the Red Rock Drug Lab, if taught the recipe. He also carries large quantities of rare 12.7mm rounds, surplus 5mm ammunition, and .308 rounds, and possesses a Sunset Sarsaparilla Star Bottle Cap available for purchase.
topic_desc_basic: Sergeant Daniel Contreras is the head of the Camp McCarran Supply Shack and a supply merchant for the NCR Army. He uses his position to steal weapons and ammunition meant for military use and resell them on the black market to mercenaries, employing intermediaries to keep his hands clean and the military police off his trail. Lieutenant Carrie Boyd suspects him of wrongdoing, but despite weekly inventory checks coming up short on guns and ammo, Contreras always pawns off the goods before the MPs can search his possessions and quarters. He also uses his connections to acquire chemical components intended for Army medical use that can be used to manufacture potent recreational drugs, and his Westside contact named Price is already in custody, making it only a matter of time before authorities arrest the sergeant for chem trafficking.
tags: black market arms dealer,camp mccarran supply shack,chem trafficking ncr,contreras supply sergeant,lt boyd investigation,price westside contact

topic_desc: Silus stands apart within Caesar's Legion as an exceptional member whose insight and intelligence survived the Legion's thorough indoctrination. He earned his centurion rank through years of unquestioning service and bravery, including once charging a group of men armed with firearms wielding only a knife. He and his men wiped out countless NCR patrols to enable free movement of Legion operatives. However, Silus was not blind to Caesar's degenerating health. Before his last mission, he waited three days for Caesar's headache to subside despite the assignment's time-critical nature, and the resulting delay led to his centuria being ambushed and routed by NCR forces. As his men opened their jugulars around him to avoid capture, Silus refused to slit his own throat, unwilling to throw away all he had accomplished for what he considered a megalomaniacal self-appointed dictator. He was captured and brought to Camp McCarran for interrogation by Lieutenant Carrie Boyd, whom he takes pleasure in antagonizing, particularly by taunting her about slave collars. Silus recognized Captain Ronald Curtis upon arrival, having met him years earlier during Frumentarii training, though he did not know Curtis's current identity. Silus is the only character within the Legion known to directly criticize Caesar's leadership.
topic_desc_basic: Silus is a centurion of Caesar's Legion who was captured by the NCR during battle and brought to Camp McCarran for interrogation. Unlike most Legionaries, he retained independent thought despite indoctrination, and his intelligence and critical observation set him apart. He earned his rank through years of devoted service and bravery, once charging armed men with nothing but a knife. However, after delaying a time-critical mission for three days while waiting for Caesar's headache to subside, his centuria was ambushed and routed by the NCR.
tags: caesar legion captured,camp mccarran interrogation,frumentarii recognition,legion independent thought,lt boyd prisoner,silus centurion

topic_desc: Tech Sergeant Reyes holds the rank of Tech Sergeant and is stationed at Camp Forlorn Hope's Command Center despite the Forlorn Hope Mandate, which reassigned female troops to Camp McCarran. Her duties extend beyond compiling reports from Rangers at Camp Golf and brass at McCarran; she also tabulates stockpiles, kill ratios, mission success rates, and radiation deaths. She self-assigned responsibility for radio security after noticing no one else cared. Her analysis revealed that fewer than a third of reported enemy sightings were being intercepted, suggesting either faulty intelligence or that NCR's enemies were one step ahead. Disturbing reports included heavy casualties at Ranger Station Alpha, Super Mutant Legionaries at Delta, and Great Khans with trained Deathclaws at Foxtrot—reports she found implausible. She sought permission to authorize a code update or field clearance to investigate personally, but officers and troopers dismissed her as a desk jockey glamorizing her role. Her plan to verify communications with Ranger stations relied on the fact that encryption unique to each station's radio would be useless if compromised elsewhere.
topic_desc_basic: Tech Sergeant Reyes manages radio communications at Camp Forlorn Hope, compiling reports from Ranger stations and Camp McCarran. She discovered alarming inconsistencies in enemy sighting reports and suspects compromised codes, but her superiors dismiss her concerns, viewing her as an incompetent desk jockey. She seeks help to verify radio security with Ranger stations to pinpoint interference affecting the NCR's war effort.
tags: camp forlorn hope,code compromise,ncr radio security,ranger station reports,tech sergeant rank

topic_desc: The Forecaster is a young orphan who lives beneath the 188 Trading Post overpass and possesses an unexplained ability to perceive fragments of the past and future. He offers these impressions to travelers for caps and speaks about them with a practical directness unusual for his age. Using the ability too intensely causes severe headaches and mental strain. To control it, he wears a Psychic Nullifier that he calls his medicine; the device quiets the visions but also leaves his mind feeling empty. His parents are dead, and he says he can perceive them only when the nullifier is removed. He surrounds himself with books, cameras, flags, and other collected objects to make the empty space below the overpass feel inhabited. The busy crossing may expose him to the people and events that appear in his visions, but the origin of his power remains unknown.
topic_desc_basic: The Forecaster is a young orphaned boy living beneath the 188 Trading Post overpass in the Mojave Wasteland. He possesses psychic abilities that allow him to provide insights into both the past and future, which he shares with travelers in exchange for caps. To manage the severe headaches caused by overusing his powers, he wears a Psychic Nullifier he calls his "medicine," though it also blanks his mind. He surrounds himself with collected wasteland items like books, cameras, and flags to cope with the emptiness.
tags: 188 trading post,cathedral psyker connection,mojave wasteland,orphaned psychic child,psychic nullifier

topic_desc: Thomas Hildern was educated by the Followers of the Apocalypse but broke with them over what he characterized as their adherence to "old-world dogma," preferring to pursue large-scale practical results. He helped form the Office of Science and Industry (OSI), an organization focused on finding practical applications for knowledge. As the ambitious director of the OSI eastern division at Camp McCarran, he openly disapproves of the direction taken by executives at OSI Central and aspires to rise to a role in the central office within a few years by demonstrating his branch's effectiveness. Despite his supervisory position, Hildern performs no actual research himself; colleague Angela Williams accuses him of taking credit for others' work. He has recently focused on the NCR's projected food shortage—production is estimated to fall short of population needs within a decade due to expansion. He identified Vault 22, a pre-war facility dedicated to agricultural research, as a potential breakthrough. Rather than seeking NCR authorization, he hires mercenaries directly, a practice Williams warns is dangerous; many hired field workers have never returned, including a scientist named Keely, whom Hildern believed had a personal interest in undermining him.
topic_desc_basic: Thomas Hildern is the director of the Office of Science and Industry (OSI) eastern division, operating out of Camp McCarran's Terminal Building. Educated by the Followers of the Apocalypse, he parted ways with them over their adherence to old-world dogma, preferring to focus on large-scale results. He helped form OSI, an organization dedicated to finding practical applications for knowledge. As director of the eastern division, his team oversees the optimization of Hoover Dam power output and research into advancing food production, including supervision of the NCR Sharecropper Farms initiative.
tags: camp mccarran,followers of apocalypse,ncr food shortage,osi eastern division,vault 22 research

topic_desc: Ulysses was a member of the Twisted Hairs, an Arizona tribe whose distinctive knotted hairstyle communicated messages based on their medicinal knowledge. After Caesar betrayed the tribe and dispatched Vulpes Inculta to enslave and murder them at Dry Wells, Ulysses continued serving the Legion as a scout and Frumentarius, using his medical knowledge to cure companions. He later lived in Hopeville, a settlement in the Divide, until underground nuclear missiles were detonated by a package the Courier delivered, destroying the area. Ulysses survived and blamed the Courier for the loss. He traveled to Big MT, where he cared for an injured Brotherhood of Steel Knight named Royce and encountered the Think Tank, who explained how the Divide's missiles were activated. On Caesar's orders, he led the White Legs against New Canaan to kill Joshua Graham, teaching them to use weapons from excavated bunkers. Despite these events, he still describes Legion members as his brothers, "even as misguided as they are." He was one of seven couriers hired by Mr. House to carry packages to the New Vegas Strip but turned down the job, leading the Courier to carry the Platinum Chip. He lured the Courier back to the Divide via graffiti near Canyon Wreckage and a radio signal, leaving decals throughout the Divide and Big MT—red marking hostile areas, white marking the way forward, and blue denoting hidden caches. He named himself after Ulysses S. Grant. He is one of only three characters in the Mojave with 10 points in all SPECIAL attributes.
topic_desc_basic: Ulysses is a courier and former Frumentarii of Caesar's Legion, originally from the Twisted Hairs tribe of Arizona. After Caesar betrayed his tribe and enslaved its members at Dry Wells, Ulysses continued to serve the Legion as a scout before settling in Hopeville, which was destroyed by nuclear missiles triggered by a package delivered by another courier. He survived the destruction and blamed the Courier for the loss of his home, seeking answers and revenge. Ulysses traveled to Big MT, where the Think Tank explained to him how the Divide's missiles were activated, and he later aided the White Legs tribe in their campaign against New Canaan on Caesar's orders.
tags: caesar legion frumentarii,lonesome road courier,the divide hopeville,twisted hairs tribe,white legs new canaan

topic_desc: Veronica's personal history is deeply intertwined with the Mojave Brotherhood's decline. She traveled west as a child under Father Elijah's command, originally bound for Hoover Dam before Elijah diverted the expedition to occupy HELIOS One. Her parents—a paladin and a scribe—both died fighting the NCR, leaving Elijah as her guardian. She describes him as a "wizard with technology" and credits him with nurturing her technical aptitude. Her former partner Christine Royce left the Brotherhood, defying procreation expectations, while Veronica stayed behind, unable to abandon her community despite recognizing its stagnation. She openly clashed with Elder McNamara's permanent lockdown, arguing the Brotherhood's original mission of controlling technology had devolved into purposeless isolation. She frequently visits the 188 Trading Post to scavenge and observe how other Mojave groups adapt, seeking solutions the Brotherhood refuses to pursue.
topic_desc_basic: Veronica is a Brotherhood of Steel Scribe assigned to the Mojave chapter, operating out of the Hidden Valley Bunker and frequently visiting the 188 Trading Post to trade and scavenge. She traveled to the Mojave as a child with her parents under Father Elijah's leadership, originally bound for Hoover Dam before Elijah diverted the group to occupy HELIOS One instead. Both of her parents were killed fighting the New California Republic, after which Elijah became her mentor and guardian, nurturing her fascination with technology. She was away from HELIOS One when the NCR seized it, and the survivors retreated underground under Elder McNamara's permanent lockdown, a policy Veronica openly opposed out of fear that isolationism would doom the Brotherhood to extinction.
tags: 188 trading post,brotherhood isolationism critic,brotherhood of steel scribe,christine royce relationship,father elijah mentor,helios one battle,hidden valley bunker,mojave brotherhood decline

topic_desc: Yes Man represents Benny's ambitious scheme to seize Mr. House's technological empire. Originally a standard PDQ-88b securitron, he was disabled by a pulse grenade and recovered by Benny's Chairmen. Followers of the Apocalypse member Emily Ortal reprogrammed him in exchange for access to Mr. House's secrets, creating an AI incapable of refusing orders or withholding information from anyone. Yes Man mined House's databases, discovering the platinum chip's delivery routes, which enabled Benny to ambush the Courier at Goodsprings Cemetery. After Benny's downfall, Yes Man transfers his allegiance to the Courier, offering full control over the Strip's securitron network. His plan involves upgrading securitrons to Mk II status via the platinum chip, securing the El Dorado Substation's power, and ultimately expelling both the NCR and Legion from the Mojave. Following the Hoover Dam battle, Yes Man discovers code fragments in House's mainframe that make him "a little more assertive," addressing concerns about his unconditional compliance.
topic_desc_basic: Yes Man is a reprogrammed PDQ-88b securitron that serves as Benny's assistant in New Vegas. Originally a standard securitron working for Mr. House, he was damaged by a pulse grenade and recovered by Benny, who had Followers of the Apocalypse member Emily Ortal reprogram him. The reprogramming made Yes Man incapable of refusing any order or withholding information from anyone, making his name a literal job description. Benny intended to install Yes Man's AI onto the Lucky 38 mainframe to seize control of all securitrons on the Strip.

topic_desc: Vault 8 served as one of Vault-Tec's control vaults, functioning without any experimental parameters. Two years after the Great War, its doors opened and residents used a Garden of Eden Creation Kit to establish Vault City. The vault's three levels include medical facilities staffed by Doctor Troy, storage areas containing spare water chips originally intended for Vault 13, and a command center with the overseer's chamber and water processing computer. The vault's nuclear reactor governs Vault City's capacity for expansion. By the time of the Chosen One's visit, Vault City had developed into a segregated settlement with strict citizenship requirements, reflecting the vault dwellers' isolationist tendencies and technological superiority over surrounding wasteland communities.
topic_desc_basic: Vault 8 was a control vault that opened two years after the Great War. Using a GECK, its inhabitants established Vault City around it. The vault contains three levels including medical facilities, storage areas, and a command center. It is powered by a nuclear reactor that governs the city's capacity for expansion.
tags: geck usage,nuclear reactor power,spare water chips,vault 8 control vault,vault city settlement
editorial_note: Vault 8 appears in Fallout 2; referenced in New Vegas context via TTW and lore.

topic_desc: Construction of Vault 92 began in May 2062 and completed in 2068, designed for 245 occupants. Overseer Richard Rubin implemented Vault-Tec's White Noise Mind Suggestion Combat Experimentation after sealing on October 23, 2077. Professor John Malleus assisted with the technical implementation, initially unaware that Rubin had extended white noise emitters beyond recording studios into living quarters. The experiments induced trance-like states with near-100% suggestion effectiveness, but caused progressive neurological damage leading to psychosis. Within months, over 30% of the population went insane, resulting in approximately 35 deaths. Malleus eventually discovered Rubin's deception and attempted to confront him. The vault also suffered structural deterioration from nearby underground water sources, eventually flooding after maintenance crews perished.
topic_desc_basic: Vault 92 was a Vault-Tec facility in the Capital Wasteland northwest of Old Olney. It recruited the world's finest musicians under the pretense of preserving musical talent. In reality, Overseer Richard Rubin conducted white noise experiments to implant combat suggestions in residents. The experiment caused widespread insanity and violence, killing most inhabitants.
tags: capital wasteland vault,combat suggestion experiment,musical talent vault,richard rubin overseer,vault 92 white noise

topic_desc: Vault 106's experiment involved releasing psychoactive drugs into the air filtration system ten days after sealing, with the Overseer fully aware that residents would become test subjects. Security personnel were ordered to dismiss concerns about unusual odors as filtration irregularities. The drugs caused persistent hallucinations, with affected residents eventually becoming violent Insane Survivors clad in Vault 106 jumpsuits. By 2277, the drugs remain active in the air system, producing blue-tinted hallucinations in anyone entering. Survivors attempted to escape by blowing through the vault walls, evidenced by skeletons and a Mini Nuke in a cave area. The vault contains a Science Bobblehead and various skill books among its ruined corridors.
topic_desc_basic: Vault 106 is a Vault-Tec vault in the Capital Wasteland, located southeast of Arefu. Ten days after the doors sealed, psychoactive drugs were released into the air filtration system as part of the vault experiment. The Overseer instructed security to lie about the unusual conditions. By 2277, the vault is destroyed and inhabited by Insane Survivors, with drugs still circulating.
tags: air filtration drugs,capital wasteland vault,hallucination experiment,insane survivors,vault 106 psychoactive drugs

topic_desc: Construction of Vault 108 began in March 2061 and was cut short in December 2069. Designed for 475 residents over 38 years, the vault's experiment deliberately left most positions unassigned for the Overseer to fill. The primary power supply was engineered to fail after 20 years, with an insufficient backup geo-thermal system. Overseer Brody Jones was chosen specifically because medical tests indicated a rare cancer would kill him within three years, creating a leadership crisis. The vault was stocked with triple the normal defensive weaponry and lacked entertainment facilities. Scientists conducted extensive cloning experiments on a subject named Gary, producing at least 54 clones. Each successive clone exhibited increasing hostility toward non-clones, with Gary 54 injuring staff. By the time of the Lone Wanderer's arrival, only hostile Gary clones and creatures remained.
topic_desc_basic: Vault 108 is a Vault-Tec vault in the Capital Wasteland, south of Canterbury Commons. Its experiment involved leaving all standard positions unfilled except three named roles, with a primary power supply designed to fail in 20 years. The Overseer, Brody Jones, was selected for his genetic predisposition to a rare cancer. Scientists also conducted cloning experiments, repeatedly cloning a man named Gary.
tags: brody jones overseer,capital wasteland vault,gary clones,power failure experiment,vault 108 cloning experiment

topic_desc: Vault-Tec Corporation operated under the government's classified Project Safehouse, protected by the New Amended Espionage Act. The multi-billion dollar corporation acquired laboratories, bought out competitors, and established headquarters in Los Angeles and Washington, D.C. Vault-Tec University in Morgantown trained its top executives and scientists. The company constructed over 100 vaults, some built in secret with numbers omitted from public records. While a small contingent of control vaults functioned as advertised, the majority featured unique experimental scenarios designed to test occupants under specific circumstances. The Enclave was involved in the planning stages, describing the program as "a social experiment on a grand scale." Vault-Tec equipment was often faulty—water chips were prone to failure, and shipping errors sometimes switched water chips and GECK deliveries. The company authorized its private security to use lethal force during admission protocols. Vault-Tec promoted its shelters through billboards, newspaper advertisements, corporate PR events, and a large exposition at the Museum of Technology in Washington, D.C. Employees received the Vault-Tec Employee Handbook, which governed all procedures down to bathroom break time limits.
topic_desc_basic: Vault-Tec Corporation was a pre-War defense corporation that designed and built a network of underground bunkers known as vaults across the United States and Canada. The company operated as early as 2031 and was the largest corporation in the country. Vault-Tec marketed vaults as shelters to protect citizens from nuclear war, but many vaults were secretly designed as social experiments. The company's mascots were Vault Boy and Vault Girl.
tags: pre-war defense contractor,project safehouse,social experiment program,vault construction,vault-tec corporation

topic_desc: The vault experiments were conceived during the planning stages of vault construction, with the Enclave describing the program as "a social experiment on a grand scale" using "a unique set of circumstances designed to test the occupants." Experimental scenarios varied widely: some vaults lacked sufficient food synthesizers, some housed only men, and others were designed to open after only six months. Scientists at Hawthorne Medical Laboratories, a Vault-Tec division, attempted to create hybrid humans in Vault 4 using radioactive resistant species. Not all vaults were completed before the Great War, and some sealed without their intended inhabitants. Others were constructed in secret, their numbers omitted from public record. The 17 control vaults were designed to function properly, preserving segments of society for reasons known only to the secretive elements behind the project. According to rumors, these elements sought to cause or hasten the Great War to see their vision realized. Vault life varied dramatically depending on whether residents occupied a control vault or an experimental one. Inhabitants were required to sign numerous forms before entry, including liability waivers, organ donation invoices, and rights revocation charters. Vault-Tec provided all clothing, bedding, and accommodations, and personal belongings were subject to review by authorized hermetics technicians.
topic_desc_basic: Vault-Tec built over 100 vaults across the United States and Canada as part of the Societal Preservation Program. Despite the program's stated goal of protecting citizens from nuclear war, a secretive shadow government subverted the project. Of the vaults, 17 were control vaults that operated as advertised, while 105 were experimental vaults with unique circumstances designed to test how inhabitants would react and behave under specific conditions.
tags: control vaults,enclave social experiment,societal preservation program,vault experiments,vault-tec testing

topic_desc: The G.E.C.K. was designed to ease the process of harnessing the post-nuclear wasteland for vault dwellers emerging from their shelters. Developed by Stanislaus Braun, the kit represented Vault-Tec's vision for post-War reconstruction. The matter-energy replicators within the kit were advertised as capable of creating food and basic items needed for building new environments. The inclusion of atmospheric chemical stabilizers and water purifiers suggests the device was intended to render contaminated surroundings habitable. The reading material—drawn from the Library of Congress and encyclopedic sources—was provided to give survivors access to accumulated human knowledge. Shipping errors during vault preparation sometimes resulted in G.E.C.K. deliveries being switched with water chips, meaning some vaults never received their intended kits. The G.E.C.K. was a critical resource for any vault dweller community intending to rebuild on the surface, combining terraforming technology with survival essentials in a single portable case. Its creation by Future-Tec, a Vault-Tec division, reflects the parent corporation's involvement in both shelter construction and post-War planning, though the extent to which vault dwellers were informed of the kit's existence varied.
topic_desc_basic: The Garden of Eden Creation Kit, or G.E.C.K., is a terraforming device created by Future-Tec, a division of Vault-Tec Corporation. Developed by Stanislaus Braun, the kit was packed into a briefcase and advertised as "the resource for rebuilding civilization after the bomb." It contained seed and soil supplements, a cold fusion generator, matter-energy replicators, atmospheric chemical stabilizers, water purifiers, and reading material including selections from the Library of Congress and a complete set of encyclopedias.
tags: future-tec division,geck terraforming device,post-war reconstruction,stanislaus braun invention,vault-tec technology

topic_desc: The United States government began the Pan-Immunity Virion Project in 2073 to counteract biological weapons, aiming to alter DNA so it would resist viral infection. By March 2075, the virion was renamed FEV, and Major Barnett ordered experiments focused on the virus's quad-helix structure, which granted subjects immunity to infection and radiation beyond expectations. Testing progressed through flatworms, insects, mice, dogs, and chimpanzees, with abnormal growth rates and increased brain activity noted in all subjects. In January 2077, research transferred to the Mariposa Military Base for human trials. When the security team discovered the inhumane nature of the work, Roger Maxson took charge, interrogated and executed scientists, and abandoned the base—an act that founded the Brotherhood of Steel. Post-War, Richard Grey fell into FEV vats at Mariposa and mutated into the Master, who sought radiation-free humans to transform into super mutants using FEV-2. The Enclave isolated the virus's most toxic elements to create FEV Curling-13, a lethal agent targeting only humans. In the Capital Wasteland, the Enclave under President John Henry Eden developed a modified FEV intended to contaminate the water supply through Project Purity, which specifically targeted immune systems on a cellular level. Vault 87 also utilized modified FEV as part of its Evolutionary Experimentation Program, transforming inhabitants into super mutants.
topic_desc_basic: Forced Evolutionary Virus, or FEV, is a pathogen developed before the Great War by West Tek in an attempt to create super-soldiers. The virus is not airborne and only transfers via injection or direct physical contact. FEV copies DNA patterns, attempting to correct the DNA of the infected individual. If the subject lacks pre-existing radiation damage, the virus increases muscle and brain mass but causes memory loss and sterility.
tags: enclave biological weapon,fev mutation,forced evolutionary virus,super soldier project,west tek pathogen

topic_desc: The Pip-Boy 3000 was developed by RobCo Industries before the Great War as a personal information processor for Vault dwellers and military personnel. The 3000A variant, an older model within the A series, is commonly found strapped to the left forearm of wasteland inhabitants who have acquired them from Vault stocks or scavenged supplies. The device integrates a Geiger counter for radiation detection, a radio receiver capable of picking up wasteland broadcasts, and a display screen that can be pushed to over-bright mode, functioning as a 360-degree illumination source in darkened environments. Files can be transferred from compatible terminals directly to the Pip-Boy. The device is powered by a fission battery, as confirmed by Christine Royce of the Circle of Steel. Father Elijah, the former elder of the Brotherhood of Steel chapter at HELIOS One, demonstrated that the Pip-Boy 3000 can be hacked remotely, dismissing it as a piece of RobCo trash. A variant known as the Pimp-Boy 3 Billion exists, obtainable through dealings with Mick, an arms dealer operating in Freeside. Vault radio broadcasts remind dwellers that proper cleaning and maintenance will ensure the device's operation for future generations.
topic_desc_basic: The Pip-Boy 3000 is a pre-War electronic Personal Information Processor manufactured by RobCo Industries. Worn on the left forearm, this multifunction device displays the wearer's vital statistics, area maps, inventory, and item properties. It includes a built-in Geiger counter, radio receiver, and a screen that can be set to over-bright mode to serve as a makeshift flashlight. The 3000A model is an older variant of the A series. Display color preferences include amber, blue, green, and white.
tags: fission battery powered,geiger counter radio,pimp-boy 3 billion,pip-boy 3000a model,robco personal processor,wrist-mounted device

topic_desc: The Vault-Tec Assisted Targeting System, known as V.A.T.S., combines the Pip-Boy's sensors and computing power with automated combat analysis. Developed before the Great War, it identifies hostile targets, evaluates specific anatomical regions, and helps the wearer plan a sequence of precise attacks more quickly than unaided observation would allow. The resulting tactical assessment can draw attention to an exposed limb, a weapon-bearing arm, or another vulnerable area while reducing reliance on reflex alone. V.A.T.S. is integrated into the Pip-Boy interface rather than carried as a separate weapon, allowing information from the wearer's surroundings to feed directly into its targeting display. Its creation demonstrates that Vault-Tec's research extended beyond shelters into personal defense and military applications. The similarity between its acronym and the Mariposa FEV vats has encouraged speculation, but no proven technical connection between those programs is known.
topic_desc_basic: The Vault-Tec Assisted Targeting System, usually called V.A.T.S., is a pre-War combat-assistance technology associated with the Pip-Boy. It analyzes nearby threats, highlights specific anatomical targets, and helps its user plan precise attacks under pressure. The system reflects Vault-Tec's work in personal survival and military technology beyond its vault program.

topic_desc: The Stealth Boy was invented by Robert Mayflower and entered production through RobCo Industries as a wrist-mounted personal stealth device, designated the 3001 variant. The device functions by generating a modulating refraction field that transmits reflected light from one side of the wearer's body to the opposite side, effectively bending visible light around the user and rendering them almost invisible to the unaided eye. Some Stealth Boys were developed through reverse engineering of captured Chinese Stealth Armor technology. After the Great War, Doctor Henry conducted research into the Mark II variant, which was intended to reduce power consumption. However, the Mark II's modulating field produced unintended permanent neurochemical changes in users, including schizophrenia and other psychological conditions. These effects proved especially devastating among the Nightkin, a faction of super mutants who relied heavily on Stealth Boys for their operations. Chewed variants of the device have been found in locations such as Charleston Cave in the Mojave Wasteland, suggesting deterioration or misuse over time. The Enclave also pursued improvements, with scientists developing a Mark III variant using Chinese schematics, drastically lowering power consumption rates compared to the Mark II while abandoning the wrist-mounted form factor.
topic_desc_basic: The Stealth Boy is a wrist-mounted personal stealth device invented by Robert Mayflower and produced by RobCo Industries. The 3001 variant generates a modulating field that transmits reflected light from one side of an object to another, rendering the wearer nearly invisible to the untrained eye. The effect lasts for a limited duration. Post-War research by Doctor Henry revealed that the device's modulating field can cause permanent neurochemical changes, including schizophrenia, particularly among Nightkin super mutants.

topic_desc: The Vertibird represents a class of vertical-lift aircraft developed by the United States military in the years leading up to the Great War. These advanced rotorcraft function as both transport vehicles and gunships, distinguished by their fuel-powered engines and formidable offensive capabilities, which include Gatling lasers, miniguns, and missile launchers. The XVB02 prototype was the culmination of pre-War vertical flight research and was scheduled to enter full military service in 2085, though the nuclear exchange of 2077 disrupted this timeline. Despite the devastation of the Great War, Vertibird technology survived and has been maintained by certain post-War factions. The Enclave, descendants of pre-War government and military personnel, have utilized Vertibirds extensively for troop deployment, supply runs, and close air support operations. In the Capital Wasteland, Enclave Vertibirds have been observed conducting operations around 2277, deploying soldiers and engaging ground targets. In the Mojave Wasteland, Vertibird sightings have been reported around 2281, associated with Enclave remnants and their ongoing activities. The aircraft's durability and versatility have made it one of the most significant pieces of surviving pre-War military hardware, granting its operators a substantial tactical advantage over factions limited to ground transportation.
topic_desc_basic: The Vertibird is a type of vertical-lift aircraft developed by the United States military before the Great War. Powered by fuel, these advanced helicopters serve as transport and gunship platforms. They are equipped with offensive weaponry including Gatling lasers, miniguns, and missile launchers. A prototype designated XVB02 was scheduled to enter full military service in 2085. Vertibirds remain operational in the post-War wasteland, used by factions such as the Enclave.

topic_desc: Project Purity was an ambitious attempt to build a large-scale water purifier capable of filtering radiation from the sealed-off Tidal Basin at the Jefferson Memorial. James and Catherine led a team of like-minded scientists, and Elder Owyn Lyons provided a permanent Brotherhood of Steel garrison with sentry guns to maintain a safe perimeter against super mutant attacks. The team found a purification method that worked but was horribly inefficient, and mounting losses strained relations with the Brotherhood. Catherine's death during childbirth on July 13, 2258 precipitated the project's collapse. James withdrew entirely, fleeing with his child to Vault 101, and Lyons pulled his troops out, leaving the scientists to fend for themselves. Madison Li and the survivors salvaged what they could and moved to Rivet City. Years later, James discovered references to the Garden of Eden Creation Kit in Vault 101 records and returned to restart the project. The Enclave under Colonel Autumn seized the memorial by force, demanding control of the facility. James sacrificed himself by flooding the control chamber with lethal radiation. Lyons' Brotherhood ultimately used Liberty Prime to break through Enclave defenses, and the purifier was activated. Elder Lyons ordered the water distributed free to all major settlements, though the Brotherhood struggled with funding and resources, forcing Scribe Bigsley to quietly sell water to sustain operations.
topic_desc_basic: Project Purity was a water purification initiative at the Jefferson Memorial in the Capital Wasteland, founded by James and Catherine with support from a Brotherhood of Steel garrison. It aimed to purify the irradiated Tidal Basin and provide millions of gallons of drinkable water. After Catherine's death in childbirth in 2258, James abandoned the project and fled to Vault 101. The remaining scientists relocated to Rivet City.

topic_desc: Hoover Dam, sometimes called the Old World Wall, was one of the most substantial sources of electrical power in the pre-War American Southwest, protected by anti-aircraft weapons. When the Great War struck, Mr. House's networked mainframes and laser systems kept the dam in almost untouched condition alongside much of Las Vegas. The plant sat abandoned for nearly two centuries until the Followers of the Apocalypse noted its continued existence as early as 2170. In 2274, NCR scouts arrived during the Mojave Campaign, prompting Mr. House to act. The Mojave Brotherhood of Steel had planned to claim the dam but was sidetracked at HELIOS One. The Treaty of New Vegas gave the NCR ninety-five percent of the dam's output while preserving Vegas sovereignty. Within a year, NCR engineers had the dam running at fifty percent capacity. The head engineer, Mike Lawson, reported that six turbines once ran but only four still functioned. In 2277, the Legion under the Malpais Legate attempted to seize the dam but was defeated when Chief Hanlon orchestrated a tactical retreat through Boulder City, detonating pre-placed explosives to trap the Legion's elite forces. Colonel Cassandra Moore and General Lee Oliver subsequently fortified the dam with a significant military presence and civilian contractors to prepare for a second Legion assault.
topic_desc_basic: Hoover Dam is a pre-War hydroelectric dam on the Colorado River that impounds Lake Mead, surviving the Great War largely intact thanks to Mr. House's defensive systems. The NCR occupied it in 2274 during their Mojave Campaign. The Treaty of New Vegas allocated ninety-five percent of the dam's power output to the NCR in exchange for recognizing Vegas sovereignty. Within a year the dam ran at fifty percent capacity.
tags: colorado river dam,first battle of hoover,hydroelectric power output,ncr mojave campaign,treaty of new vegas,turbine capacity

topic_desc: ARCHIMEDES II was commissioned by Poseidon Energy, which maintained behind-closed-doors relations with elements of the United States military that would become the Enclave. The system is an orbital laser platform tied to the HELIOS One solar collection arrays in Nevada. It can be triggered by triangulating between a beacon at HELIOS One and a targeting device called Euclid's C-Finder, allowing the satellite to precisely mark a point on the ground for bombardment. Three laser beams converge on the target, followed by a massive blue laser from orbit. The Brotherhood of Steel under Elder Elijah occupied HELIOS One and discovered the ARCHIMEDES II secret, but in 2276 the NCR laid siege during Operation: Sunburst and expelled the Brotherhood, seizing the facility. Ignacio Rivas, a Follower of the Apocalypse embedded at HELIOS One, has actively kept the NCR ignorant of the weapon's true nature, believing some things are best left buried with the old world. The NCR hired an incompetent conman known as Fantastic to manage the power plant, and the internal security systems remain too dangerous for soldiers to penetrate fully, though it is likely only a matter of time before the Archimedes mainframe is reached.
topic_desc_basic: ARCHIMEDES II is an energy-based orbital artillery satellite developed by Poseidon Energy at HELIOS One in Nevada. The Brotherhood of Steel discovered it under Elder Elijah, but lost HELIOS One to the NCR in 2276 during Operation: Sunburst. The NCR has been unable to unlock its secrets, partly because a Follower of the Apocalypse named Ignacio Rivas has deliberately kept them in the dark, fearing the weapon could fall into the wrong hands.

topic_desc: The REPCONN Test Site sits in a large valley accessible through a single canyon west of Novac. Before the war, REPCONN was finalizing a merger with RobCo Industries when a waste spill occurred around the time RobCo representatives were to visit. Steve Reynolds, the Launch Facility Project Manager, was blamed by Senior Engineer Martin Neimeyer, who cited Reynolds' overworking and under-compensation of employees as the cause, while Reynolds blamed Neimeyer. The facility features a reinforced checkpoint, a roundabout with a Delta IX rocket statue, research laboratories at the top, an assembly hall where rockets were prepared, and a basement connecting to the launch dome. Post-war, the Bright Brotherhood ghouls took refuge in the research laboratories, intending to undertake what they call the Great Journey into space using the facility's rockets. Chris Haversam, a human who believes himself a ghoul, serves as their engineer. Nightkin led by Davison occupied the basement, searching for a shipment of Stealth Boys whose records indicate two shipments were received and returned to the manufacturer, with five units missing due to workplace misbehavior. Feral ghouls escaped containment and wandered toward Novac, alarming local residents. The Bright Brotherhood's outer defenses were insufficient to stop the nightkin, who punched through and left dead Brotherhood members in their wake.
topic_desc_basic: The REPCONN Test Site is a former rocket testing facility west of Novac, built around a rocket launch dome. Before the war, REPCONN was merging with RobCo Industries when a waste spill weakened its position. Post-war, the Bright Brotherhood, a group of ghouls led by Jason Bright seeking to travel into space on rockets, occupied the facility. Nightkin under Davison also moved in, searching for a shipment of Stealth Boys stored in the basement.

topic_desc: Sierra Madre vending machines were created at Big MT's Y-0 Research Center and commissioned by Frederick Sinclair, who bankrupted himself funding the project after witnessing the technology at a World's Fair exhibit. Sinclair struck a deal with Big MT executives to use the Villa as a proving ground for experimental technologies. The machines were designed not merely as vending devices but as emergency dispensers capable of supplying food, chems, security equipment, and maintenance tools in the event of nuclear catastrophe. Certain supplies were restricted by dispenser codes issued only to trained professionals and doctors. To Sinclair, the machines represented self-sufficiency for the Sierra Madre. To his employees, however, the machines felt like a company store—they received a modest amount of chips with each paycheck and could barely afford anything, especially given Sinclair's ban on all other vending machines. The Great War and the Sierra Madre's isolation left these as the only known surviving examples of the underlying technology. Around 2281, Father Elijah, a rogue elder of the Brotherhood of Steel, recognized the machines' potential as unlimited sources of food, supplies, medical assistance, ammunition, and even currency. The machines use Sierra Madre chips as batteries, drawing on alloys and raw materials within the chips to assemble dispensed items. According to Dean Domino, similar vending technology was common before the war.
topic_desc_basic: Pre-War devices developed at Big MT's Y-0 Research Center, Sierra Madre vending machines dispense food, supplies, and other items in exchange for Sierra Madre chips. Frederick Sinclair bankrolled their development after seeing them at a World's Fair exhibit, intending them as emergency dispensers for surviving a nuclear holocaust. They remain functional in the ruins of the Sierra Madre.
