topic_desc: Nuka-Cola entered the beverage market in 2044 after two years of experimentation by John-Caleb Bradberton. Its unique taste resulted from a combination of seventeen fruit essences balanced to enhance classic cola flavor, and it contained 120% of the recommended daily allowance of sugar. Within a year it was available nationwide, and by 2067 a vending machine stood on almost every street in America. The iconic rocket-shaped bottle replaced an earlier curved blue glass design after a rival corporation successfully sued for patent infringement, resulting in increased sales. Numerous flavor variants followed, including cherry, grape, and orange. The final variant, Nuka-Cola Quantum, was created in October 2076 using an isotope of strontium-90, the product of a three-year research program. Marketed as fortified with vitaminerals and health tonics, frequent consumption could cause addiction and splitting headaches. The Nuka-Cola Corporation aggressively competed with rivals, launching Nuka-Cola Wild to counter Sunset Sarsaparilla and hiring mercenaries to sabotage Vim! Pop operations. The company also purchased existing soda brands, rebranding them as new Nuka-Cola flavors. In the post-War world, Nuka-Cola remains the soft drink of choice for many wastelanders, and its bottle caps function as the standard currency across the wasteland.
topic_desc_basic: Nuka-Cola is a soft drink invented by John-Caleb Bradberton in 2044 and produced by the Nuka-Cola Corporation. It dominated the American soda market, containing 17 fruit essences and 120% of the recommended daily sugar allowance. Its signature rocket-shaped bottle replaced an earlier curved blue design. Post-War, Nuka-Cola bottle caps serve as the most common wasteland currency.

topic_desc: Bottle caps emerged as the dominant post-War currency due to several practical advantages: they are difficult to counterfeit, the total number in circulation is relatively small, and they can be traded virtually anywhere. The Crimson Caravan Company has sought to control all bottle cap production to prevent mass production and inflation, maintaining the currency's stability by replacing worn and damaged caps. An advertising campaign by the Nuka-Cola Corporation once allowed the exchange of bottle caps with robotic vendors at the Whitespring Resort following the release of Nuka-Cola Quantum. In the Mojave Wasteland, bottle caps circulate alongside NCR dollars and Legion denarius, all recognized as legal tender by caravan companies and on the New Vegas Strip. Merchants in the Mojave also accept nonstandard variants such as Sunset Sarsaparilla bottle caps. The Sink Central Intelligence Unit was programmed by Doctor Mobius to accept bottle caps, either for debugging purposes or as part of his speculation concerning post-holocaust economic systems. The widespread use of caps is tied to their ubiquity as Nuka-Cola bottle caps, the most commonly encountered type.
topic_desc_basic: Bottle caps are the standard currency across the wasteland, valued because they are difficult to counterfeit and exist in limited numbers. They can be traded nearly anywhere. In the Mojave, bottle caps, NCR dollars, and Legion denarius are all accepted as legal tender by caravan companies and on the New Vegas Strip. Mojave merchants also accept Sunset Sarsaparilla caps.

topic_desc: The New California Republic issues its own paper currency, the NCR dollar, as part of its development into a large nation with formal institutions including a military, courts, and representative government. The currency is printed and circulated in several denominations—$5, $20, and $100—and is valued at approximately half the equivalent of bottle caps. The notes are issued by the Republic Reserve Bank located in Angel's Boneyard, and the signature of Treasurer John Michael Henderson appears on the front of all notes. In the Mojave Wasteland, NCR dollars are accepted as legal tender alongside bottle caps and Legion denarius by caravan companies and on the New Vegas Strip. The Republic's economy is supported by trade routes and merchant companies such as the Crimson Caravan, the Far Go Traders, and the Gun Runners. The NCR's economic strength has historically depended on gold reserves, and landowners and Brahmin Barons within the Stockmen's Association utilize bribery to influence their stake in the economy. The NCR also competes with other political powers for valuable trading assets such as gold ore from Redding's mines.
topic_desc_basic: The NCR dollar is the official currency of the New California Republic, printed in denominations of $5, $20, and $100. It is valued at roughly half the equivalent of bottle caps. Notes are issued by the Republic Reserve Bank in Angel's Boneyard and bear the signature of Treasurer John Michael Henderson.

topic_desc: The Legion denarius follows the silver currency of the ancient Roman Empire that Caesar used as a model for his state. The coin is minted from scavenged silver and bears Caesar's profile with the words Caesar Dictator, while Magnum Chasma appears on the reverse. Its gold counterpart, the aureus, is worth twenty-five denarii, preserving the exchange ratio used by Rome. A denarius normally trades for about four bottle caps in the Mojave because merchants recognize the value of its metal even when they reject Legion rule. Damaged coins may be accepted for less, and some have been repurposed as metal shot for improvised ammunition. New Vegas casinos exchange winnings for Legion money at established rates, and denarii also serve as pieces in Caravan. The coin therefore circulates beyond Legion territory despite the regime's hostility toward outside culture and independent commerce.
topic_desc_basic: The denarius is one of two forms of currency used by Caesar's Legion, the other being the more valuable aureus. The coin bears Caesar's profile on its face, inscribed "Caesar Dictator," with "Magnum Chasma" on the reverse. It is minted from scavenged silver and is the more commonly encountered of the two Legion coins. In the Mojave Wasteland, it is accepted as payment owing to its precious metal content, with a typical exchange rate of four bottle caps to one denarius.

topic_desc: The Crimson Caravan Company exemplifies the scale and ruthlessness of wasteland caravan trade. Established in the Hub over 130 years ago, it became one of New California's most influential merchant houses, holding two of six seats on the Hub's Council. Its early success stemmed from a policy of accepting any job, no matter the danger, and employing only experienced guards paid six hundred bottle caps per run. With the formation of the New California Republic, the company became a key driver of the Republic's economy, securing lucrative contracts to supply military-grade weaponry and equipment. The company's organizational structure relies on fixed-duration work contracts: employees receive food, water, and quarters but forfeit wages if they leave early, and non-compete clauses can restrict future employment. In the Mojave, executive manager Alice McLafferty oversees operations from a New Vegas branch hampered by the incompetent Henry Jamison, installed through pressure from the Jamison family of Redding. McLafferty upholds the company tradition of undermining competitors through sabotage, industrial espionage, and buyouts, including an agreement with the Van Graffs to eliminate rivals. Competitors include the Gun Runners, Cassidy Caravans, the Far Go Traders, and the Mormon traders of New Canaan. Following the destruction of the NCR's gold reserves, Crimson Caravan and other Hub merchants reportedly conspired to reintroduce the bottle cap as the standard wasteland currency.
topic_desc_basic: Caravan trade is the lifeblood of commerce across the wasteland, with heavily armed convoys of pack brahmin carrying goods between settlements along established routes. The Crimson Caravan Company, founded in the Hub over a century ago, is among the largest such operations, known for taking any job regardless of risk. Caravaneers wear light leather armor and carry firearms for protection. Competition between trading houses is fierce, involving sabotage, espionage, and buyouts alongside open commerce.

topic_desc: Radiation is measured in units called rads or sieverts, and its effects escalate with cumulative exposure. Early symptoms include nausea, mild vomiting, and fatigue, progressing to persistent vomiting, impaired recovery, violent hemorrhaging, hair loss, and skin sloughing. At the most severe stages, victims suffer gastrointestinal bleeding, severe diarrhea, intense agony, and death. Gamma rays comprise the ionizing radiation responsible for these effects. Centuries after the Great War, areas directly struck by nuclear weapons remain highly irradiated, with radioactive hotspots persisting for hundreds of years. The Glow and the Glowing Sea are notable examples of such enduring contamination. Radiation also drives mutation at the genetic level, producing enlarged versions of pre-War species such as radscorpions, geckos, spore plants, and brahmin. In humans, radiation can cause sterility or transform individuals into ghouls, some of whom become feral and emit radiation while losing body heat. The Children of Atom have developed a religious reverence for radiation. Medical countermeasures include Auto-Docs, inoculations, decontamination arches, and system flushes. Pip-Boy units and Wattz Electronics C-Radz Geiger counters detect ambient radiation levels. Radiation suits offer varying degrees of protection. Notably, microwaves such as those emitted by the Microwave Emitter are non-ionizing and do not cause irradiation, though they can boil water inside cells and cause severe burns.
topic_desc_basic: Radiation, sometimes called the "phantom death," is a tasteless, odorless lingering danger present throughout the wasteland, caused by nuclear detonations and toxic waste. Measured in rads, exposure causes nausea, vomiting, anemia, fatigue, hair and tooth loss, hemorrhaging, and death. Some life forms have adapted, and radiation can cause mutations in creatures and humans, including the transformation of some humans into ghouls. Geiger counters, radiation suits, and decontamination arches help mitigate exposure.

topic_desc: Founded by Robert House on June 25, 2042, RobCo Industries grew into one of the pre-War world's foremost robotics and software corporations. Its product line included the Eyebot, Protectron, and Sentry Bot platforms, as well as the Stealth Boy Model 3001 personal stealth device. RobCo invested in public exhibits, including a joint exposition with General Atomics at the Museum of Technology in Washington, D.C. The company pursued aggressive acquisition strategies, purchasing REPCONN Aerospace between 2075 and 2076 after a year of share buying, despite resistance from REPCONN's longtime CEO. House then used the acquisition to run a weapons research program for Colonel Moretti of the U.S. military, repurposing REPCONN's plasma rocket propulsion system. RobCo also acquired H&H Tools Factory, which had been part of the inheritance stolen from House by his brother Anthony. RobCo's influence extended into vault infrastructure: Vault-Tec selected RobCo Pip-Boy models for vault dwellers, and RobCo contributed military-grade defensive turret systems to Vault 79's construction. The Brotherhood of Steel's Mojave chapter has noted the existence of RobCo vaults in the Mojave Desert. The Semi-Autonomous Immobile Weapon Platform turret system was developed at the RobCo Research Center. In cooperation with General Atomics, RobCo was contracted to collaborate on Liberty Prime, intended to liberate Anchorage, Alaska, with General Chase publicly confirming the project as a superweapon for U.S. dominance on the Alaskan front. RobCo also partnered with the Nuka-Cola Corporation for the RobCo Battlezone in Nuka-World's Galactic Zone and participated in the Watoga initiative with Atomic Mining Services and General Atomics International to build a "city of the future."

topic_desc: General Atomics International was a globe-spanning pre-War corporation whose products ranged from nuclear reactors and household software to laser technology and industrial robots. Its best-known machine was the Mister Handy, a floating domestic servant equipped with multiple tools; the military Mister Gutsy adapted the same basic design for combat. General Atomics also supplied nuclear backup systems for vaults and wave-particle diverters used in energy-weapon research. The company cooperated with RobCo and the United States Army on major robotics programs, including Liberty Prime and robobrain development. It publicly promoted automation as a complete answer to domestic, industrial, and administrative work, even experimenting with automated management systems. This broad portfolio left General Atomics machines and components scattered through homes, factories, laboratories, and military installations after the Great War.

topic_desc: Poseidon Energy was a major pre-War conglomerate with operations in oil, gasoline, refining, manufacturing, and electric power on both American coasts. Its national PoseidoNet system linked distant company facilities, while subsidiaries and affiliates pursued petroleum, nuclear, and solar energy. Poseidon also accepted military research contracts and developed experimental weapons. In the Mojave, its HELIOS One facility supported ARCHIMEDES, an orbital laser system, while ARCHIMEDES II could be directed using Euclid's C-Finder. topic_desc: West Tek was founded in 2002 and became one of the United States government's most important defense and biomedical contractors. Its engineers produced the first practical power-armor frame and the T-45 series, followed by work on the more capable T-51. In 2073, the company began the Pan-Immunity Virion Project to create broad protection against the New Plague and hostile biological weapons. Experiments soon revealed that the virion could act as a powerful mutagen. Under military direction it was renamed the Forced Evolutionary Virus, and research shifted from immunization toward deliberate alteration of living organisms. By 2077, Californian FEV staff and materials were being transferred to Mariposa Military Base despite objections to human testing. West Tek's combination of armor engineering and biological research left two enduring legacies: advanced protective technology and the virus responsible for many later wasteland mutations.

topic_desc: The Sunset Sarsaparilla Company was founded in 1918 around a sarsaparilla recipe said to have been left by a mysterious stranger. The story linked the drink to sunset and to a blue star stamped on certain bottle caps. Over the following decades, the beverage became well known across the western United States and sold especially strongly in the Southwest. The company later invested in RobCo automation for custodial work and regional distribution. A rumor that starred caps could be redeemed for a prize spread before the Great War. Rather than deny it, company managers promoted the story after it produced an enormous increase in sales, placing the Festus automaton in their headquarters to represent their cowboy-themed brand. The rival Nuka-Cola Corporation attempted to buy the company, but Sunset Sarsaparilla remained independent and its bottles, caps, machinery, and advertisements survived throughout the Mojave.

topic_desc: The Crimson Caravan Company's Mojave branch is a fortified trading compound southeast of Freeside's North Gate and near the New Vegas Medical Clinic. Alice McLafferty manages the operation. Its barracks house caravaneers and guards between journeys, while pack brahmin, a roadside store, workbenches, and a central office support regular trade across the region. The compound's layout reflects the practical needs of a caravan company: merchants require protected lodging, animal pens, repairs, supplies, and armed escorts before returning to dangerous roads. topic_desc: The Gun Runners began as a small Hub gang that settled in a factory in northeastern Los Angeles. Profits from selling captured and imported weapons convinced them to abandon ordinary gang activity and use the factory's machinery to manufacture arms. With pre-War schematics, scrap metal, and imported raw materials, they became skilled machinists and gunsmiths capable of producing military-grade weapons and ammunition. Their Mojave branch was established in 2155, and by 2281 the company operated throughout the American Southwest. The Gun Runners and Crimson Caravan became two of the NCR's oldest and most powerful merchant houses. Army contracts account for much of Gun Runner business in contested regions, and their weapons equip NCR troops and presidential guards. Their organization is spread among separate manufacturing and trading groups, with guarded brahmin caravans carrying valuable weapons between markets.

topic_desc: The Followers of the Apocalypse treat medicine as part of a wider humanitarian mission built around freely shared knowledge and resources. Their members provide medical services, education, agricultural instruction, and research intended to help communities survive without dependence on powerful governments. In the Mojave, Julie Farkas administers the Followers' Old Mormon Fort outpost. Its doctors and researchers care for refugees and other people around Freeside despite limited supplies. Because medicine scavenged from pre-War hospitals is finite, Followers study local flora, including barrel cacti, in search of treatments that communities can produce for themselves. Their work also extends to clean water, desert agriculture, and the repair of basic infrastructure, since disease and injury cannot be separated from living conditions. The organization accepts members according to their skills and expects knowledge to be used for public benefit rather than hoarded for profit or control.

topic_desc: The Codex is the central constitution of the Brotherhood of Steel, dating to the order's first decades under Roger Maxson. It sets out the Brotherhood's laws, doctrines, responsibilities, and core beliefs. Members who take the Oath of Fraternity swear to follow its commands and conduct themselves with honor; serious violations are judged by the Council of Elders. Different chapters interpret portions of the Codex in different ways, but all treat it as the foundation of Brotherhood identity. Scribes are responsible for preserving and updating it. The accompanying Scrolls record the lives of Brotherhood members, including their admission, character, battles, technology recoveries, promotions, reassignment, and death. Chapters are expected to synchronize these records with Lost Hills. An Elder may order a deserter or insubordinate member struck from the record, making the Codex both a rulebook and the Brotherhood's institutional memory.

topic_desc: Caesar's Legion grew from Edward Sallow's capture by the Blackfoot tribe in 2247. After teaching the Blackfoot new methods of warfare, Sallow helped them defeat or absorb seven neighboring tribes. He then crowned himself Caesar and systematically erased the identities of conquered peoples. Tribal tattoos were burned or scraped away, families were broken apart, and people from different tribes were forced together so their former loyalties would disappear. This process produced what Caesar called a single great tribe, modeled on his understanding of ancient Rome. Slavery is fundamental to that system rather than incidental to it. The Legion treats individuals as property or instruments whose value comes from labor, reproduction, warfare, or service to the state. Conquest therefore destroys both personal freedom and the cultures that might compete with loyalty to Caesar.

topic_desc: The New California Republic defines itself as a democratic nation governed by laws and elected institutions. Its five founding states joined by vote in 2189, growing from the settlement of Shady Sands into a republic spanning much of the American Southwest. NCR citizens have access to the court system and vote for representatives in the Hall of Congress. Those representatives form the legislature and select national leaders who guide the Republic's government. Citizenship therefore carries legal rights and political participation uncommon in much of the wasteland, along with obligations to a state that collects taxes, enforces laws, fields an army, and issues currency. The Republic formally opposes slavery and supports broad civil freedoms. In practice, distant communities may experience NCR rule through soldiers, officials, merchants, and expanding regulations before they see its promised security or representation, creating tension around annexation and citizenship.

topic_desc: Wasteland tribes are not a single culture. Each community may preserve its own language, symbols, family structures, history, and ways of surviving local conditions. The Blackfoot of Arizona illustrate both the strength and vulnerability of those identities. When Edward Sallow, Joshua Graham, and Bill Calhoun encountered them near the Grand Canyon, a translation failure contributed to the travelers' capture. Sallow learned that the Blackfoot were fighting seven other tribes and taught them tactics drawn from old military histories. Victory allowed the Blackfoot to defeat or assimilate their rivals, but Sallow then destroyed the cultures he had gathered. Tribal names and loyalties were replaced by the uniform identity of Caesar's Legion. Their story shows why dialect, custom, oral knowledge, tattoos, and kinship can be essential to a tribe's continuity—and why forced assimilation is a form of cultural destruction.

topic_desc: The Wasteland Survival Guide is a practical handbook written and published by Moira Brown with assistance from the Lone Wanderer. It gathers field-tested knowledge about finding food and medicine, recognizing wasteland creatures, and enduring the hazards of the post-War world. Rather than keeping that experience confined to one settlement, Moira arranged for the book to be distributed by travelers. Copies could therefore move with caravans and wanderers to communities far beyond the Capital Wasteland. The guide's importance lies in turning scattered experience into knowledge that ordinary people can carry, teach, and improve upon. A scavenger may know one safe route or useful plant, but a published survival guide can preserve many such lessons for readers who never met the original explorers. It represents the practical value of observation, documentation, and freely shared information in a dangerous world.

topic_desc: Ghoulification is a severe mutation caused by radiation exposure. During the process, a person's skin dries and flakes away, often leaving an appearance similar to extensive radiation burns. Hair and the nose may be lost, and the transition can take months. Survivors age far more slowly than ordinary humans, allowing some ghouls to live for centuries, but they become sterile. Further radiation generally does not harm them and may instead help their bodies recover. Ghoulification is not a reliable path to survival: some people deliberately exposed themselves in pursuit of longevity, while others died of radiation poisoning before any stable mutation occurred. Physical mutation does not by itself erase a person's intelligence, emotions, memories, or moral judgment. Some ghouls later become feral, but the cause and timing of that decline remain uncertain, and treating every ghoul as inevitably feral is prejudice rather than medical knowledge.
topic_desc_basic: Ghoulification is the mutation of a human after extreme radiation exposure. topic_desc: Super mutation occurs when a human is exposed to a strain of the Forced Evolutionary Virus. The resulting super mutant usually gains exceptional size, strength, endurance, and resistance to radiation and disease. Intelligence is not affected uniformly: results depend on the viral strain, the subject, and the conditions of exposure. The virus originated in West Tek's Pan-Immunity Virion research before the military redirected it toward human experimentation. Californian research was transferred to Mariposa Military Base in 2077, where vats and staff supported later experiments. The Master eventually used Mariposa FEV to create an organized mutant army. In the Capital Wasteland, Vault 87's Evolutionary Experimentation Program produced another population whose members continued growing as they aged and often raided settlements for humans to convert. These separate origins explain why super mutants differ in culture, intelligence, behavior, and physical development.
topic_desc_basic: Super mutants are humans transformed by variants of the Forced Evolutionary Virus. topic_desc: Nightkin were created by the Master as elite super-mutant stealth troops. Their purple coloration reflects additional experimentation, while their name comes from near-constant use of Stealth Boys to cloak themselves. They guarded important Unity sites and served as commanders, scouts, hunters, and abductors. After the Master's fall, surviving Nightkin scattered across the wasteland. Some later followed leaders such as Marcus, Tabitha, or Davison. Long-term Stealth Boy exposure causes serious mental illness among many Nightkin, including hallucinations, paranoia, schizophrenia, and divided personalities. These conditions shape their speech and behavior but do not make every Nightkin identical or incapable of reason. In the Mojave, groups occupy places such as Black Mountain and REPCONN, while isolated individuals wander elsewhere. Their combination of great physical strength, military experience, cloaking technology, and psychological distress makes peaceful contact difficult and dangerous without understanding their condition.

topic_desc: Ghouls are humans transformed by radiation. Their skin may dry and fall away over months, their aging slows, and further radiation generally stops harming them. These changes do not remove their humanity. Non-feral ghouls can reason, remember, feel pain and regret, build communities, practice professions, and form relationships like other people. In the Capital Wasteland, Underworld became a major ghoul settlement partly because discrimination made ordinary human communities unsafe. Medical workers there treat illness and study whether ghoulification can be stopped or reversed. Fear that every ghoul will suddenly become feral is widespread but unsupported; the cause and timing of feral decline are uncertain. Some humans repeat claims that ghouls carry disease without evidence, using those assumptions to justify exclusion or violence. Understanding the difference between physical mutation and feral behavior is therefore essential when dealing with ghoul communities.
topic_desc_basic: Ghouls are radiation-mutated humans whose appearance and lifespan have changed dramatically. Many form their own communities because ordinary humans exclude or attack them out of fear and misinformation.
